chapters.title: Chapter 601: Try Not to Kill Each Other
paragraphs: Seris showed more interest this time.
"The Land of First Dawn?"
"Yeah, it’s a special land where three people from our academy are going to be sent."
"You and who else?"
"Rindo, whom you also met in the Special Area, and another person you don’t know."
The third person was naturally Roderick, but the girl knew nothing about that boy.
Seris looked toward the mountain peak.
"When are you leaving?"
"Probably soon, I need to return first, check my equipment, and make the final arrangements."
Then it was his turn to ask a question.
"What about you? Are you going straight to that Hidden Area?"
She nodded.
"I’m going to the Pendragon base, but before that, I want to look around this area, if possible, I want to find the fallen city of Frost."
"Then let me know if you find anything interesting at the base."
"Okay."
Lian smiled.
"Especially if you find any treasures that would be suitable for me."
Seris looked at him for a moment.
"Come and take them yourself."
"That’s not a bad idea."
He laughed and didn’t reject her offer, perhaps visiting that base in the future wasn’t such a bad idea.

They stood in silence for a short while, not the kind of heavy and uncomfortable silence, but the normal silence between two people who had traveled together for a long time and now had separate plans.
Lian finally spoke.
"Then, goodbye for now."
Seris nodded.
"See you."
"Yeah. Take care of yourself."
"You too."
The girl looked at him for another moment, then turned toward her own route back.
Lian also activated the option to return to Earth, blue light formed around his body, and a few seconds later, he disappeared from the mountains.
Seris continued on her own path without stopping.
Sooner or later, they would see each other again, but for now, both of them had more important things to do.
When Lian opened his eyes again, instead of the cold mountain wind, a gentle breeze touched his face.

He was also back in the city of Verendal, and since he had nothing else to do in this city, he went straight to the city’s transportation center and, after paying the fee, entered a portal with the capital of his country as its destination.
It didn’t take long for him to find himself in the capital’s transportation center, and as before, he took a taxi and returned to the academy.
The academy’s familiar tall buildings stood before him.
The grounds were unusually quiet, and only a few students could be seen in the distance, while the sounds of training came from only a small number of buildings.
Most students and Awakened were currently in the Ruined Realm to hunt, increase their levels, and complete missions.
The academy was still active, but a large number of its students were spending most of their time in the other world and only returned for necessary training, rest, or administrative matters.
Lian put his hands into his pockets and walked toward the central building, along the way, several students recognized him.
As he passed by, one of them fixed his gaze on the back of Lian’s right hand, while another whispered something to his companion.
He didn’t even need to listen to guess what they were talking about.
The news from Verendal had also reached the academy, the Ancestral Dragon Mark, the support of Rhaenar Pendragon, and the unexpected invitation from Kairos to join the Primal Firmament.
Of course, these reports were only part of the truth, if the full truth became public, God knew what the reactions would be like.
When he reached the central notice board, his eyes stopped on one of the announcements.
Selected Students to Be Sent to the Land of First Dawn
Under the title, the names of three students were listed.
Lian.
Rindo.
Roderick.
Only three people from the academy had been selected for this stage.
The journey would begin at Base #3, and after arriving there, the group would have to travel by land for about a week to reach the main destination.
Lian looked at the names for a few seconds, then gave a faint smile.
Finally, it’s time.
But before anything else, there was someone he should visit, so he moved away from the board and headed toward the Student Council building.
The hallway of the Student Council building was almost empty.

In the past, several students would usually wait in front of the council office, some had come to submit their requests, while others wanted to talk about problems with their classes or training schedules.
But now, only two people could be seen at the end of the hallway.
Lian walked straight toward the council president’s office and knocked on the door a few times.
"Come in."
A familiar voice came from behind the door.
He entered.
Rindo was sitting behind a large desk, with several files in front of him, and he was reviewing a report that was probably related to the upcoming expedition.
When the door opened, he raised his head, and for a moment, his gaze settled on the young Vorhelm.
Then he closed the file.
"So, you finally showed up."
"I missed seeing you."
Lian smiled.
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds.
"Then you could have come back sooner."
Lian laughed and sat on the chair across from the desk without waiting for an invitation.
"Are you always this strict?"
"Only when someone who should be preparing for an important expedition is nowhere to be found until the last moment."
As Rindo spoke, he took a closer look at him.
Lian noticed that his friend was paying more attention to his physical condition than to his clothes or Ancestral Dragon Mark.
After a few seconds, the Student Council President asked,
"You’re not seriously injured, are you?"
"No, I’m fine for now."
Rindo briefly glanced at his right hand.
"Considering the news I heard from Verendal, that answer isn’t very reassuring."
"Don’t worry, if there were something wrong with me, I probably wouldn’t be sitting here right now."
Rindo remained silent for a moment, then spoke.
"That was exactly the kind of answer I expected to hear from you."
Lian laughed, but behind this short conversation, both of them were aware of something that didn’t need to be said directly.
They had already experienced situations where their survival was uncertain until the very last moment.
When two people face death together, they no longer need to constantly use warm words to prove their friendship.
Rindo was still the same organized and strict person as before.
But Lian knew that if he ever truly needed help, Rindo would be one of the people he could count on.
"So, how are the preparations for the expedition going?" the young Vorhelm asked, glancing at the files on the desk.
The Student Council President picked up one of them.
"Almost everything is ready. The transfer to Base #3 has been arranged, and after that, we’ll have to travel by land with the main group."
"One week, right?"
"About that, though it depends on the condition of the route."
Rindo opened the file.
"For now, the plan is to travel without any unnecessary stops. But if the security situation changes, the route or departure time might change as well."
Lian nodded.
"Then we still have time."
"Time to prepare, yes, not to waste."
His smile changed slightly.
"Right, I’d prefer not to struggle to stay alive as much this time."
Rindo gave a small nod.
"Same here."
Then he looked at the files.
"Only three people from our academy are being sent, me, you, and Roderick. So I expect all three of us to cooperate, at least when it comes to matters related to the journey."
"Has Roderick still not returned?"
"According to the latest report I received, no, but he’s expected to return soon."
"Then at least one of the three of us hasn’t finished his journey yet."
Rindo looked at him.
"I hope you two won’t start your old problems again when he returns."
The young Vorhelm shrugged.
"I don’t have a problem with him."
He looked at him for a few seconds, then placed the file on the desk.
"Lian, I know enough about what happened between you two."
"Then you know that most of the problems weren’t started by me."

"I know, but I want you to show some restraint during this trip, at least until he does something stupid, turn a blind eye to his actions, I’d prefer it if our journey didn’t turn into a personal fight before we even reached our destination."
Lian rested his hand on the armrest of the chair.
"As long as Roderick doesn’t go looking for trouble, I won’t bother him either."
Rindo didn’t continue the subject, apparently, that answer was enough for him for now.
As the young Vorhelm looked around the office, he noticed several different files on the other side of the desk.
They had the Student Council’s seal on them, but unlike the expedition files, their titles were about transferring the council’s responsibilities.
He looked at Rindo.
"I guess you’ve already started handling your graduation matters, right?"
Rindo nodded.
"Yes, I’m finishing the rest of my work, and then I’ll have to hand over the position of Student Council President, I need to do that before our expedition, at least."
"What are your plans after that?"
"I want to join the Federation."
"The Federation?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"I’ll probably start in one of its operational or management departments, they haven’t made a final decision about my initial position yet."
The young Vorhelm looked at him for a few seconds, this choice suited Rindo’s personality perfectly.

chapters.title: Chapter 602: The Race for the Council
paragraphs: Rindo was not the kind of person who took on important responsibilities just to gain fame or improve his social position.
He genuinely had the ability to manage things.
Even in dangerous situations, he usually kept his calm and tried to make decisions that did not only benefit one person or a specific group.
Of course, this did not mean he was perfect, sometimes he became too strict and expected others to act with the same level of discipline as him.
But these qualities would probably be useful for someone who wanted to join the Federation’s structure.
Lian gave a faint smile.
Could it be that he planned to become the leader of the Federation one day?
For a moment, the thought seemed amusing, but when he thought about it more carefully, he realized that it was not entirely impossible.

Rindo was young, talented, and had good management skills, and more importantly, unlike many influential people, the respect he showed others was not determined only by their family names or social positions.
Actually, it might not be a bad thing, having a friend at the head of the Federation could be very valuable in the future.
Of course, the distance between joining the Federation and becoming its leader would probably be very long.
But Lian himself had achieved things in a short period that had once seemed difficult even to imagine.
So who could speak with certainty about Rindo’s future?
"What’s so funny?"
Rindo’s voice pulled Lian out of his thoughts.
He smiled.
"No. I was just thinking that maybe one day, I’ll have to make an appointment with a few ministers just to see you."
He looked at him for a few seconds, then replied in the same calm tone.
"If that day comes, I hope you’ll at least let me know before you come."
"So I can’t count on our friendship?"
"I’ll probably make an exception for you."
"What an honor."
This time, the corner of Rindo’s mouth also rose slightly, but he soon returned to his usual expression.
Lian pointed at the files about transferring responsibilities.
"So, what about the next Student Council President?"
"We haven’t made a final decision yet, do you still not want the position?"
"No."
His answer came so quickly that the Student Council President remained silent for a moment.
"You don’t even need to think about it more?"
"I’ve already thought about it, and my answer is still the same."
Lian shrugged.
Rindo let out a short sigh.
"I thought you might have changed your mind after everything that happened recently."

"Why would I change my mind? I already have enough work to do, if I had to make decisions about student conflicts and problems with training schedules every day, I’d probably have no time left to train."
"Being the Student Council President isn’t just about dealing with student conflicts."
Rindo replied.
"I know, that’s why I’m even more certain that I don’t want it."
The young Vorhelm nodded.
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds, then shook his head.
"Then we’ll probably move forward with Seraphina."
"Are you leaving Cassian out?"
"Not necessarily, it depends on the situation."
He paused for a moment and looked at one of the files before answering.
"The situation?"
"Choosing a successor isn’t only about management skills, whoever becomes the Student Council President must also be able to gain the students’ support.
Rindo placed his fingers on the desk.
"Seraphina has good abilities, and Cassian can still be a suitable candidate, but the main issue is how the election goes."
"You mean Roderick?"
Lian tilted his head slightly, this was a topic they had discussed before, and the result had always been the same.
Roderick was a very strong candidate, the strongest candidate for Student Council President.
He nodded.
"No matter how much Roderick’s reputation was damaged after the final exam, he’s still the most popular student in the academy."
Lian thought about this for a moment, the situation was not particularly strange.
Roderick held an important position among the students and had built a wide network of connections and supporters.
Losing an exam, even if it had dealt a heavy blow to his pride, could not erase all his social influence.
Rindo continued.
"Many people still consider him the best choice for leadership, even if he doesn’t run in the election himself, supporting another candidate can change the result."
Then he looked at Lian.
"Of course, you’ve also become a bigger taboo among the students."
"A taboo?"
The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
The Student Council President studied him for a few seconds.
"Roderick is popular, he has supporters, and at the same time, everyone fears him, but things are different when it comes to you."
"Some people admire you, some are afraid of you, and the rest, well, both."
"After Verendal, you’re no longer just a talented student, your name has been mentioned alongside two Celestials. On top of that, you’ve also received one of the Pendragons’ most important legacies."
"So I’m an unpopular taboo?"
Lian gave a faint smile.
"No."
Rindo answered without hesitation.
"You’ve become someone many people would prefer to be on good terms with, but they don’t know how to approach you, there’s an important difference between admiration, fear, and popularity."
Lian thought about this for a few moments.
"Roderick can enter a group, and many people will willingly gather around him, but when you enter the same group, people might not even dare to speak to you comfortably."
"Wow, I didn’t think I’d become this scary."

"Maybe you don’t see yourself that way, but your reputation is different, you also need to consider that Roderick ruled by isolating and suppressing people, yet the students fear you more, because they don’t know how they should act around you."
"What a hassle."
The corner of Lian’s mouth rose slightly.
"That’s why defeating Roderick in the election won’t be easy."
Rindo became more serious this time.
After a short pause, he continued.

"Under normal circumstances, I wouldn’t have a problem with Roderick becoming the next Student Council President, but I don’t want him to create the same lord-and-servant system inside the academy again."
Lian’s smile slowly disappeared, he knew very well what Rindo was talking about.

For a long time, Roderick had used his position and influence to create a system where some students received special privileges because they were close to him, while others had to follow their wishes to avoid trouble.
Rindo did not agree with such a system, and his opposition was not only related to his personal disagreement with Roderick.
"The Student Council isn’t supposed to be a noble’s court, whoever becomes its president should work for the benefit of the students, not make the students work for his benefit."
Lian nodded.
"So that’s why you prefer Seraphina.

"That’s one of the reasons, but it’s still too early to make a final decision, even so, I think she’s the only person who can compete with Roderick in popularity, if you support her too, her victory might even become certain."
"Of course I’ll support her, although it seems you have no intention of giving yourself a break, even in your final days here."
Lian gave a small smile.
Rindo replied.
"As long as I have responsibilities, I see no reason to leave my work unfinished."
Whatever the case, the decisions had more or less been made, Seraphina would become the next Student Council President, at least they had to make sure of that.
Unfortunately, the Student Council President had considerable power over the students in the Ruined Realm, most students depended on the academy for resources, teams, and the chance to form groups.

Not everyone was like Lian or his friends, geniuses who could make progress however they wanted, the others needed support, and the academy was the one that supported them, at least until they joined a guild.
And the Student Council President had enough power to influence this system and its structure.

During the nine months they had been away, Roderick had taken advantage of the Student Council President’s absence and built a powerful network that could influence this very system of academy support for students.
Rindo could not allow that man to become the Student Council President and bring back his system.
They talked a little longer, the young Vorhelm asked about their other friends, and it turned out that all of them were in the Ruined Realm.
Everyone wanted to increase their levels as quickly as possible so they could catch up with others their age and even surpass them.
Selina and Liana were still together, making progress as a group and exploring new areas around Base #3.

Cassian, Ethan, and Marcus had also become much closer after the events in the Special Area and had practically formed a group, according to the latest news about them, they had managed to find a dungeon.
Their group had even managed to enter the top five in the group hunting rankings, one of the five rankings at Base #3.
As for Seraphina, even Rindo had no exact information about her, except that she was safe, but it was unclear where she was or where she had gone.

This made Lian frown slightly, he hoped that the girl had not gotten herself into trouble, but hearing that the information center at Base #3 had recorded her status as alive and safe stopped him from worrying too much about it.
The girl had a dual class and carried the legacy of a destroyed civilization, it was unlikely that she would die so easily.

Rindo himself had also spent most of the past two months with Cassian, Ethan, and Marcus, and during that time, they had managed to find and explore an ancient ruin that belonged to a destroyed empire.
It was only a few days ago that he had been forced to leave those three because of the expedition to the Land of First Dawn.
In short, everyone had been busy with their own lives during this time.
A while later, Lian left the council office, and on his way back to his residence, he looked at the quiet academy grounds once more.
Everything seemed peaceful.
But his conversation with Rindo had reminded him that even in the absence of most students, internal rivalries were still going on.
The Student Council succession, Roderick’s influence, and the change in his own position among the students, none of these things were his current priority, however.
He would be sent to the Land of First Dawn in a few days, and before that, he had more important things to do.
He went straight to his dormitory.
"I’m finally back."
He let out a quiet breath.
He decided to check his equipment supplies before doing anything else.
His World-Devourer Bastion armor was still with him. Its structure had gradually recovered after the heavy battles of the past,
The treasures were also still in their places, but when he reached the section containing his potions, his eyebrows drew together slightly.
Only a small number of his best healing potions remained, and his supply of mana recovery potions was no longer in very good shape either.
The antidotes and emergency medical supplies had also been used during his previous missions.
At the moment, he might not need healing potions as much as he had in the past.
The Indestructible Body had greatly increased his resistance and natural recovery ability.
On the other hand, he now had access to many defensive structures and abilities that he had never even imagined before.
But that did not mean he was completely immune to harm, the Indestructible Body was still only twenty percent complete.
And Lian knew better than anyone that some enemies could inflict dangerous injuries without being affected by his body’s normal defenses.
Besides, he no longer only had himself to think about, One, Two, and Three,
the Special Colony Members who might need healing resources in future battles.
Especially Three, who had still not recovered from a large part of the injuries it had suffered in their recent battle.

"Why would I change my mind?
I already have enough work to do, if I had to make decisions about student conflicts and problems with training schedules every day, I’d probably have no time left to train."
"Being the Student Council President isn’t just about dealing with student conflicts."
Rindo replied.
"I know, that’s why I’m even more certain that I don’t want it."
The young Vorhelm nodded.
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds, then shook his head.
"Then we’ll probably move forward with Seraphina."
"Are you leaving Cassian out?"
"Not necessarily, it depends on the situation."
He paused for a moment and looked at one of the files before answering.
"The situation?"
"Choosing a successor isn’t only about management skills, whoever becomes the Student Council President must also be able to gain the students’ support.
Rindo placed his fingers on the desk.
"Seraphina has good abilities, and Cassian can still be a suitable candidate, but the main issue is how the election goes."
"You mean Roderick?"
Lian tilted his head slightly, this was a topic they had discussed before, and the result had always been the same.
Roderick was a very strong candidate, the strongest candidate for Student Council President.
He nodded.
"No matter how much Roderick’s reputation was damaged after the final exam, he’s still the most popular student in the academy."
Lian thought about this for a moment, the situation was not particularly strange.
Roderick held an important position among the students and had built a wide network of connections and supporters.
Losing an exam, even if it had dealt a heavy blow to his pride, could not erase all his social influence.
Rindo continued.
"Many people still consider him the best choice for leadership, even if he doesn’t run in the election himself, supporting another candidate can change the result."
Then he looked at Lian.
"Of course, you’ve also become a bigger taboo among the students."
"A taboo?"
The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
The Student Council President studied him for a few seconds.
"Roderick is popular, he has supporters, and at the same time, everyone fears him, but things are different when it comes to you."
"Some people admire you, some are afraid of you, and the rest, well, both."
"After Verendal, you’re no longer just a talented student, your name has been mentioned alongside two Celestials.
On top of that, you’ve also received one of the Pendragons’ most important legacies."
"So I’m an unpopular taboo?"
Lian gave a faint smile.
"No."
Rindo answered without hesitation.
"You’ve become someone many people would prefer to be on good terms with, but they don’t know how to approach you, there’s an important difference between admiration, fear, and popularity."
Lian thought about this for a few moments.
"Roderick can enter a group, and many people will willingly gather around him, but when you enter the same group, people might not even dare to speak to you comfortably."
"Wow, I didn’t think I’d become this scary."

"Maybe you don’t see yourself that way, but your reputation is different, you also need to consider that Roderick ruled by isolating and suppressing people, yet the students fear you more, because they don’t know how they should act around you."
"What a hassle."
The corner of Lian’s mouth rose slightly.
"That’s why defeating Roderick in the election won’t be easy."
Rindo became more serious this time.
After a short pause, he continued.

"Under normal circumstances, I wouldn’t have a problem with Roderick becoming the next Student Council President, but I don’t want him to create the same lord-and-servant system inside the academy again."
Lian’s smile slowly disappeared, he knew very well what Rindo was talking about.

For a long time, Roderick had used his position and influence to create a system where some students received special privileges because they were close to him, while others had to follow their wishes to avoid trouble.
Rindo did not agree with such a system, and his opposition was not only related to his personal disagreement with Roderick.
"The Student Council isn’t supposed to be a noble’s court, whoever becomes its president should work for the benefit of the students, not make the students work for his benefit."
Lian nodded.
"So that’s why you prefer Seraphina.

"That’s one of the reasons, but it’s still too early to make a final decision, even so, I think she’s the only person who can compete with Roderick in popularity, if you support her too, her victory might even become certain."
"Of course I’ll support her, although it seems you have no intention of giving yourself a break, even in your final days here."
Lian gave a small smile.
Rindo replied.
"As long as I have responsibilities, I see no reason to leave my work unfinished."
Whatever the case, the decisions had more or less been made, Seraphina would become the next Student Council President, at least they had to make sure of that.
Unfortunately, the Student Council President had considerable power over the students in the Ruined Realm, most students depended on the academy for resources, teams, and the chance to form groups.

Not everyone was like Lian or his friends, geniuses who could make progress however they wanted, the others needed support, and the academy was the one that supported them, at least until they joined a guild.
And the Student Council President had enough power to influence this system and its structure.

During the nine months they had been away, Roderick had taken advantage of the Student Council President’s absence and built a powerful network that could influence this very system of academy support for students.
Rindo could not allow that man to become the Student Council President and bring back his system.
They talked a little longer, the young Vorhelm asked about their other friends, and it turned out that all of them were in the Ruined Realm.
Everyone wanted to increase their levels as quickly as possible so they could catch up with others their age and even surpass them.
Selina and Liana were still together, making progress as a group and exploring new areas around Base #3.

Cassian, Ethan, and Marcus had also become much closer after the events in the Special Area and had practically formed a group, according to the latest news about them, they had managed to find a dungeon.
Their group had even managed to enter the top five in the group hunting rankings, one of the five rankings at Base #3.
As for Seraphina, even Rindo had no exact information about her, except that she was safe, but it was unclear where she was or where she had gone.

This made Lian frown slightly, he hoped that the girl had not gotten herself into trouble, but hearing that the information center at Base #3 had recorded her status as alive and safe stopped him from worrying too much about it.
The girl had a dual class and carried the legacy of a destroyed civilization, it was unlikely that she would die so easily.

Rindo himself had also spent most of the past two months with Cassian, Ethan, and Marcus, and during that time, they had managed to find and explore an ancient ruin that belonged to a destroyed empire.
It was only a few days ago that he had been forced to leave those three because of the expedition to the Land of First Dawn.
In short, everyone had been busy with their own lives during this time.
A while later, Lian left the council office, and on his way back to his residence, he looked at the quiet academy grounds once more.
Everything seemed peaceful.
But his conversation with Rindo had reminded him that even in the absence of most students, internal rivalries were still going on.
The Student Council succession, Roderick’s influence, and the change in his own position among the students, none of these things were his current priority, however.
He would be sent to the Land of First Dawn in a few days, and before that, he had more important things to do.
He went straight to his dormitory.
"I’m finally back."
He let out a quiet breath.
He decided to check his equipment supplies before doing anything else.
His World-Devourer Bastion armor was still with him.
Its structure had gradually recovered after the heavy battles of the past,
The treasures were also still in their places, but when he reached the section containing his potions, his eyebrows drew together slightly.
Only a small number of his best healing potions remained, and his supply of mana recovery potions was no longer in very good shape either.
The antidotes and emergency medical supplies had also been used during his previous missions.
At the moment, he might not need healing potions as much as he had in the past.
The Indestructible Body had greatly increased his resistance and natural recovery ability.
On the other hand, he now had access to many defensive structures and abilities that he had never even imagined before.
But that did not mean he was completely immune to harm, the Indestructible Body was still only twenty percent complete.
And Lian knew better than anyone that some enemies could inflict dangerous injuries without being affected by his body’s normal defenses.
Besides, he no longer only had himself to think about, One, Two, and Three,
the Special Colony Members who might need healing resources in future battles.
Especially Three, who had still not recovered from a large part of the injuries it had suffered in their recent battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 603: Business Is Business
paragraphs: "I think it’s time to do some shopping."
He preferred to buy resources and never have to use them rather than discover in a deadly situation that his supplies had run out.
However, the academy’s ordinary shop was not the best choice for this kind of purchase, he knew someone else who could probably provide more suitable items.
Miranda.
Lian took out the special customer card he had received during their previous meeting.
Before he entered the Special Area, that woman had also provided him with useful resources and equipment.
Besides, Miranda was not just an ordinary seller.
She was one of the lords of the Black Market Towers, a woman with wide connections and access to rare goods.
Building connections with someone like her was not just a good idea, it could also be very useful in the future, and besides, that woman was an Overlord as well.
Having a good relationship with an Overlord was another advantage.
Lian activated the contact information on the card and sent a short message.
"Hello, Lady Miranda, I need some potions and equipment."
A few minutes later, a reply arrived, much sooner than he had expected.
"Look who finally showed up, Vorhelm."
He smiled.
"Did you miss me?"
"I missed our deals more."
"I thought so too." Lian let out a short laugh.
Miranda’s next reply was a little longer, she asked him to send an approximate shopping list so she could check the available stock.
The young Vorhelm wrote down a few main items and sent the list, and some time later, he received an address for their meeting.
But when he read it, he fell silent for a moment.
The main shop of the Awakened Association.
Lian checked the message again and then asked,
"Are you sure you didn’t send me the wrong address?"
"No."
"Weren’t we supposed to meet at the Black Market Tower?"
"This time, come to the Association shop, I’ll be waiting for you."
He stared at the screen for a few seconds.
Strange.
As far as he knew, Miranda worked in the Black Market, so why was she inviting him to one of the Awakened Association’s official locations?
Lian put the card away and stood up.
"Well, I guess I’ll find out soon enough."
The Awakened Association shop was very different from the Black Market Tower.

The main hall was filled with bright, even lighting, protected display cases stood along the walls, and different kinds of potions, defensive equipment, and cultivation materials were kept behind special glass.
The staff wore matching formal uniforms, and most customers provided their permits or account information before making a purchase.
Even the way the goods were displayed was much more organized than in the Black Market.
Lian looked around for a moment, the last time he had come here, he had received a bronze card, but he doubted he would need that card at the moment.
Then he approached one of the staff members.
"I have an appointment with Miss Miranda."
After hearing her name, the young woman checked the meeting information, and once the appointment was confirmed, her attitude became more formal.
"Mr. Lian Vorhelm?"
"That’s me."
"Miss Miranda is waiting for you, please follow me."
Lian raised an eyebrow, it seemed he really did have an important appointment.
The employee led him through the public area of the shop and took him to a quieter floor, at the end of the hallway stood a large door bearing the emblem of the Awakened Association.
After she announced his arrival, the door opened and he entered the office.
Miranda was sitting behind a large desk.
She wore dark formal clothes, and her hair was neatly arranged. Several sales reports lay on the desk, and a small case sat beside her.
When Lian entered, the woman raised her head and gave him a familiar smile that was cold, serious, and professional at the same time.
"Welcome."
The young Vorhelm looked at her for a few seconds, then at the office, and then back at her.
"I have a question."
The woman raised an eyebrow.
"Ask."
"Did you change jobs?"
Miranda fell silent for a moment, then laughed.
"No. I’m also the head of the Awakened Association’s shop department."
Lian raised his eyebrows.
"Also?"
"Yes. I manage this department, and at the same time, one of the Black Market Towers is also under my management."
He said nothing for a few seconds, then let out a quiet whistle.
"Wow, business genius at its finest." It was certainly a big surprise to him, he had never expected this woman to manage both.
Did the Awakened Association know that this woman was basically the owner of part of the world’s largest illegal market, yet chose to ignore it?
Or did it not know and simply ignore it? Of course, he doubted that the world’s largest organization would be unaware of such a fact.
Besides, this woman was so powerful that the Awakened Association could not do much to her anyway, so it was better to keep her under its watch.
She smiled.
"That’s enough."
Lian sat down on the chair across from her.

"No, I’m seriously impressed, you have a position in the official market and in the Black Market, so if someone can’t buy something through one channel, they’ll probably end up coming to you through the other."
Miranda placed her fingers on the desk.
"I prefer to say that I provide suitable services for every kind of customer."
"What’s the difference?"
"Mine sounds more legal."
"Right, you’re really a genius."
Miranda shook her head slightly.
"If you’re done praising me, we can talk about your purchase."
Miranda moved one of the files on her desk aside.
"I saw your list, advanced healing potions, mana recovery potions, antidotes, and several kinds of emergency equipment, do you have a long journey ahead of you?"
The young Vorhelm nodded.
"I’m going back to the Ruined Realm."
"I guessed that, do you have a specific destination?"
"The Land of First Dawn."
Her expression became more serious for a moment.
"So your departure is getting close."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"You know about it too?"
"Of course, when you do business with Awakened, it’s better to know when and where they’re being sent."
The woman gave a slight smile.
"Especially when one of your customers is among those who were selected."
Lian nodded, she glanced at his shopping list and then asked,
"By the way, it seems you haven’t brought anything to sell lately."
Lian looked at her for a moment.
"Why?"
"Before, whenever you returned, you always had a few interesting materials or treasures with you, even monster corpses, but I haven’t received any offers from you lately."
"Personal use." He thought for a moment and answered simply.
Miranda looked at him for a few seconds.
"All of them?"
"Almost."
The woman let out a short sigh.
"What a shame, I was hoping you had brought something interesting for me this time too."
"Maybe next time."
She did not try to ask any more questions about Lian’s treasures, she was experienced enough to know that unnecessary curiosity could damage her relationship with a valuable customer.
Instead, she turned her attention back to his current purchases.

"Well, there is no problem with the healing potions, we have several types suitable for serious injuries, and for mana recovery, I can offer you higher-quality options than the ones you bought last time."
Lian nodded.
"Good, I’d prefer to have more of them."
"Judging by the items you’re buying, I guess you don’t plan to use them only for yourself."
"Maybe." The young Vorhelm smiled, he was buying supplies for both himself and his colony.
Miranda glanced at him but did not continue, instead, she opened one of the sales reports.
"By the way, I heard you’ve recently attracted the attention of two Celestials."
"News really does travel fast." He sighed.
"Especially when it concerns my valuable customers." She nodded.
Miranda’s gaze rested on Lian’s Ancestral Mark for a moment.
"You’ve also received the Pendragon Mark, that was truly unexpected."
"It was unexpected for me too." Lian shrugged.
The woman smiled, who would have thought that the boy who had brought her the first fallen corpse from the tenth Ruined Realm a year ago would reach such a position today?
She had been lucky that day to establish a good connection with him directly, and she felt that this relationship would become even more beneficial to her in the future.
For someone like her, everything was about business and money, wherever there was money, she would be there too.
"Then I hope we’ll have more interesting deals in the future."
"It seems you’re making more plans for my future than I am." Lian replied calmly.
Miranda laughed.
"A good businesswoman always has plans for her valuable customers."
After checking the list, she paused for a moment at the section for mana recovery potions.
"You want a lot of mana potions."
"Some of my skills consume a lot of mana."
The woman thought for a few seconds, then a different smile appeared on her face, the same smile Lian remembered from their previous meetings.
A smile that usually meant a business offer was coming.
"Then perhaps I have something even better for you."
"What?"
Miranda stood up and walked toward a protected case beside the wall, after checking her own access mark, the case opened.
She took out a small, dark-colored box and placed it on the desk.
When the box opened, he saw a delicate metal seal with very thin lines of blue light moving across its surface.
Miranda pushed the box slightly toward him.
"Mana Reservoir Seal."
Lian picked it up, the seal’s structure was different from most of the treasures he had seen before.
Several small mana rings were built into it, and it seemed to be designed to store energy in a compact space.
"What does it do?"
"You can store some of your own mana inside it while resting, then during a fight, the seal gradually returns that energy to your body."
Lian looked at it for a moment.
"So it’s an extra mana reservoir?"
"More or less, but not in a way that lets you use all the energy inside it at once."
Miranda explained that the seal had a limited transfer speed and had to be filled again with its owner’s mana after it was emptied.
"It’s useful for fighters whose skills consume a lot of mana, especially if they don’t have time to recover their mana naturally between two powerful attacks."
Lian kept his eyes on the seal, and he immediately thought of Wings of God.
Some of its uses, especially long flights or powerful attacks, consumed a large amount of his mana.
The seal could not make up for the huge cost of an attack at that very moment.
But if it gradually returned some of the mana he had spent after he used a skill, it could allow him to stay in a fight for longer.

chapters.title: Chapter 604: There Goes My Money Again ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: He put the seal back inside the box.
"How much does it cost?"
Miranda showed her usual business smile.
"For an ordinary customer? Very expensive."
"And for me?" Lian tilted his head slightly.
"A little less than very expensive."
"I guess that’s how you became one of the most successful merchants in the world."
"Exactly, that’s the reason I’m still successful in business." Miranda shrugged slightly.
Lian looked at the box for a few seconds and then said,
"If I’m going to spend this much, at least give me a better discount on the potions."
She was silent for a moment, then her smile grew a little wider.
"Now you’re finally learning how to negotiate properly."
Their bargaining did not take long.
Miranda knew very well how much of a discount was reasonable to keep an important customer, and Lian had no intention of wasting too much time over a difference of a few units in price.

It should not be forgotten that he had around 200 million dollars in his account, more or less, and unfortunately, since he did not live a luxurious life either, the money had remained untouched the entire time.
In the end, the purchase was completed.
Advanced healing potions, mana recovery potions, multipurpose antidotes, emergency medical equipment, and several consumable resources suitable for healing his colony members.
And of course, the Mana Reservoir Seal.
After receiving the items, he examined the seal for a moment and then stored it with the rest of his equipment.
Miranda was confirming the final purchase report at the same time.
"By the way, Lian."
"Yes?"
"When you travel to the Land of First Dawn, you’d better be more careful than ever."
Lian became a little more serious, this was exactly the same warning Professor Aldric had given him.
Despite everyone describing it as a land that was like paradise, that man believed something was wrong with that place and that they needed to be careful.
"Have you heard anything?"
Miranda looked at him for a moment.
"I don’t have any specific information I can sell you, but all I can say is that you should be careful, the origin of that place is unknown, and anything unknown is dangerous."
He thought for a few seconds and then nodded.
"I understand."
"Good, I don’t want to lose one of my customers."
Lian stood up.
"Until next time."
"Goodbye for now."
He left the office, but as he exited the building, he looked back at the official shop of the Awakened Association once more.
A woman who managed one of the Black Market Towers while also holding a managerial position in the Association’s official shop.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
She really has an unusual talent for business.
He became even more curious about her story, wondering how one person could achieve something like this when it should not even be legally possible.
When he returned to his dormitory, most of his preparations were complete, and his potions had been restocked.
He had emergency equipment, and the Mana Reservoir Seal could also be useful in long battles.
However, one thing remained, he sat down on the chair behind his desk.
Then he opened the system window, and his gaze remained on his Fragment balance for a moment.
[Fragments: 561]
This was the reward from his recent achievements, he could save the Fragments for the future, but he had wanted to combine several overlapping skills for a long time.
Especially now that his fighting style had become clearer than before.
Lian relied more on his fists, physical strength, and close-range skills.
The Indestructible Body had also greatly improved his abilities in this kind of combat.
However, there were still two areas he could improve.
Understanding enemy movements better and having a direct, focused strike that could break through defenses.
He checked his skill list.
Then he selected the first three skills.
[Predator’s Instincts]
[Night Eyes]
[Echo Adaptation]
All three were useful in different parts of combat.
Predator’s Instincts helped him detect dangers and enemy movements earlier, it even helped him see the flow of blood, while Night Eyes improved his vision in dark conditions.
Echo Adaptation was useful for recognizing and adapting to repeating patterns.
But if he could combine all these effects into a single skill, the result would probably be much more effective.
He activated the combination option.
[Three skills have been selected for combination]
[Predator’s Instincts + Night Eyes + Echo Adaptation]
[Possible Result: Primordial Predator’s Perception]
[Combination Cost: 260 Fragments]
[Proceed with the combination?]
Lian selected the confirmation option without hesitation, a few moments later, a faint blue light appeared before his eyes.
He felt some of the information from the three skills being rearranged in his mind, rather than his senses suddenly becoming stronger in an uncontrollable way.
Instead, he felt that the information he received from his surroundings was now being processed through more coordinated paths.
The faint sound of the curtain moving beside the window, the change in the airflow, and even the movement patterns of the tree branch’s shadow on the ground... everything seemed clearer.
But more important than the clarity of his senses was the connection between them.
For a moment, he followed the movement of a small leaf behind the window, as the wind changed direction, the leaf began to spin.
From its initial movement, he was able to predict the likely path of its continued rotation more quickly.
Of course, this was only a simple test.
In a real battle, enemies could act against their previous patterns or use skills that left no usual signs.
But this increase in his analysis speed was valuable to Lian.
A new window appeared.
[Skill combination successful]
[New Skill: Primordial Predator’s Perception]
[Rank: Divine]
[260 Fragments consumed]
[Remaining Fragments: 301]
"Not bad."
He could imagine how useful this skill would be alongside [True Sequence].
One was for examining the structure and sequence of energy, while the other was for analyzing physical signs and movement patterns and reacting more quickly.
Of course, neither of them meant that he could see the future.
But he did not need that either, if he could gather more information about his enemies and use it more quickly, that was enough.
After a while, he turned his attention to the second combination.
This time, he selected three different skills.
[Suppressing Palm]
[Iron Fortress Charge]
[Cataclysm Pulse]
Lian looked at them for a few seconds, all three were related to direct strikes and physical force in terms of their nature.
However, each of them covered a different part of combat.
Iron Fortress Charge strengthened the force of movement and impact.
Suppressing Palm could be both a massive attack and a precise, focused strike.
And Cataclysm Pulse could turn the force of impact into a destructive wave.
If these three skills were combined into a single attack, they could concentrate a large part of his current physical power at one specific point.
And that was exactly what he wanted.
He selected the combination option.
[Three skills have been selected for combination]
[Suppressing Palm + Iron Fortress Charge + Cataclysm Pulse]
[Possible Result: Disaster Suppression Fist]
[Combination Cost: 280 Fragments]
[Proceed with the combination?]
"Confirm."
A short flow of mana moved through his right arm, and Lian curled his fingers for a moment.
He felt that the new skill’s structure had been designed to coordinate the force of his body’s movement, the suppressing pressure, and the destructive impact wave at the same moment.
However, unlike an ordinary punch, using it properly required the right timing and angle.
If the enemy moved out of the way before the impact, a large part of the gathered force would be wasted, and its mana cost was also higher than that of a simple strike.
Even so, against a target that could not easily escape or had no proper defense? The result could be devastating.
He decided not to test the skill in his room for now.
The last thing he wanted was to have to explain the broken wall of his dormitory.
A few seconds later, the system window appeared.
[Skill combination successful]
[New Skill: Disaster Suppression Fist]
[Rank: Divine]
[Potential: Holy]
[280 Fragments consumed]
[Remaining Fragments: 21]
Lian kept his gaze on the last number.
561 Fragments.
540 Fragments spent.
And only 21 Fragments remaining.
He leaned back in his chair for a moment and then let out a short sigh.
"Well, I’m almost broke again."
Of course, unlike someone who truly regretted his decision, a faint smile could be seen on his face.
Two new combination skills, one for perception and analysis, and the other for releasing his body’s immense power in a direct strike.
And considering the new physical strength he had gained after being refined in the Dragon Blood River, the second combination could be very effective in future battles.
Most importantly, his new offensive skill had Holy potential!
The skill ranks were Common, Great, Divine, Holy, and Eternal, and now he had another offensive skill with Holy potential.
Lian closed the system window.
Now almost everything was ready, he only had to wait for the expedition to begin.
The day passed quickly, and at the start of the next day, the young Vorhelm left the dormitory building.
The evening light fell across the academy’s stone-paved grounds, and a gentle breeze moved the branches of the trees beside the path.
There were still few students around.
However, when he approached the central training ground, he noticed a small gathering along one of the main paths.
Several students were standing at a certain distance from each other and talking in low voices.
Something about the way they were standing caught Lian’s attention, they had gathered around someone.
Not with wild excitement, but with caution and respect.
He looked through the crowd and then saw a familiar face.
Roderick.

chapters.title: Chapter 605: The Day Everything Changed ( GT Bonus - )
paragraphs: Roderick.
The young man was standing in the center of the path.
He was wearing dark combat clothes, and signs of travel and many battles could be seen on parts of his equipment.
His hair was a little longer than before, but the biggest change was not in his appearance.
The way he stood was different.
Straight, calm, and with a confidence that made him look more like a noble who was used to giving orders than a student who had just returned from the Ruined Realm.
He listened to the people around him, but he did not feel the need to react to everything they said.
When one of the students asked him something, Roderick gave only a short answer and then turned his gaze toward the central building.
Lian examined him for a moment, he could not see his information, but the presence and aura he gave off were far beyond those of everyone around him.
He was at least Level 40, and there was a good chance that he had also completed his Second Evolution.
Apparently, Roderick had truly spent a lot of time hunting and fighting, this level of progress was considered a major achievement for most Awakened.
He did not have any more information about Roderick’s new abilities.
But from the change in the quality of his presence, he could tell that Roderick had gained a lot of combat experience during this time.
For a moment, he moved his gaze across the students around him.
Elena was not there.
His ex-girlfriend and Roderick’s current girlfriend was not standing beside him, unlike some of their previous meetings.
Lian only paid brief attention to her absence, then stopped thinking about it.
But at that exact moment, Roderick also noticed his presence.
His gaze passed through the crowd and remained fixed on Lian’s face for a few seconds.
Then he ended his brief conversation with the student in front of him and slowly walked toward Lian.
The students around them moved aside a little without anyone needing to tell them to.
Roderick stopped in front of Lian, and silence fell for a moment as the two young men looked at each other.
Roderick no longer had the impatient and angry behavior he had shown in the past, even when his gaze settled on the Ancestral Mark of the young Vorhelm, he showed no clear reaction.
Only after a few seconds did he speak.
"Lian."
"Roderick." Lian gave a slight nod.
The man examined him for a moment.
"I heard some interesting things have happened to you lately."
"It seems the same is true for you."
Roderick remained silent for a few seconds, then looked away from the Ancestral Mark.
"Looks like we both made good use of our time."
"Seems so." Lian gave a very faint smile.
He placed his hands behind his back, and his expression remained calm, but there was something in his eyes that the young Vorhelm knew very well.
The same old pride, the same desire to prove his superiority, only this time, it was hidden behind much more controlled behavior.
"The Land of First Dawn is a good opportunity to settle this once and for all."
"I agree." Lian nodded.
Roderick looked toward the central building for a moment, then turned back to him and spoke again.
"Of course, the result is already clear, this time, you won’t even be able to touch my clothes."
Lian kept his gaze directly on his face.
"If there’s something you want to prove, you’ll probably have plenty of chances there, you’d better not say something stupid that you’ll regret later."
Silence lasted for a few seconds.
Roderick neither became angry nor smiled, he only gave a slight nod.
"Good, but I’m not making empty promises, I’m just stating a simple fact, it’s time for you to understand how big the gap between us is."
This time, there were no clear threats in their conversation.
But the students standing nearby could easily feel the tension between them.
Roderick had spent a long time preparing to return to this point.
He was now Level 40, had gained more experience in real battles, and believed that the Land of First Dawn would give him a good chance to make up for the humiliation he had suffered in the past.
It was time for him to take back his royal throne, to make progress in the future, he needed to show that he was still the only true king!
But Lian? His gaze remained calm.
Even after seeing Roderick’s new level, not the slightest sign of worry appeared on his face, and this bothered Roderick more than any harsh reply could have.
"Good, both of you are here."
A serious voice came from the other end of the area.
Lian and Roderick turned their heads almost at the same time, Master Silas was walking toward them.
He was the same instructor who had previously been in charge of the Broken Crown Test and was known for his strictness and discipline.
Of course, Rindo was also beside him, and they were walking toward the two of them together.
When he came closer, he gave the two young men a brief look.
"Looks like all the members of the expedition have finally returned."
Roderick lowered his head slightly.
"Master."
Lian also nodded.
"Hello."
Silas began without any introduction.
"We’ll hold the final preparation meeting tomorrow., Lian, Rindo, and Roderick; only you three will take part in the expedition from this academy."
His gaze moved across all three of them.
"The route will begin at Base #3, after we transfer to the base, we’ll have the main part of the journey ahead of us on land."
Several students nearby looked at each other when they heard the name of the Land of First Dawn.
But Silas paid no attention to them.
"All equipment, medical supplies, and essential items must be checked before the final meeting, once we set out, you won’t have many chances to make up for anything you’re missing."
Lian nodded, fortunately, he had already taken care of this part.
"My equipment is ready." Roderick also answered calmly.
The instructor nodded, but contrary to their expectations, he still had no intention of leaving, and his gaze remained on Roderick for a moment before returning to Lian.
"I’ll make one thing clear right now."
Both of them looked at him.
"I’m aware of your personal conflicts, I don’t want to know which of you thinks he’s right or what happened in the past."
His voice became a little firmer.

"As long as you’re under the responsibility of this expedition, no personal conflict must put the mission’s safety at risk, I know the Land of First Dawn isn’t dangerous, but I don’t want any unexpected variables."
"Of course." Roderick answered without changing his expression.
"No problem." Lian also nodded.
He examined them for a few seconds and then spoke.
"I hope so."
He gave the academy grounds a brief look.
"Here, you might be able to make up for some mistakes with your family reputation or fame, but it’s not like that in the Ruined Realm."
He paused briefly.
"Over there, if you make a mistake, there won’t always be someone to save you before you die.
Lian looked at him in silence.
For a moment, memories of his first days in the Ruined Realm came back to his mind.
A time when even a Level 20 monster could crush all his bones.
A time when he had been forced to use almost all his strength just to obtain a golden key, and a time when surviving against the Dreadmaw Sovereign had felt more like a miracle.
But now? That same monster had become the third special member of his colony.
His body and soul had reached a much higher stage, and he had abilities that he could not even have imagined during his first trip.
However, he was not foolish enough to think that these improvements meant he had reached the end of his path.
The Land of First Dawn was still unknown.
And if his past experiences had taught him anything, it was that there were always creatures in the Ruined Realm that could change all his calculations.

Across from him, Roderick was also standing calmly, a young man who had returned at Level 40 with new confidence, a man who still believed that his past defeat had to be made up for one day and that he had to prove once again that he was the true king.
The question of which of them was superior went all the way back to their high school days, a long conflict that had existed between them.
Roderick had carried this obsession with superiority and being a king since those days, and he had tried to turn all the high school students into his subordinates.
That was where his conflicts with Lian had begun, and those conflicts had continued until today, for a time, it would not have been wrong to say that Roderick had even managed to win.
Lian still remembered the day everything changed.
After he failed his Awakening, his family no longer looked at him the same way. A few days later, Elena left him, and not long after that, the Vorhelm family threw him out of their home.
In contrast, Roderick had obtained a Four-Star Class and managed to join the strongest guild in the country, which was also one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
And Lian’s ex-girlfriend had become his new girlfriend.
He still believed he could change something. He trained, searched for ways to improve, and told himself every day that he must not give up.
But no one cared.
Roderick used his power and influence to turn Lian’s life into hell. His former friends slowly distanced themselves from him, and even those who had once treated him kindly pretended not to know him.
Lian endured life without family, without love, and without anyone he could rely on, well Except for Kain, though he wasn’t exactly someone you could rely on that much.
Some nights, he didn’t even have a place to sleep. Yet every morning, he got back up and searched for a way to survive.
He no longer thought about revenge, he no longer waited for anyone to come and save him.
He had learned only one thing.
In this world, if you were weak enough, even the people who once loved you could abandon you without a second thought.
Did he hate those days? perhaps those were the very years that shaped the Lian he was today.
And one day, this grudge between them had to come to an end.
The Land of First Dawn was approaching, and there would probably be many chances to reveal the true difference in their strength.
After examining both of them, Silas tucked the files under his arm.
"Be here on time tomorrow."
Roderick nodded.
"Of course."
"Okay, Master." Lian also replied.
Silas walked past them without saying anything else.
For a few moments, silence returned between the two young men.
Roderick gave Lian a brief look, then gave a slight nod with the same noble dignity and walked toward the central building.
Lian watched him leave, then put his hands in his pockets and looked at the evening sky.
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
The Land of First Dawn...

Of course, Rindo was also beside him, and they were walking toward the two of them together.
When he came closer, he gave the two young men a brief look.
"Looks like all the members of the expedition have finally returned."
Roderick lowered his head slightly.
"Master."
Lian also nodded.
"Hello."
Silas began without any introduction.
"We’ll hold the final preparation meeting tomorrow., Lian, Rindo, and Roderick; only you three will take part in the expedition from this academy."
His gaze moved across all three of them.
"The route will begin at Base #3, after we transfer to the base, we’ll have the main part of the journey ahead of us on land."
Several students nearby looked at each other when they heard the name of the Land of First Dawn.
But Silas paid no attention to them.
"All equipment, medical supplies, and essential items must be checked before the final meeting, once we set out, you won’t have many chances to make up for anything you’re missing."
Lian nodded, fortunately, he had already taken care of this part.
"My equipment is ready." Roderick also answered calmly.
The instructor nodded, but contrary to their expectations, he still had no intention of leaving, and his gaze remained on Roderick for a moment before returning to Lian.
"I’ll make one thing clear right now."
Both of them looked at him.
"I’m aware of your personal conflicts, I don’t want to know which of you thinks he’s right or what happened in the past."
His voice became a little firmer.

"As long as you’re under the responsibility of this expedition, no personal conflict must put the mission’s safety at risk, I know the Land of First Dawn isn’t dangerous, but I don’t want any unexpected variables."
"Of course." Roderick answered without changing his expression.
"No problem." Lian also nodded.
He examined them for a few seconds and then spoke.
"I hope so."
He gave the academy grounds a brief look.
"Here, you might be able to make up for some mistakes with your family reputation or fame, but it’s not like that in the Ruined Realm."
He paused briefly.
"Over there, if you make a mistake, there won’t always be someone to save you before you die.
Lian looked at him in silence.
For a moment, memories of his first days in the Ruined Realm came back to his mind.
A time when even a Level 20 monster could crush all his bones.
A time when he had been forced to use almost all his strength just to obtain a golden key, and a time when surviving against the Dreadmaw Sovereign had felt more like a miracle.
But now?
That same monster had become the third special member of his colony.
His body and soul had reached a much higher stage, and he had abilities that he could not even have imagined during his first trip.
However, he was not foolish enough to think that these improvements meant he had reached the end of his path.
The Land of First Dawn was still unknown.
And if his past experiences had taught him anything, it was that there were always creatures in the Ruined Realm that could change all his calculations.

Across from him, Roderick was also standing calmly, a young man who had returned at Level 40 with new confidence, a man who still believed that his past defeat had to be made up for one day and that he had to prove once again that he was the true king.
The question of which of them was superior went all the way back to their high school days, a long conflict that had existed between them.
Roderick had carried this obsession with superiority and being a king since those days, and he had tried to turn all the high school students into his subordinates.
That was where his conflicts with Lian had begun, and those conflicts had continued until today, for a time, it would not have been wrong to say that Roderick had even managed to win.
Lian still remembered the day everything changed.
After he failed his Awakening, his family no longer looked at him the same way.
A few days later, Elena left him, and not long after that, the Vorhelm family threw him out of their home.
In contrast, Roderick had obtained a Four-Star Class and managed to join the strongest guild in the country, which was also one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
And Lian’s ex-girlfriend had become his new girlfriend.
He still believed he could change something.
He trained, searched for ways to improve, and told himself every day that he must not give up.
But no one cared.
Roderick used his power and influence to turn Lian’s life into hell.
His former friends slowly distanced themselves from him, and even those who had once treated him kindly pretended not to know him.
Lian endured life without family, without love, and without anyone he could rely on, well Except for Kain, though he wasn’t exactly someone you could rely on that much.
Some nights, he didn’t even have a place to sleep.
Yet every morning, he got back up and searched for a way to survive.
He no longer thought about revenge, he no longer waited for anyone to come and save him.
He had learned only one thing.
In this world, if you were weak enough, even the people who once loved you could abandon you without a second thought.
Did he hate those days? perhaps those were the very years that shaped the Lian he was today.
And one day, this grudge between them had to come to an end.
The Land of First Dawn was approaching, and there would probably be many chances to reveal the true difference in their strength.
After examining both of them, Silas tucked the files under his arm.
"Be here on time tomorrow."
Roderick nodded.
"Of course."
"Okay, Master." Lian also replied.
Silas walked past them without saying anything else.
For a few moments, silence returned between the two young men.
Roderick gave Lian a brief look, then gave a slight nod with the same noble dignity and walked toward the central building.
Lian watched him leave, then put his hands in his pockets and looked at the evening sky.
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
The Land of First Dawn...

chapters.title: Chapter 606: A Familiar Place, New Faces
paragraphs: The sound of soldiers’ footsteps, iron wheels rolling over the stone pavement, and the occasional roars of monster carriers could be heard throughout the wide area of Base #3.
A blue light appeared in the base’s transportation area, and a few seconds later, four people emerged from it.
Lian stepped forward and looked around.
The huge stone walls, the guard towers, the Awakened moving in small groups past the military buildings, and the staff checking newly arrived supplies.
Everything was familiar.
Unlike the academy, where a large part of the student body was currently in the Ruined Realm, Base #3 was still full of activity.
He stood still for a few seconds, thinking about how much had happened since the last time he was here.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
Those were some interesting times.
"Lian."
Instructor Silas’s voice pulled him out of his thoughts.
The instructor was standing a few steps ahead with Rindo and Roderick, and he looked at Lian.
"We don’t have much time, first we need to complete the registration process."
Lian nodded.
"Okay, Instructor."
Then he followed them toward the Expedition Coordination Building, a special building for expeditions located in the eastern part of the base.
It was a large building with several waiting halls, permit inspection rooms, and a dedicated area for people who had received permission to enter restricted areas of the Ruined Realm.
When he entered the main hall, his eyes moved across the people present, the people who would be joining them on this trip.
There were very few of them, though this was not particularly surprising.
The Land of First Dawn was considered one of the most important areas under their country’s control and influence, a place where access to its resources was subject to strict regulations.
Even most powerful Awakened could not enter without a permit, and during this period, only ten people had received the right to explore the area.
Three people from their own academy.
Two representatives from the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
Three people from the French National Academy.
One person from the London Academy.
And the last person had come from Germany’s Adler National Academy.

In fact, only those three were supposed to participate, but their country’s government had decided to allow a limited number of talented students from several other countries to enter in order to strengthen international relations.
As Lian entered, he felt several curious gazes on him.
Some people openly examined the Ancestral Dragon Mark on his hand, while others only gave him a brief glance before returning to their own business.
Roderick walked toward the document inspection area with a straight posture and a calm manner.
Rindo also handed the academy’s documents to the receptionist without wasting any time.
The young Vorhelm preferred to wait in a corner for the time being, so he sat on one of the chairs beside the window and looked at the people present.
In terms of appearance, most of them were not very different from the elite students at their own academy, but the way they carried themselves showed that they were not ordinary Awakened.
Of course, he could not use his system to see their levels or traits.
The information the system displayed about monsters was not available in the same way for human Awakened.
Therefore, the only way to properly understand these people was to observe their behavior and evaluate their strength in real situations.
His gaze remained on two people sitting in the far end of the hall.
Both of them had symbols belonging to Ancient Guilds.
Interesting.
If even two Ancient Guilds had received only a limited number of spots for an expedition like this, then the value of this area must be much greater than what the public reports said.
At that moment, a young man with brown hair and blue clothes walked past the reception desk.
He was holding a long, folded umbrella that looked more like a decorative item than a piece of equipment for an Awakened.
However, the umbrella was not what caught Lian’s attention.
While talking to one of the staff members, the young man noticed that the woman needed help moving several small boxes.
Without waiting for her to ask, he placed his umbrella against the wall and picked up two boxes.
"Where should I put these?"
The staff member looked surprised for a moment before pointing out the place.
The young man carried the boxes over with a smile, picked up his umbrella again, and returned toward the hall.
On the way, he noticed one of the foreign candidates sitting alone on a chair.
He spoke to him for a few sentences, and when he realized that the other person was not very interested in talking, he nodded without insisting and continued on his way.
Then his eyes settled on Lian and Rindo, his smile grew a little wider, and he walked straight toward them.
"Hello! You two are from the academy in this country, right?"
Lian raised his head, while Rindo, who had just finished the document inspection, gave the young man a brief look.
"Yes."
"Great!"
The young man held out his hand with a friendly smile.
"Noah Laurent. I’m from the French National Academy, nice to meet you."
Lian stood up and shook his hand.
"Lian."
Noah paused for a moment. Then he looked more closely at his handsome face.
"Lian... Vorhelm?"
"Yeah."
Noah’s smile widened.
"So I’ve finally found you!"
"You were looking for me?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Not exactly." Noah laughed. "But when I found out you were joining this expedition too, I got curious and wanted to meet you in person, I’ve heard your name a lot lately."
His gaze briefly fell on the Ancestral Dragon Mark on Lian’s hand.
However, unlike most people who knew about him, he did not start asking a series of questions about the events in Verendal.
Instead, he turned toward Rindo.
"And you must be Mr. Rindo, right?
Rindo gave a slight nod.
"That’s right."
"It’s nice to meet you."
"Likewise."
Noah waited for a few seconds, but when he saw that Rindo had no intention of continuing the conversation, he smiled without showing the slightest sign of annoyance.
"Well, now I’ve met two more people."
The young Vorhelm looked at him.
"Are you asking everyone for their names?"
"Of course! We’re going to spend a week in the same caravan before entering an area where we’ll probably have to trust each other, wouldn’t it be better to get to know one another now?"
He thought for a moment and then nodded.
"That makes sense."
Noah smiled.
"I’m glad you agree."
Then he picked up his long umbrella from beside the chair and walked toward the two representatives from the Ancient Guilds.
Lian watched him leave for a few seconds.
What an interesting guy.
Rindo said nothing, as he was busy checking a short report he had received from the expedition staff.
However, Lian noticed that Noah was not only friendly toward them.
The young Frenchman spoke to almost everyone in the hall with the same respect and friendly attitude, from the candidates to the staff members.
At the same time, he had enough social awareness to stop bothering people when they showed no interest in talking.
Some time later, Silas entered the hall, and the scattered conversations slowly stopped as the ten candidates turned their attention toward the instructor.
He spoke without any introduction.
"The initial permits have been approved, but preparing the caravan will still take a few hours, the defensive equipment and support supplies must be fully checked."
Several people looked at one another.

"Until we announce the departure, you can move around within the permitted areas of the base. However, I want to make one thing clear, no one is allowed to leave the base without informing the staff."
He then looked at Rindo and Roderick.
"You’ll receive the final gathering time through your communication devices."
Rindo nodded, while Roderick also gave a short reply without any objections.
Lian stood up.
A few hours of free time?
For someone who had many memories of this base, it was a good opportunity, so he decided to visit some old places before the journey began.
The mission hall of Base #3 was still as crowded as he remembered.
The Awakened stood in front of large boards, talking about their recent hunts or the available missions.
The sounds of mission registration devices, the movements of the staff, and scattered conversations filled the hall.
Well, he had never actually come here before and had only seen it from a distance, he was not the type of person who liked doing missions very much.
He mostly preferred to explore freely.
