chapters.title: Chapter 607: After Kael’s Departure
paragraphs: However, the atmosphere in the hall was quite fun
Lian put his hands in his pockets and headed toward the central area.
There were several large ranking boards there.
Some were for the country’s academy students, while others covered all Awakened registered at the base.
He first looked at the student rankings.
There were five different categories.
Most Solo Hunts.
Most Group Hunts.
Best Mission Performance.
Best Exploration and Resource Discovery.
And Best Support and Rescue Performance.
He looked through the names on the boards for a moment.
"So even healers have their own rankings."
This system made sense.
If the number of monsters killed was the only standard for judging performance, many important roles within a group would be ignored.
A skilled healer could be far more valuable than someone who had only defeated a few weak monsters by saving the lives of several Awakened during a mission.
As expected, Kain still held first place in Most Solo Hunts, and no one had managed to beat his record yet.
However, his attention was mainly drawn to the second set of boards.
The official rankings of the country’s Awakened Association.
Unlike the student rankings, these rankings included all qualified Awakened registered at the base.
There were three main categories.
Individual Combat Achievements.
Group Combat Achievements.
And Exploration and Border Services.
A notice beside the boards explained that every three months, the top ten individuals or groups in each category would receive rewards based on their final scores.
Financial credits, training resources, shopping points at the Association’s store, and priority access to certain special missions.
He tilted his head slightly.
Not bad.
For Awakened who spent most of their time in the Ruined Realm, these rewards could be a good source of motivation.
But just as he was about to walk past the boards, his eyes stopped on the first-place team in the group category.
The group’s name was familiar, and he recognized it even without seeing their former leader’s name.
Kael’s former group held first place in the Group Combat Achievements ranking at Base #3, as he could tell from the names of its members.
Lian looked at the board for a few seconds before giving a faint smile.
So they were still doing well even after Kael left, and they had managed to remain the best group at the base.
It had been a long time since he had last seen them.
"Lian?"
A familiar voice came from behind him.
He turned around.
A girl with fiery red hair and a large sword on her back stood a few steps away.
Her eyes stayed on Lian’s face for a moment before she smiled.
"It’s really you!"
Lian recognized her immediately.
Rhea.
And three other familiar faces were standing beside her.
Zak, the dual-wielding swordsman, Bren, the shield-bearing warrior, and Elias, the group’s healer.
He smiled.
"Looks like you’re all still together."
"Did you think we could get rid of each other that easily?" Rhea walked a few steps closer.
The young Vorhelm glanced at the huge sword on her back.
"At least you still have the same sword."
She laughed.
"And I’m even better at using it than before.
"Good, I just hope you don’t insult people the first time you meet them anymore."
Rhea paused for a moment before laughing even louder.
"You still remember that?"
"It’s hard to forget. I think you called me a freeloader before you even knew my name."
Zak, who had been silent until then, raised the corner of his mouth.
"Well, that really was a big mistake on her part."
Rhea turned her head toward him.
"Zak!"
"It’s the truth." The swordsman shrugged.
Lian laughed, but the atmosphere soon became calmer.
Bren stepped forward and held out his hand.
"I’m glad to see you again."
Lian shook his hand.
"Me too."
"By the way, we never properly thanked you for what happened during the siege." Bren continued in a more serious tone.
"You don’t need to. This is my base too, so protecting it is only natural."
"Maybe to you, but we haven’t forgotten what you did."
This time, Rhea also nodded without making a joke.
During the siege of Base #3, they had witnessed the efforts Lian made and the dangers he faced to defend the base.
Those events had changed the way they saw him.
He was no longer just the unknown young man who had once argued for a bigger share in the middle of a battle against a Lava Behemoth.

"We haven’t seen you at this base since that incident. We heard that you went to a Special Area and came back with quite a few injuries. Unfortunately, we couldn’t check on you back then." Elias added with a gentle smile.
"A lot of time has passed since then, but yeah, we had a hard time in that Special Area."
At the same time, Lian had a chance to take a closer look at the four of them.
Since their last meeting, their presence had changed noticeably.
The mana around Elias’s body had become denser.
Bren’s body seemed much stronger.
Even Zak’s movements and Rhea’s balance were different from before.
He couldn’t see their exact status through the system, but judging from the pressure of their presence and their auras, he guessed that they had made great progress.
They were probably not far from their Second Evolution anymore.
Of course, this was only an estimate.
However, it seemed that the group had continued to grow even without Kael.
"By the way, how is Kael?" he asked.
Rhea nodded, but there was a hint of frustration in her voice.
"He’s doing well, though he barely has time to talk to us these days."
Lian already knew that Kael had joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
However, he still didn’t know much about his new situation.
"Are his training sessions that intense?"
"More intense than we expected." Zak answered.
She continued.
"The last time we talked, he said his training schedule took up almost all his time. Apparently, his new teachers are very strict about controlling the lightning element."
"He even said that he had only recently realized how much there was about lightning that he still didn’t know." Elias added.
The young Vorhelm smiled when he heard this, as he still remembered their old battle on the plains.
Kael’s control over the lightning element had been amazing even back then.
Unlike Lian, who mainly used lightning to improve his movements and physical attacks, Kael truly used it like a skilled mage.
If he was now training under the guidance of teachers from one of the Ancient Guilds, he could probably reach a much higher level in the future.
"Then he’s making a lot of progress."
Rhea smiled.
"I hope so, but don’t think we’re going to fall behind just because he left."
Lian glanced at the ranking board.
"It doesn’t look like you have."
Bren nodded.
"After he left, we had to change our fighting style."
"We used to coordinate most of our moves with Kael’s lightning attacks, but now we’ve divided the responsibility of controlling the battlefield among ourselves." Zak continued.
Rhea placed her hand on the hilt of her large sword.
"And I finally have more chances to attack."
"You weren’t exactly holding back before."
"Now I’m better at attacking." She replied casually.
Lian let out a short laugh, but despite the light tone of their conversation, he could feel the group’s real progress.
They hadn’t simply learned a few new skills.
They had been forced to rebuild their roles and teamwork without relying on their strongest former member.
And the results seemed to be quite good.
After talking for a while, Rhea realized that Lian had returned for the expedition to the Land of First Dawn.
"We’ll probably leave today."
"Then take care of yourself." She added.
Lian smiled.
"You all take care of yourselves too."
Bren put a hand on Zak’s shoulder and said that they should get back to their delayed missions.
Elias and Rhea also prepared to leave, but just before they parted ways, Rhea turned around again.
"Lian."
He looked at her, and the girl smiled.
"Next time you come back, maybe we can hunt together again. And I’m sorry for how I acted when we first met."
Lian smiled and nodded.
"Why not."
He watched them leave for a few seconds before looking at the first-place ranking on the board again.
Good.
It seemed the others hadn’t been sitting around doing nothing either.
When he returned to the departure area, the preparations for the convoy were almost complete.
Several armored carriages stood in the designated area, the transport monsters waited under the control of their handlers, and the escort groups were moving around the route.
The ten selected candidates were also gradually gathering at the meeting point.
Noah was one of the last people to return.
He had his long umbrella resting on his shoulder and was walking toward the group while talking to one of the staff members.
When he saw Lian, he smiled.
"So you’re back too."
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
"Your base is an interesting place. I had time to look around a little."
"For someone who just arrived, it probably is."
Noah’s smile widened.
"Have you been here before?"
"For a long time."
"Then if we come back here again, you’ll probably have to show me around the entire base."
"If I have time." The young Vorhelm shrugged
"I’ll count on that." He nodded with satisfaction.
At that moment, the escort commander’s voice came from the front of the area, and everyone present turned their attention toward him.
The commander was an experienced man wearing dark military armor.
Several senior officers, reconnaissance officers, and defensive mages stood beside him.
After checking the latest reports, he announced,
"All units, prepare to move. From this moment on, the safety of the ten selected candidates will be the escort’s top priority."
His gaze moved across the students.
"It will take about a week to reach our destination. During the journey, no one is allowed to leave the protected area without permission."

sentences.text: However, the atmosphere in the hall was quite fun
Lian put his hands in his pockets and headed toward the central area.
There were several large ranking boards there.
Some were for the country’s academy students, while others covered all Awakened registered at the base.
He first looked at the student rankings.
There were five different categories.
Most Solo Hunts.
Most Group Hunts.
Best Mission Performance.
Best Exploration and Resource Discovery.
And Best Support and Rescue Performance.
He looked through the names on the boards for a moment.
"So even healers have their own rankings."
This system made sense.
If the number of monsters killed was the only standard for judging performance, many important roles within a group would be ignored.
A skilled healer could be far more valuable than someone who had only defeated a few weak monsters by saving the lives of several Awakened during a mission.
As expected, Kain still held first place in Most Solo Hunts, and no one had managed to beat his record yet.
However, his attention was mainly drawn to the second set of boards.
The official rankings of the country’s Awakened Association.
Unlike the student rankings, these rankings included all qualified Awakened registered at the base.
There were three main categories.
Individual Combat Achievements.
Group Combat Achievements.
And Exploration and Border Services.
A notice beside the boards explained that every three months, the top ten individuals or groups in each category would receive rewards based on their final scores.
Financial credits, training resources, shopping points at the Association’s store, and priority access to certain special missions.
He tilted his head slightly.
Not bad.
For Awakened who spent most of their time in the Ruined Realm, these rewards could be a good source of motivation.
But just as he was about to walk past the boards, his eyes stopped on the first-place team in the group category.
The group’s name was familiar, and he recognized it even without seeing their former leader’s name.
Kael’s former group held first place in the Group Combat Achievements ranking at Base #3, as he could tell from the names of its members.
Lian looked at the board for a few seconds before giving a faint smile.
So they were still doing well even after Kael left, and they had managed to remain the best group at the base.
It had been a long time since he had last seen them.
"Lian?"
A familiar voice came from behind him.
He turned around.
A girl with fiery red hair and a large sword on her back stood a few steps away.
Her eyes stayed on Lian’s face for a moment before she smiled.
"It’s really you!"
Lian recognized her immediately.
Rhea.
And three other familiar faces were standing beside her.
Zak, the dual-wielding swordsman, Bren, the shield-bearing warrior, and Elias, the group’s healer.
He smiled.
"Looks like you’re all still together."
"Did you think we could get rid of each other that easily?" Rhea walked a few steps closer.
The young Vorhelm glanced at the huge sword on her back.
"At least you still have the same sword."
She laughed.
"And I’m even better at using it than before.
"Good, I just hope you don’t insult people the first time you meet them anymore."
Rhea paused for a moment before laughing even louder.
"You still remember that?"
"It’s hard to forget.
I think you called me a freeloader before you even knew my name."
Zak, who had been silent until then, raised the corner of his mouth.
"Well, that really was a big mistake on her part."
Rhea turned her head toward him.
"Zak!"
"It’s the truth." The swordsman shrugged.
Lian laughed, but the atmosphere soon became calmer.
Bren stepped forward and held out his hand.
"I’m glad to see you again."
Lian shook his hand.
"Me too."
"By the way, we never properly thanked you for what happened during the siege." Bren continued in a more serious tone.
"You don’t need to.
This is my base too, so protecting it is only natural."
"Maybe to you, but we haven’t forgotten what you did."
This time, Rhea also nodded without making a joke.
During the siege of Base #3, they had witnessed the efforts Lian made and the dangers he faced to defend the base.
Those events had changed the way they saw him.
He was no longer just the unknown young man who had once argued for a bigger share in the middle of a battle against a Lava Behemoth.
"We haven’t seen you at this base since that incident.
We heard that you went to a Special Area and came back with quite a few injuries.
Unfortunately, we couldn’t check on you back then." Elias added with a gentle smile.
"A lot of time has passed since then, but yeah, we had a hard time in that Special Area."
At the same time, Lian had a chance to take a closer look at the four of them.
Since their last meeting, their presence had changed noticeably.
The mana around Elias’s body had become denser.
Bren’s body seemed much stronger.
Even Zak’s movements and Rhea’s balance were different from before.
He couldn’t see their exact status through the system, but judging from the pressure of their presence and their auras, he guessed that they had made great progress.
They were probably not far from their Second Evolution anymore.
Of course, this was only an estimate.
However, it seemed that the group had continued to grow even without Kael.
"By the way, how is Kael?" he asked.
Rhea nodded, but there was a hint of frustration in her voice.
"He’s doing well, though he barely has time to talk to us these days."
Lian already knew that Kael had joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds.
However, he still didn’t know much about his new situation.
"Are his training sessions that intense?"
"More intense than we expected." Zak answered.
She continued.
"The last time we talked, he said his training schedule took up almost all his time.
Apparently, his new teachers are very strict about controlling the lightning element."
"He even said that he had only recently realized how much there was about lightning that he still didn’t know." Elias added.
The young Vorhelm smiled when he heard this, as he still remembered their old battle on the plains.
Kael’s control over the lightning element had been amazing even back then.
Unlike Lian, who mainly used lightning to improve his movements and physical attacks, Kael truly used it like a skilled mage.
If he was now training under the guidance of teachers from one of the Ancient Guilds, he could probably reach a much higher level in the future.
"Then he’s making a lot of progress."
Rhea smiled.
"I hope so, but don’t think we’re going to fall behind just because he left."
Lian glanced at the ranking board.
"It doesn’t look like you have."
Bren nodded.
"After he left, we had to change our fighting style."
"We used to coordinate most of our moves with Kael’s lightning attacks, but now we’ve divided the responsibility of controlling the battlefield among ourselves." Zak continued.
Rhea placed her hand on the hilt of her large sword.
"And I finally have more chances to attack."
"You weren’t exactly holding back before."
"Now I’m better at attacking." She replied casually.
Lian let out a short laugh, but despite the light tone of their conversation, he could feel the group’s real progress.
They hadn’t simply learned a few new skills.
They had been forced to rebuild their roles and teamwork without relying on their strongest former member.
And the results seemed to be quite good.
After talking for a while, Rhea realized that Lian had returned for the expedition to the Land of First Dawn.
"We’ll probably leave today."
"Then take care of yourself." She added.
Lian smiled.
"You all take care of yourselves too."
Bren put a hand on Zak’s shoulder and said that they should get back to their delayed missions.
Elias and Rhea also prepared to leave, but just before they parted ways, Rhea turned around again.
"Lian."
He looked at her, and the girl smiled.
"Next time you come back, maybe we can hunt together again.
And I’m sorry for how I acted when we first met."
Lian smiled and nodded.
"Why not."
He watched them leave for a few seconds before looking at the first-place ranking on the board again.
Good.
It seemed the others hadn’t been sitting around doing nothing either.
When he returned to the departure area, the preparations for the convoy were almost complete.
Several armored carriages stood in the designated area, the transport monsters waited under the control of their handlers, and the escort groups were moving around the route.
The ten selected candidates were also gradually gathering at the meeting point.
Noah was one of the last people to return.
He had his long umbrella resting on his shoulder and was walking toward the group while talking to one of the staff members.
When he saw Lian, he smiled.
"So you’re back too."
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
"Your base is an interesting place.
I had time to look around a little."
"For someone who just arrived, it probably is."
Noah’s smile widened.
"Have you been here before?"
"For a long time."
"Then if we come back here again, you’ll probably have to show me around the entire base."
"If I have time." The young Vorhelm shrugged
"I’ll count on that." He nodded with satisfaction.
At that moment, the escort commander’s voice came from the front of the area, and everyone present turned their attention toward him.
The commander was an experienced man wearing dark military armor.
Several senior officers, reconnaissance officers, and defensive mages stood beside him.
After checking the latest reports, he announced,
"All units, prepare to move.
From this moment on, the safety of the ten selected candidates will be the escort’s top priority."
His gaze moved across the students.
"It will take about a week to reach our destination.
During the journey, no one is allowed to leave the protected area without permission."

chapters.title: Chapter 608: The Colony’s Next Step
paragraphs: Roderick was standing calmly near one of the carriages.
After receiving a copy of the travel schedule, Rindo also headed toward the area assigned to the academy students.
Lian glanced at the main gate of the base.
For a moment, memories of his early days after returning came back to him, but this time, he wasn’t leaving the base to hunt a few ordinary monsters or look for a rare plant.
His destination was much farther away.
The heavy sound of the gate’s mechanism echoed through the area, the huge iron doors slowly opened, and the advance units began to move.
Then came the transport monsters and support carriages, and among them, the ten selected Awakened.
As he passed through the gate, he took one last look at the familiar walls of Base #3 before turning his attention to the road ahead.
The journey to the Land of First Dawn had begun.
The first two days of the journey passed without any important incidents.
The convoy traveled along relatively safe roads, while the reconnaissance teams checked the route ahead for monsters or possible obstacles.
Sometimes, creatures could be seen in the distant plains, but most of them preferred to stay away after sensing the presence of the escort forces.
During the day, the ten selected candidates were allowed to rest in the central part of the convoy, check their equipment, or gather more information about their destination.
Lian spent most of his time observing the route and reviewing his future plans, but there was one thing that had been on his mind for a long time.
The Colony.
He now had three Special Colony Members.
One.
Two.
And Three.
All three were powerful creatures with completely different abilities.
However, the capacity for ordinary members was still untouched.
Lian opened the window for his Colony Sovereign Talent.
[Special Colony Members: 3/5]
[Ordinary Members: 0/100]
One hundred ordinary members, and he hadn’t filled even a single slot.
He looked at the number one hundred for a moment.
"The problem is that I’m really not interested in personally commanding a huge army."
From the beginning, he had been more interested in having a few powerful subordinates than gathering a large number of weak monsters.
Managing an army, even if all its members could be controlled through the Colony Link, required constant decision-making.
Positioning, supplies, choosing targets, coordination during battle, and most importantly, preventing dozens of creatures from waiting for his direct orders at the same time.
He had no interest in being forced to decide the movements of every single subordinate in the middle of a battle.
However, now that he had three Special Colony Members, another idea had come to his mind.
"Maybe they don’t all need to be directly under my command."
He opened the Colony Structure section.
[Natural Colony Hierarchy]
[Sovereign]
[Queen]
[Commander]
[Worker]
Lian looked at the information for a few seconds, as he had never assigned any specific organizational positions to his Colony Members before.
He himself held the position of Sovereign.
However, One, Two, and Three were only considered Special Colony Members, being a Special Colony Member did not automatically mean having the position of Commander or Queen.
These were two different systems.
He placed his hand under his chin.
If he added more ordinary members to the Colony in the future, he could probably form smaller groups under the command of his Special Colony Members.
One was suitable for breaking defensive positions and fighting in heavy battles.
Two had various abilities that could be used for hunting and complex operations.
And Three? Despite all the crimes it had committed in the past, its intelligence could not be ignored.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign had commanded creatures under its control for decades and had a great deal of experience using its subordinates to achieve different goals.
In terms of leadership, it might even be more suitable than the other two members.
Lian smiled for a moment.
Thirty members for each of them...
With this arrangement, ninety ordinary members would be divided into three groups, while the remaining ten slots could be used for independent missions or special situations.
But for now, this was only an idea.
He still didn’t know how well each Special Colony Member could manage its subordinates in practice.
Besides, he still had two empty slots for Special Colony Members, which meant he could instead assign a small battalion of twenty members to each Special Colony Member.
On the other hand, the exact role of the Queen position in the Colony’s structure was still not entirely clear to him, so there was no need to rush into assigning positions.
Lian closed the window.
"First, I need to find suitable members."
"Then I can decide how to divide them."
At the same time, another one of his personal belongings caught his attention.
The Celestial Book of Treasure.
He looked at the book’s cover for a moment, the Land of First Dawn was famous as a paradise of treasures.
According to the information he had read earlier, many rare training resources, ancient treasures, and unknown artifacts could be found in this region.
This was one of the main reasons why entry into the area was so strictly limited, but for him, the region’s appeal was not limited to the value of its resources.
He had a book that could identify hidden treasures.
The last time he had used it to search for something, he had found the Sphere of Witness.
Lian ran his fingers over the book’s cover, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
This book was going to be very useful there.
Of course, he still didn’t know how well the resources in that region would match his current level of power.
But even if he couldn’t use a treasure right away, it would still be worth keeping or selling.
From that point of view, the upcoming journey could bring him great benefits.
On the afternoon of the second day, he found an opportunity to rest for a short while beside one of the support carriages.
At the same time, Noah came toward him from another part of the convoy, carrying his long folded umbrella and holding two containers of a hot drink.
"Want one?"
Lian looked at him.
"What is it?"
"A hot drink. I thought you might want one too."
He accepted one of the containers.
"Thanks.
Noah sat beside him, but unlike what someone might have expected from his sociable personality, he didn’t start talking right away.
For a while, they both looked at the wide plains in front of them.
Then,
"Have you traveled along this route before?"
"Not this far. I mostly operated around the base."
"I haven’t been to this region either."
Noah took a sip of his drink.
"Honestly, I’m more curious about what the place actually looks like than worried about the dangers."
"Because of the treasures?" The young Vorhelm gave him a brief glance.
"Those too, but I’ve heard that some parts of the region are completely different from any of the known areas in the Ruined Realm."
The young Frenchman smiled.
"I think seeing a completely different place is worth the journey by itself."
Lian thought about those words for a moment.
Noah had been friendly from the beginning, but it seemed that his interest in this mission was not only about gaining power or fame.
He genuinely enjoyed discovering new things.
At that moment, one of the guards passing by them put a heavy container on the ground and bent down to check its damaged straps.
Noah put his drink aside without saying anything unnecessary.
"Do you need help?"
The man raised his head, and a few seconds later, Noah was helping him secure the container.
Lian watched the scene.
"He really treats everyone this way." He whispered softly.
What was even more interesting was that he didn’t seem to be trying to attract attention, even when no one was watching him, he still acted the same way.
He took another sip of his hot drink, at least, Noah didn’t seem like a bad person.
The third day also passed in relative peace.
The convoy traveled through several rocky areas, and along the way, the scouts spotted several small groups of monsters in the distance.
However, none of them posed a serious threat to the convoy, during one of their short stops, Roderick spent some time training alone.
Lian watched his movements from a distance.
His speed, accuracy, and the way he shifted his weight during his attacks, everything was more organized than before.
Roderick no longer relied only on raw strength and his noble confidence, his movements showed signs of real combat experience.

After watching for a few minutes, Lian turned his gaze away, it was clear that the result of their draw had made Roderick extremely angry, and he had spent all this time after the final exam getting stronger.
It seemed he wanted revenge for the humiliation of that day, no matter what it took.
The young Vorhelm burst out laughing at the sight, this poor guy didn’t know that he couldn’t even defeat an ant... his ant.

Rindo also spent most of his time checking the travel schedule and the condition of the group, he treated the other selected candidates politely and formally, but showed no interest in unnecessary conversations.
When Noah once tried to ask for his opinion about their destination, he gave only a short answer before returning to the map.
Noah didn’t continue the conversation either, and he showed no signs of being upset.
It seemed he had quickly realized that Rindo was not the kind of person who could be drawn into a long conversation with nothing more than a friendly attitude and a few casual words.
By the end of the third day, the convoy had continued along its route without any major problems.
But on the morning of the fourth day... everything changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 609: Ten Targets, One Trap
paragraphs: The road passed between two rocky slopes.
On the right, a slope covered with gray rocks rose toward higher ground. On the left, it led to an open plain where several low hills could be seen in the distance.
The sky was partly cloudy.
Sunlight sometimes passed through the clouds and fell on the rocks beside the road.
The convoy moved at a steady speed.
The advance units were several hundred meters ahead, while the guard groups moved around the central carriages.
Lian was sitting inside one of the carriages reserved for the selected candidates, his eyes half-closed as he examined the flow of the surrounding mana.
At the same time, the rough sound of a communication device came from the front of the convoy.
"Commander, we’ve found something suspicious up ahead."
"Report." The man in charge of the escort immediately replied.
A few seconds of static followed, and then the scout continued.
"There are several damaged carriages beside the road. It looks like a convoy has been attacked."
The commander looked toward the road ahead.
"Any signs of enemies?"
"Not yet, but we’ve found several bodies, and there might be an injured person beside the carriages."
"Distance?"
"About two hundred meters from the main route."
The commander remained silent for a moment before raising his hand.
"All units, stop."

The order was sent to different parts of the convoy through the communication devices, the carriage wheels slowly came to a stop, and the transport monsters halted under the control of their handlers.
The commander headed toward the front of the convoy.
However, unlike what an inexperienced person might have done, he didn’t order all his forces to approach the damaged convoy.
Instead, he called over several members of the reconnaissance team.
"Approach from the right side, and don’t touch the carriages until the area has been checked."
He then ordered the defensive mages to check the surrounding area for any unknown mana flows.
Lian looked outside through the carriage window, and several broken carriages could be seen beside the road in the distance.
One had completely overturned.
A small amount of smoke was rising from the back of another.
Two motionless bodies lay on the ground, and a person wearing bloodstained clothes was sitting beside one of the wheels.
At first glance, the scene looked like the result of an attack by several powerful monsters, but the longer he looked, the more he felt that something was wrong.
He stepped out of the carriage and stood within the area marked off by the guards, the distance was still great, but his enhanced senses allowed him to notice certain details.
One of the broken wheels was several meters away from the main carriage, yet there were no clear marks in the dirt around it showing that it had been dragged or rolled there.
In another area, the broken pieces of wood were scattered almost in the same direction, but the impact marks on the carriage did not match that direction.
Lian slightly furrowed his brows, these things didn’t look like they had been broken here.
He turned his attention to the injured person, who was still sitting beside the wheel, but his behavior was strange.
Every time the scouts moved a little closer, he raised his head and looked at them, yet he neither shouted for help nor tried to make his way toward the main road.
What is he waiting for?
At that moment, Rindo also approached from another part of the convoy, his eyes settled on the injured person before he spoke to the escort commander.
"I suggest that no one gets any closer."
The commander turned his head toward him.
"Do you have a reason?"
"The injured person isn’t acting normally, and besides, the positions of the carriage remains don’t look like the result of an ordinary accident."
"It looks like some of the pieces were brought here from somewhere else." Lian also nodded and added.
The commander looked at both of them for a few seconds before turning to one of his officers.
"Hold the reconnaissance team in place, don’t let them move any farther."
The man immediately passed on the order.
The commander looked at the scene again, he had reached a similar conclusion, and there was a high chance that it was a trap.
In such a situation, his first duty was to protect the ten selected candidates, so he gave an order through his communication device.
"All ten selected candidates, return to the central area, defensive units, take your positions around the outer ring, mages, prepare the main defensive barrier."

If it’s really a trap, why is it so obvious?

Five paths and five connection points, all of them were forming a flow that returned toward the central barrier.

Rindo was trapped several meters away, and Noah could also be seen behind one of the translucent walls.

Ten names.
The names of all ten selected candidates.

Interesting.

A black bird with its wings spread wide, a vulture that seemed to be landing on a fresh corpse.
One of the soldiers instinctively took a step back when he saw the symbol.
"The Black Vultures..."
His voice was barely audible, but the escort commander heard him, and his expression immediately became more serious.
The Black Vultures.
A criminal organization whose name was linked to murder, theft, kidnapping, and illegal missions.

On the left, it led to an open plain where several low hills could be seen in the distance.
The sky was partly cloudy.
Sunlight sometimes passed through the clouds and fell on the rocks beside the road.
The convoy moved at a steady speed.
The advance units were several hundred meters ahead, while the guard groups moved around the central carriages.
Lian was sitting inside one of the carriages reserved for the selected candidates, his eyes half-closed as he examined the flow of the surrounding mana.
At the same time, the rough sound of a communication device came from the front of the convoy.

"Report." The man in charge of the escort immediately replied.

"There are several damaged carriages beside the road.

"Any signs of enemies?"

"Distance?"

chapters.title: Chapter 610: They Chose the Wrong Target
paragraphs: The presence of the Black Vultures here had a very clear meaning.
The convoy from Base #3 had become the target of a planned operation.
One of the five masked figures remained on the high ground to the right, holding a metal panel in his hand, and he seemed to be in control of the mana flows of the formation.
The second person took position on the high ground to the left.
He held a long weapon that allowed him to cover the movements of the guards from a long distance.
The other two moved toward the sides of the convoy, while the fifth person walked slowly forward along the main road.
He was not taller than his companions, but the way he moved and the reactions of the other four showed that he was the leader of the operation.
The masked man stopped about thirty meters from the central area and looked at the ten semi-transparent enclosures for a moment.
Then he turned his head toward his people.
"None of the ten targets can die." His voice was calm and almost emotionless.
"As for the others, it doesn’t matter if they resist."
The escort commander immediately drew his sword.
"All units, defensive formation! Protect the central area!"
However, before the guards could finish changing their positions, a sharp sound came from the high ground.
Whooosh!
Something thin passed through the air, and one of the guards standing a few meters away from the mages protecting the convoy turned his head.
But it was too late.
A metal projectile passed through a gap in his neck armor, his body froze for a moment, and then he fell to the ground with a muffled sound.
The guard beside him immediately raised his shield, and the second projectile struck its surface, creating a brief shower of sparks.
However, the masked figure on the high ground did not stop. He turned his weapon toward another target, while two ground attackers also moved in from the opposite side.
One of the guards rushed forward to meet them with his sword.
The first attacker deflected the strike with his short weapon and moved past the guard’s body. At the same time, the edge of his weapon struck the back of the guard’s knee.
The man lost his balance.
Before he could steady himself, another strike hit his shoulder and knocked him to the ground.
The attacker did not even stop to check whether the man was dead or not. His target was reaching the central area.

This behavior was familiar to Lian, and he could tell with just one look that they were professionals. The masked figures were carrying out a mission, and it was clear that they had been sent here with a specific goal.
Every move they made was meant to remove an obstacle or help them reach their target.
As far as he knew, the Black Vultures worked on contracts. That meant someone had hired them to attack their convoy.
But who would dare to attack a convoy protected by the governments? Each of the ten young people in this convoy had come from one of the world’s most respected academies.
The escort commander shouted from behind the circle of guards.
"Do you understand who you’re dealing with? These people are under official protection!"
The leader of the Black Vultures gave him a brief look.
"We know."
"Then you should retreat before it’s too late."
"If they were ordinary people, why would we spend so much time preparing this plan?" The masked man tilted his head slightly.
Then he moved his gaze across the ten selected candidates’ enclosures.
"That’s exactly why we’re here."
The commander gritted his teeth, as this answer removed all the important doubts.
The attackers were not trying to steal a treasure or something like that. They had not even shown any interest in the convoy’s expensive equipment.
They had come to kidnap the ten selected Awakened.
Some of them were children of powerful families, while others were supported by organizations with great influence.
If the Black Vultures managed to capture these people alive, they could demand huge amounts of money, resources, or political favors in exchange for their release.
They might even have been hired by someone to carry out this exact task.
And worse, the entire plan had been designed using information that should never have been in their hands.
The commander glanced at the active formation for a moment.
Damn it...
He had taken every necessary step to protect the selected candidates, but those same measures had placed the ten people in the best possible position to be kidnapped.
Inside one of the enclosures, Roderick clenched his fist, his gaze fixed on the semi-transparent wall. For a moment, he examined the flow of mana within it.
Then he took one step forward and punched the surface directly.
BANG!
The light of the enclosure shook violently, and faint cracks appeared across its surface for a fraction of a second.
But they quickly closed again.
He frowned slightly, as his punch had not been weak.
His physical strength had increased greatly after his recent progress, and his fist could withstand a powerful impact.
However, instead of simply resisting the attack, the structure of the enclosure spread part of the impact’s energy among the outer nodes.
Because of this, breaking it with raw strength was difficult.
Roderick looked outside. One of the masked figures was approaching.
Without rushing, he prepared his fist again.
Inside another enclosure, Rindo examined the movement of the mana flow instead of attacking.
He had noticed that the light on the walls changed slightly whenever the leader of the Black Vultures approached.
It was as if the formation had to move part of its energy whenever it opened an enclosure and took a target out.
He looked toward one of the outer connection points, then spoke to the escort commander in a firm voice.
"On the left! The main flow passes through the node near the rock. If that point is disabled, part of the formation will become unstable."
The reason their protective enclosures had suddenly turned into a prison against them was an extremely powerful formation that seemed to require five nodes to function.
Each of these nodes helped establish and operate the formation, and the mana needed to power it flowed from one node to another.
The commander immediately signaled to one of the mages, but before the mage had time to prepare an attack, the long-range attacker fired from the high ground.
The projectile struck the ground in front of him and released a wave of pressure, forcing him to retreat.
This time, Rindo looked at the shooter.
"So they won’t let us get close to the nodes."
At the same time, Lian was still standing inside his own enclosure. Unlike Roderick, he had not attacked the wall even once.
His gaze only moved between different points, five paths, five nodes, and an energy flow that moved between them in a clear pattern.
He was examining the structure of the formation step by step.
Interesting.

This trap had been activated using the mana of the defensive barrier itself. After examining the barrier’s protective pattern, the formation had turned the outer flow into a network of separate enclosures.
However, to keep the nodes working together, it still depended on reflective paths.
Sunlight passed through the small metal plates and kept the formation’s connection paths clearly marked at different points.
At first, this was an advantage, because it allowed the nodes to stay connected without needing direct physical links.
But for Lian? It was a major weakness.
He gave a faint smile.
"Looks like luck is on my side today."
Inside the Eclipse Core, a small amount of Eclipse Energy began to move.
He raised his right hand.
Ordinary sunlight passed through the semi-transparent wall of the enclosure.
That was enough.
He activated the talent [The Corrupt Sun] and guided a very thin stream of Eclipse Energy along one of the reflective paths.
The first strand passed through the inner surface of the enclosure, following the same path that the formation had left open for the exchange of reflected light.
The corrupted energy moved along the reflected light and headed toward the first node, which was hidden between two rocks some distance away.
When it reached the node, no explosion occurred. Only one of the mana lines on its surface changed color.
Its color shifted from pale blue to black, and then a small part of its energy structure began to break down.
At that moment, the masked figure responsible for controlling the formation raised his head. His gaze fixed on the metal panel in his hand.
One of the indicators had changed.
"What...?"
He immediately sent more mana into the node, but the result was the opposite of what he expected.
Instead of stabilizing the structure, the new energy passed through the damaged path and exposed a larger part of the lines to corruption.
The masked figure pulled his hand back.
"Damn it!"
Farther below, the leader of the Black Vultures heard him.
"What happened?"
"One of the formation’s nodes is breaking down!"
"Strengthen it."
"I can’t! The mana structure is being corrupted!"
The leader remained silent for a moment, then turned his gaze toward the ten enclosures and focused on a calm young man who was still holding his right hand up.
Lian released the second strand. This time, the Eclipse Energy passed through the reflective surface of one of the plates beside the road and headed toward another node.
At that moment, the person controlling the formation noticed its path.
He used his control device to turn one of the reflective plates and tried to block the path of the light.
The young Vorhelm noticed the change, the second strand lost its path for a moment, but before it could fully disperse, his gaze settled on another reflection.
If one path was blocked, he could simply choose another.
There were not just one or two paths and lines of light and reflection but there were countless ones.
A broken metal surface lay a few meters away from the node and he changed the direction of the energy, and the strand passed through a second reflection before reaching the side of the node.
Although he could have used other methods to break through, he chose this approach to examine the structure and complexity of the arrays.
Perhaps he could learn more about them in the process.
This time, the masked figure did not even have time to correct the path.
Crack!
A dry sound came from the structure of the formation, and one of the nodes completely stopped working, as a result, the wall of the enclosure near Rindo shook for a moment.
He felt the change and immediately looked back at Lian.
The young Vorhelm was still examining the energy paths, but Rindo now understood what was happening.
Lian had found a way to destroy the network of the array

chapters.title: Chapter 611: The Trap Is Broken
paragraphs: However, another problem remained.
The protective mages were still trying to regain control by increasing the energy of the main barrier, and while they thought this was the right thing to do, they were making a huge mistake.
Rindo turned his head toward the commander.
"Stop feeding energy into the defensive barrier!"
The commander looked at him.
"What?"
"The more energy you put into it, the longer you’ll keep those enclosures active."
One of the mages immediately checked his control device, and a few seconds later, the color drained from his face.
"He’s right, Commander! The new energy is being transferred to the outer network!"
The commander immediately gave an order.
"Cut off the energy supply to the barrier! Right now!"
The mages immediately stopped the flow of mana, preventing the formation from using any more energy from the convoy.
However, a considerable amount of energy still remained inside the nodes, and the leader of the Black Vultures had no intention of letting his plan fail so easily.
"Subdue the one destroying the nodes."
The order was brief.
One of the two ground attackers immediately changed direction, moved toward Lian’s enclosure, and pulled a metal device from his waist.
The device was designed to restrain Awakened. It consisted of folding rings that could close around a target’s body once they got close enough.
However, before the attacker could reach him, Lian released the third strand of Eclipse Energy. This time, his target was a node located closer to Roderick’s enclosure.
The corrupted energy moved along the reflected light, and just as it reached the node, Roderick felt a change in the pressure against the walls of his enclosure.
Without hesitation, he raised his fist and focused his striking force on the point where he had noticed the disturbance a few moments earlier.
And then... CRACK!
His punch struck the wall, splitting the enclosure’s light around the damaged point, and this time, the cracks did not close.
He stepped forward and delivered a second punch, causing a large section of the wall to collapse.
He stepped out through the scattered light and immediately turned his fist toward the attacker who had been approaching Lian to restrain him.
The masked man was forced to change direction, and the two weapons collided with a heavy sound.
Roderick pushed forward, forcing the attacker to take one step back, but instead of trying to fight him head-on, the man turned his body and attacked from a lower angle.
Roderick deflected the strike with the side of his weapon, then closed the distance with a short forward movement.
The attacker had no choice but to retreat several meters to avoid the next strike.
Roderick did not chase him. Instead, his gaze briefly shifted toward Lian, who was still inside his enclosure.
But now, the light on Lian’s walls had also become unstable at several points.
Without saying anything, Roderick placed himself between the attacker and Lian’s enclosure.
Lian noticed the movement for a moment, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
"At least you understand that this isn’t the time to settle personal scores."
At the same time, the leader of the Black Vultures finally realized where the real problem was.
The young man who was supposed to be one of the operation’s most valuable hostages was destroying the formation without using raw power.
And worse, the type of energy he was using was different from ordinary energy.
He looked at the reflective plates for a moment, then signaled to the person controlling the formation.
"Cut off the light paths."
The masked man immediately turned several of the remaining plates. The direct reflections decreased, but it was already too late.
Lian had already identified alternative paths, and he used the fourth strand of Eclipse Energy to reach the nearby node.
Sunlight reflected off the surface of one of the convoy’s armored carriages, and this time, the strand traveled along a shorter path before reaching the node.
A few seconds later... CRACK!
The fourth node stopped working.
Rindo’s enclosure shook for a moment before part of its wall collapsed.
Rindo immediately moved out of the enclosure.
Instead of heading toward the enemy, he went straight to the escort commander and passed on the information he had gathered over the past few minutes.
"There’s still one main node left. As long as it’s active, some of the enclosures won’t open completely."
The commander nodded.
"Where is it?"
Rindo pointed toward the northern side of the road.
"Behind the broken rock, near the man controlling the formation."
The commander immediately signaled to the guards, but before they could launch their attack, the light of the fifth strand of Eclipse Energy passed by Lian’s enclosure.
The young Vorhelm had found the final path.
This node was more resistant than the others, and a large part of the formation’s stored energy remained inside it.
He released more Eclipse Energy, causing a slight strain to form inside his core.
He immediately limited the flow.
There was no need to use up all his reserves, as the node’s structure was already under pressure.
He only needed to destroy the last part that kept it connected to the others.
The fifth strand reached the connection point. For a few moments, the node’s mana flow resisted, but then the corrupted lines spread throughout its structure.
And finally... CRRACK!
The fifth node broke.
At the same time, all ten separate enclosures lost their stability. The semi-transparent walls around the selected candidates collapsed and turned into scattered particles of mana.
Lian lowered his hand and let out a calm breath.
"Well, that’s done."
However, the battle was not over yet.
As soon as the enclosures collapsed, one of the masked attackers threw three restraining devices toward one of the selected candidates from France.
His goal was clear.
If they couldn’t capture all ten people, they might still have a chance to take at least one of them with them.
But before the devices could reach their target, the sound of something metallic opening rang through the air.
Click!
A round umbrella with twelve metal ribs opened in front of the target, and the first restraining device struck its surface before being deflected.
The second came from a lower angle.
With a short turn of his body, Noah moved the umbrella’s handle and changed the projectile’s direction.
The third device arrived almost at the same time, but this time, Noah closed the umbrella. Its narrow tip struck the restraining device, and a precise hit sent it toward the ground.
Thud!
The metal device sank into the dirt.
He took one step forward. His usual smile was still on his face, but his eyes had become completely serious.
"I don’t think you’re taking anyone with you."
The masked attacker charged without answering. He pulled a short weapon from his waist and made a direct attack toward Noah’s side.
The young Frenchman lowered his closed umbrella, and the two weapons collided.
However, instead of meeting his opponent’s strength head-on, he turned the umbrella’s handle and redirected the force of the attack to the side. Then he stepped into his opponent’s range.
The tip of the umbrella struck the attacker’s wrist, and in the same movement, its curved handle locked behind the man’s forearm.
Noah turned his body, disrupting his opponent’s balance and forcing him to take two steps back.
Everything happened within a few seconds.
However, Lian, who had been freed nearby, watched every movement. His eyes narrowed slightly for a moment.
Strange.
Noah’s stance did not seem completely natural for the weapon he was holding. The distance between his feet, the angle of his shoulders, and the position of his free hand.
It was as if he was used to fighting with a longer and different weapon.
Could that umbrella not be his main weapon?
But at that very moment, Noah opened the umbrella again.
With a very precise turn, he deflected the attacker’s next strike, then quickly closed the umbrella and delivered a heavy blow to the man’s wrist.
The masked man’s weapon nearly slipped out of his hand.

Noah immediately took one step back without stopping, keeping the right defensive distance between them. His movements were so natural and professional that even Lian began to doubt his own judgment for a moment.
"Maybe I’m overthinking it."
In any case, one thing was clear. This young Frenchman was far more skilled than his friendly appearance suggested.
On the other side of the battlefield, Rindo was helping the guards move the selected candidates away from the damaged area.
Without shouting or giving unnecessary orders, he passed on the information they needed and pointed out the paths that were still covered by the enemy’s long-range attacker.
Roderick had also forced one of the ground attackers to retreat toward the nearby rocks.
His sword moved with precise speed, and every strike was meant to limit his opponent’s movements.
However, the attacker was no inexperienced fighter either. After two heavy clashes, he realized that fighting Roderick directly was dangerous.
Therefore, instead of continuing the fight, he used the broken rocks around him to create distance.
At the same time, Lian turned his gaze toward the front of the convoy, where one of the injured guards lay on the ground.
The long-range attacker on the high ground had turned his weapon toward him.
The young Vorhelm saw the movement and acted without hesitation. Two enormous black wings spread open behind him.
[Wings of God]
A strong gust of wind swept around his body, and several guards instinctively looked up.
"H-How did he get those?!" Roderick whispered in disbelief, unable to believe what he was seeing with his own eyes.
The shadow of the two black wings fell across the ground, covering part of the road for a moment. But before anyone even had time to take in the sight, Lian rose into the air.
He shot toward the high ground at incredible speed.
The long-range attacker noticed him approaching and turned his weapon, but it was already too late.
Lian appeared a short distance away from him and thrust his right hand forward.
BANG!
His fist struck the middle of the weapon. The metal broke under the pressure, sending shattered pieces flying in every direction, and the attacker threw himself backward to avoid the next strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 612: The Vultures’ Retreat ( Edited )
paragraphs: However, the force of the impact had traveled all the way up his arm, and for a moment, he could not move his fingers properly.
Lian was about to move forward, but at that exact moment, the escort commander’s voice came from below.
"All selected candidates, stay back! Support units, cover the others!"
He glanced down briefly.

The central area of the convoy was still vulnerable, two guards were lying on the ground, several selected candidates had only just escaped their enclosures, and the main defensive formation had also been disabled.
On the other hand, it was unclear what other traps the masked figures might have prepared along their escape route.
Besides, even if he captured them, he would gain nothing. The Black Vultures sent on missions were not given any information about the reasons behind those missions.
They were also trained to kill themselves if they were captured, so it was unlikely that he could get any information from them.
Lian watched the retreating attacker for a moment, then decided not to move any farther away from the convoy. With a single movement of his wings, he returned to the road.
At the same time, the leader of the Black Vultures reviewed the final situation on the battlefield.
The formation had been destroyed, all ten targets had been freed, and the escort forces were forming their defensive formation again.
And at least three of the selected candidates had shown far greater strength than the initial estimates suggested.
His gaze rested on Roderick for a moment, then moved to Noah, and finally to Lian.
The young man had two black wings spread behind him and had destroyed one of his men’s weapons with a single punch.
He narrowed his eyes. The information they had was incomplete. They knew that Lian Vorhelm had obtained the Pendragon Ancestral Mark.
However, the details of his new abilities were not available in public reports. On the other hand, the energy he had used to destroy the formation had a very unusual nature.
If the operation continued, its cost would probably become much higher than they had planned.
More importantly, the mission was to capture ten hostages alive in the shortest possible time, not to fight until every last man was dead.
The leader raised his right hand.
"The operation is canceled."
One of his companions, who was still fighting Roderick, turned his head.
"But we still—"
"I said retreat."
The man’s tone had not changed, but that was enough. The two ground attackers immediately moved away.
The person responsible for the formation gathered his remaining equipment and moved along the upper path between the rocks.
The long-range attacker also abandoned his broken weapon and retreated after the others.
Noah did not try to chase the man in front of him. Instead, he first looked at the injured guard behind him and made sure there was no immediate danger threatening him.
Roderick did not lower his fist either, but he did not leave the protected area without the commander’s order.
Farther away, the leader of the Black Vultures stopped for a moment before retreating, his gaze fixed on Lian.
"The information we had about you was outdated."
Lian looked at him calmly, and the masked man continued.
"We won’t make the same mistake next time."
"Then you’d better make sure there is a next time." The young Vorhelm spoke calmly.
Silence followed for a moment, then the leader turned away without answering, and the five attackers retreated along the rocky paths they had prepared in advance
Lian didn’t pursue them, but that didn’t mean he intended to let them leave alive.
He preferred to keep the abilities of his cores a secret from these bastards.
Black energy of the End appeared at his fingertips, which he shaped into thin lines of light, each line had a corresponding reflection on the body of one of the vultures.
He adjusted them so that the moment they disappeared from sight, they would immediately meet their end.
The energy of the End would erase their existence in an instant, leaving behind no evidence whatsoever.
None of the escort forces were allowed to pursue them without an order, and after checking the injured, the commander decided that securing the convoy had to come before everything else.
The battle was over.
But its consequences were far more serious than a simple victory might suggest.
A few minutes after the Black Vultures retreated, the convoy was still on high alert.
The escort commander did not allow the guards to leave their positions immediately.
First, the scouting teams checked the surrounding high ground. Then the mages examined the remains of the Inverted Reflection Array to see whether any other active nodes remained.
This was the same formation that had turned the protective enclosures into a prison.
Only after they were reasonably certain that the danger had passed did they receive orders to treat the injured.
Lian landed near one of the damaged carriages. His Wings of God disappeared behind him, and he walked toward the guards lying on the ground.
One of them was still conscious.
The man gritted his teeth as he tried to endure the pressure on his injured leg. His armor had been torn open around the knee, and blood was flowing down between the metal pieces.
A healer was kneeling beside him, trying to stop the bleeding, but another guard who had been standing near the mages was no longer moving.
The attacker’s projectile had passed directly through a gap in his neck armor. Even the healers’ quick response had not been enough to save him.
Lian looked at the motionless man’s body for several seconds, then turned his gaze toward the remains of the broken defensive structure.
The battle had lasted only a few minutes.
But those few minutes had been enough for one guard to lose his life and several others to suffer serious injuries.
He knew very well that if the Black Vultures had succeeded in capturing the ten selected candidates, the number of victims would probably have been much higher.
However, the failure of their plan did not mean the victory had come without a cost. In another part of the battlefield, Noah was sitting beside an injured guard.
He had placed his metal umbrella on the ground and was helping a healer who was trying to keep the man’s broken arm in place.
"Easy. You don’t need to move it." Noah said gently as he took the medicine container from the healer’s hand.
The guard struggled to breathe.
"I thought... it was over."
Noah gave him a brief smile.
"But you’re still here."
The man wanted to say something, but the pain in his arm made him wince.
Without continuing the conversation, Noah returned the container to the healer and helped the man move into a more suitable position.
After finishing, he looked at his own hands for a moment.
The blood on his fingers had dried, and his smile slowly faded.
He remained silent for a few seconds, then stood up and walked toward the next injured person.
Lian watched the scene from a distance. Over the past few days, he had noticed that Noah was friendly and sociable.
But now, he was seeing another side of his personality. The young Frenchman was not simply trying to get other people’s attention.
Even after the danger had passed, he preferred to help the injured as much as he could.
He glanced briefly at the folded umbrella beside him.
And apparently, he was also a very good fighter.
At the same time, Rindo was examining one of the metal panels left behind by the formation with the escort commander.
Most of the structure had been destroyed, but one section that stored information was still intact, and lines of mana were moving across its surface.
And the names of the ten people were recorded among those lines.
Lian.
Rindo.
Roderick.
And the names of the other seven selected candidates.
Beside each name, there was also information about the academy or guild that person represented.
The escort commander remained silent for a moment, then spoke in a low voice.
"So they really knew who would be inside the convoy beforehand."
"It wasn’t just the names. The movements of this convoy and its members weren’t secret, but look at this." Rindo shook his head and pointed toward another section of the panel.
"Look at the recorded positions."

The commander followed his gaze. Several small markers were displayed beside the names, and they almost perfectly matched the positions assigned to the selected candidates inside the central protected area.
The commander’s expression grew more serious.
Rindo continued.
"They also had information about the convoy’s defensive formation. They knew which area the selected candidates would be moved to when an alert was announced."
"Then the deployment information was leaked."
Rindo paused for a moment.
"That’s highly likely, but we still don’t know how."
The commander nodded. This distinction was important. Someone among the officials responsible for the deployment might have sold the information.
However, the theft of documents, infiltration of communication networks, or indirect access to security procedures were also possible.
Without more evidence, accusing a specific person or organization would not be the right decision.
Lian, who had approached the group, looked at the list for a moment.
Ten names, ten targets, and an operation designed to capture these exact people.
He gave a very faint smile.
"So we’re worth a lot more to some people than I thought."
Of course, this was not particularly surprising.
If the Black Vultures had succeeded in kidnapping even a few of these ten selected candidates, they could have made huge demands of the great families and ancient guilds.
However, from Lian’s point of view, the quality of the plan was a more important issue.
The attackers had not simply taken advantage of the commander’s mistake. In fact, they had counted on him making the right decision.
This made Lian consider the Black Vultures far more dangerous than a group of powerful bandits.
Even so, he still felt that something was wrong. If the Black Vultures wanted to make sure the operation succeeded, they should have sent more than five people.
Why had they sent such a small group? Was their real goal truly what it appeared to be?
At the same time, the investigation team finally reached the fake carriages.
When they brought back their initial report, the commander realized that the scene had been even more carefully planned than he had imagined.
The body of the person who had supposedly been injured beside a wheel did not belong to a living, injured person at all.
It was a human-shaped dummy covered in realistic clothing and fake blood, with limited head and shoulder movements controlled by a hidden mechanism inside the carriage.
From a distance of two hundred meters, it was difficult to tell the difference between it and a real human. However, the dummy’s main purpose was not to trick the guards into approaching.
It was only supposed to look real enough to force the commander to stop and investigate the situation.
And the rest of the scene? It deliberately contained flaws that experienced people could identify.
