Lian looked at him calmly, and the masked man continued.
"We won’t make the same mistake next time."
"Then you’d better make sure there is a next time." The young Vorhelm spoke calmly.
Silence followed for a moment, then the leader turned away without answering, and the five attackers retreated along the rocky paths they had prepared in advance
Lian didn’t pursue them, but that didn’t mean he intended to let them leave alive.
He preferred to keep the abilities of his cores a secret from these bastards.
Black energy of the End appeared at his fingertips, which he shaped into thin lines of light, each line had a corresponding reflection on the body of one of the vultures.
He adjusted them so that the moment they disappeared from sight, they would immediately meet their end.
The energy of the End would erase their existence in an instant, leaving behind no evidence whatsoever.
None of the escort forces were allowed to pursue them without an order, and after checking the injured, the commander decided that securing the convoy had to come before everything else.
The battle was over.
But its consequences were far more serious than a simple victory might suggest.
A few minutes after the Black Vultures retreated, the convoy was still on high alert.
The escort commander did not allow the guards to leave their positions immediately.
First, the scouting teams checked the surrounding high ground.
Then the mages examined the remains of the Inverted Reflection Array to see whether any other active nodes remained.
This was the same formation that had turned the protective enclosures into a prison.
Only after they were reasonably certain that the danger had passed did they receive orders to treat the injured.
Lian landed near one of the damaged carriages.
His Wings of God disappeared behind him, and he walked toward the guards lying on the ground.
One of them was still conscious.
The man gritted his teeth as he tried to endure the pressure on his injured leg.
His armor had been torn open around the knee, and blood was flowing down between the metal pieces.
A healer was kneeling beside him, trying to stop the bleeding, but another guard who had been standing near the mages was no longer moving.
The attacker’s projectile had passed directly through a gap in his neck armor.
Even the healers’ quick response had not been enough to save him.
Lian looked at the motionless man’s body for several seconds, then turned his gaze toward the remains of the broken defensive structure.
The battle had lasted only a few minutes.
But those few minutes had been enough for one guard to lose his life and several others to suffer serious injuries.
He knew very well that if the Black Vultures had succeeded in capturing the ten selected candidates, the number of victims would probably have been much higher.
However, the failure of their plan did not mean the victory had come without a cost.
In another part of the battlefield, Noah was sitting beside an injured guard.
He had placed his metal umbrella on the ground and was helping a healer who was trying to keep the man’s broken arm in place.
"Easy.
You don’t need to move it." Noah said gently as he took the medicine container from the healer’s hand.
The guard struggled to breathe.
"I thought... it was over."
Noah gave him a brief smile.
"But you’re still here."
The man wanted to say something, but the pain in his arm made him wince.
Without continuing the conversation, Noah returned the container to the healer and helped the man move into a more suitable position.
After finishing, he looked at his own hands for a moment.
The blood on his fingers had dried, and his smile slowly faded.
He remained silent for a few seconds, then stood up and walked toward the next injured person.
Lian watched the scene from a distance.
Over the past few days, he had noticed that Noah was friendly and sociable.
But now, he was seeing another side of his personality.
The young Frenchman was not simply trying to get other people’s attention.
Even after the danger had passed, he preferred to help the injured as much as he could.
He glanced briefly at the folded umbrella beside him.
And apparently, he was also a very good fighter.
At the same time, Rindo was examining one of the metal panels left behind by the formation with the escort commander.
Most of the structure had been destroyed, but one section that stored information was still intact, and lines of mana were moving across its surface.
And the names of the ten people were recorded among those lines.
Lian.
Rindo.
Roderick.
And the names of the other seven selected candidates.
Beside each name, there was also information about the academy or guild that person represented.
The escort commander remained silent for a moment, then spoke in a low voice.
"So they really knew who would be inside the convoy beforehand."
"It wasn’t just the names.
The movements of this convoy and its members weren’t secret, but look at this." Rindo shook his head and pointed toward another section of the panel.
"Look at the recorded positions."
The commander followed his gaze.
Several small markers were displayed beside the names, and they almost perfectly matched the positions assigned to the selected candidates inside the central protected area.
The commander’s expression grew more serious.
Rindo continued.
"They also had information about the convoy’s defensive formation.
They knew which area the selected candidates would be moved to when an alert was announced."
"Then the deployment information was leaked."
Rindo paused for a moment.
"That’s highly likely, but we still don’t know how."
The commander nodded.
This distinction was important.
Someone among the officials responsible for the deployment might have sold the information.
However, the theft of documents, infiltration of communication networks, or indirect access to security procedures were also possible.
Without more evidence, accusing a specific person or organization would not be the right decision.
Lian, who had approached the group, looked at the list for a moment.
Ten names, ten targets, and an operation designed to capture these exact people.
He gave a very faint smile.
"So we’re worth a lot more to some people than I thought."
Of course, this was not particularly surprising.
If the Black Vultures had succeeded in kidnapping even a few of these ten selected candidates, they could have made huge demands of the great families and ancient guilds.
However, from Lian’s point of view, the quality of the plan was a more important issue.
The attackers had not simply taken advantage of the commander’s mistake.
In fact, they had counted on him making the right decision.
This made Lian consider the Black Vultures far more dangerous than a group of powerful bandits.
Even so, he still felt that something was wrong.
If the Black Vultures wanted to make sure the operation succeeded, they should have sent more than five people.
Why had they sent such a small group?
Was their real goal truly what it appeared to be?
At the same time, the investigation team finally reached the fake carriages.
When they brought back their initial report, the commander realized that the scene had been even more carefully planned than he had imagined.
The body of the person who had supposedly been injured beside a wheel did not belong to a living, injured person at all.
It was a human-shaped dummy covered in realistic clothing and fake blood, with limited head and shoulder movements controlled by a hidden mechanism inside the carriage.
From a distance of two hundred meters, it was difficult to tell the difference between it and a real human.
However, the dummy’s main purpose was not to trick the guards into approaching.
It was only supposed to look real enough to force the commander to stop and investigate the situation.
And the rest of the scene?
It deliberately contained flaws that experienced people could identify.

chapters.title: Chapter 613: A New Land, A New Danger
paragraphs: Lian stopped smiling as he heard the report, so even those mistakes had been intentional.
The attackers had probably studied similar situations many times before, and they knew that an experienced commander wouldn’t rush forward.
They knew he would gather the Chosen within the central protection zone, and they knew that the main defensive barrier would activate if there was even a small chance of an ambush.
Every step had been predicted in advance, but they had failed to calculate one thing correctly, that one of their intended hostages had the ability to wear down the array’s structure.
After the inspection was over, the escort commander ordered the important remains of the array to be collected for further investigation.
The injured were also moved to the medical carriages.
However, he didn’t immediately order the convoy to continue moving.
A large part of the convoy’s protective equipment needed to be checked again, and some defensive arrays had also been damaged during the attack.
On the other hand, they couldn’t ignore the possibility that another group of Black Vultures might be hiding near their route.
Therefore, the convoy remained in the same area for a while.
The commander sent an urgent report to the responsible centers through his communication device.

In addition to information about the attack, the report also mentioned the possibility that confidential information about the expedition had been leaked, and a short meeting with the escort unit leaders was held afterward.
The conclusion was clear.
The mission would not be canceled.
However, from this moment on, the route and the way the Chosen were protected had to be managed more carefully.
The ten Chosen were also not allowed to leave the convoy’s main area until the necessary checks were completed.
On the fourth night, the camp had a different atmosphere.
Small fires had been lit in different places, but the lively conversations from the first few days were no longer heard.
The guards were patrolling the camp in larger groups.
The protective mages were busy checking replacement equipment, and the healers were also regularly checking the condition of the injured.
Lian was sitting beside one of the carriages, while Roderick was cleaning his sword a little farther away, and Rindo was checking the latest security reports with the escort commander.
Despite their old disagreements, none of the three had allowed personal matters to affect their decisions during the attack.
"Can I sit here?" Noah’s voice came from beside him.
Lian raised his head. The young Frenchman was holding a small container of food, and his folded umbrella was hanging over his shoulder.
"Go ahead."
He sat down beside him.
For a while, both of them silently looked at the fire near one of the carriages.
Then Lian pointed at his umbrella.
"That’s an interesting weapon."
Noah glanced at it and smiled.
"I like it."
"It’s an unusual choice."
"Why? It works in the sun, and it works in the rain."
"And apparently, it works against bandits and monsters, too." The young Vorhelm let out a short laugh.
"That’s one of its uses, too."
Noah placed the food container beside him, picked up the umbrella, and looked at its handle for a few moments before turning back to Lian.
"Do you think it’s strange?"
"What?"
"That I fight with an umbrella."
"More than the weapon itself, I found the way you used it interesting." Lian thought for a moment.
"I’ll take that as a compliment." Noah smiled.
"Have you been training with it for a long time?"
He tilted his head slightly and remained silent for a moment before answering with his usual smile.
"Long enough."
Lian looked at him. It wasn’t a clear answer.
But on the other hand, there was no reason for him to be overly curious about the main weapon or real fighting style of someone he had only recently met.
During the battle, Noah’s stance had seemed a little unusual to him, as if he was used to holding a different kind of weapon.
However, his skill with the umbrella was undeniable.
The young Vorhelm didn’t continue the subject.
The young Frenchman also noticed that he had no intention of asking more questions. He looked at the fire for a moment before speaking.
"Today could have ended much worse."
"Yeah." Lian nodded.
Noah looked at his food container for a few seconds.
"That guard who was standing beside the mages..."
He left the sentence unfinished.
Lian knew who he was talking about, the man who had been killed before the battle had even fully begun.
"He didn’t even get the chance to defend himself." This time, there was no smile on the young Frenchman’s face.
"That was their plan. They wanted to open a path to their target before anyone could react."
Noah nodded.
"I know."
Silence fell between them for a few seconds, and then he looked toward the medical carriages.
"At least we managed to save the others."
"For now."
Noah looked at him, and Lian continued.
"We still have a long way to go, so we’d better stay alert until we reach our destination."
The young Frenchman looked at him for a few moments before giving a small smile.
"I completely agree with that."
He picked up his food container and stood up.
"By the way, we’re leaving early tomorrow morning, so you should get some rest."
"You too."
Noah headed toward the camp’s medical area, and Lian watched him leave for a few seconds.
He’s an interesting guy.
But unlike a few days ago, it wasn’t just his friendly behavior that interested him now. The young man had a high level of combat ability.
And apparently, he was much calmer in dangerous situations than one would expect from his cheerful and outgoing appearance.
On the fifth day, the convoy started moving again.
This time, the defensive formation had changed.
The scouts moved at different distances, and the protective mages were required to check any unknown mana structure before the convoy approached it.
No one was allowed to rely only on the usual procedures, and even when passing through relatively safe areas, the guards watched their surroundings more carefully.
Throughout the day, several reports about possible Black Vultures activity in the region were received, but no direct signs of those five people were found again.
Even so, the organization’s name continued to come up among the convoy members. Some soldiers talked about their past attacks.
Others were worried about how the attackers had managed to obtain confidential information about the expedition.
Lian also thought about this from time to time. In his eyes, the Black Vultures were not simply a group of powerful criminals.
Having the resources to prepare such an array, knowing the protective procedures, and gaining access to information about the ten Chosen showed that a much larger network was behind this operation.
And such a network couldn’t operate for long without powerful financial and intelligence connections.

He turned his gaze toward the plains outside the carriage. Some important people were probably using them, too. He had grown up in a great family that had direct connections to the world’s power structure.
Because of this, he knew better than many ordinary Awakened that some influential people preferred to leave their dirty work to groups that had no official connection to them.
Of course, he had no evidence yet to prove that such people were actually supporting the Black Vultures, but he took the possibility seriously, even considering it almost certain.
"It doesn’t matter for now."
He let out a calm breath.
"If they get in my way again, I’ll deal with them then." However, he kept one possibility in mind.
That the bandits had been sent by his stepmothers.
It was possible.
On the sixth day, the convoy’s route changed.
The rocky roads gave way to smoother paths, and there were more signs of a permanent human presence.
Small watchtowers stood at different distances.
Trade groups joined the main road from side routes, and large convoys sometimes passed them from the opposite direction.
This was one of the newly discovered trade routes in the Ruined Realm. Apparently, several mana crystal mines had been discovered in this area, so the Federation was building roads here.
The convoys they saw were carrying mana crystals.
The seventh day.
Sunlight fell across a vast plain.
But unlike the previous days, the light in the area looked strange.
Lian, who was sitting beside one of the carriage windows, noticed that the light on the horizon looked a little different.
At first, he thought the change was caused by the sun’s position, but when he looked more closely, he realized the light was coming from a direction that had no direct connection to the sun.
Far away, a golden line could be seen on the horizon.
It was thin and almost impossible to notice, but with every minute the convoy moved forward, the line grew larger.
He narrowed his eyes.
What’s that?
A few minutes later, it was no longer possible to mistake it for ordinary light.
The golden line had become a massive surface, one that rose from the ground and stretched beyond the clouds.
At first, only a small part of it could be seen, but when the convoy passed over the last hill, the true sight was revealed.
A massive curtain of golden and white light covered the entire horizon.
Its edges stretched in both directions, reaching so far that the eye couldn’t see where they ended.
The upper part of the curtain also passed through the clouds and disappeared at an unknown height.
Strands of light moved across its surface, sometimes slowly, like waves forming on water, and sometimes in the form of long folds that stretched from the ground to great heights.
But the strangest part of the sight wasn’t the light itself, but what was hidden behind it. No one could see what lay on the other side of the curtain.

No mountains, no forests, no plains, and not even the continuation of the sky could be seen behind it. It was as if a huge part of the Ruined Realm had been separated from the rest of the world, with a curtain of dawn drawn across its border.
The convoy slowly came to a stop.
For a while, no one spoke. Even the sounds made by the monster beasts pulling the carriages seemed insignificant compared to the sight before them.
Then the carriage doors opened, and the ten Chosen stepped outside one after another.
Noah raised his head, and his gaze moved toward the highest part of the curtain.
"This is amazing..."
Roderick was standing some distance away, with his hands behind his back, examining the sight without saying anything unnecessary.
After looking at the curtain, Rindo also turned his attention toward the entrance and the guards stationed around it.
But Lian felt something else.
Thump!
A powerful heartbeat echoed through his soul.
The Heart of Ruin had reacted, and its reaction was extremely powerful, so powerful that it made his entire soul tremble.
Something existed behind that curtain, something the Heart of Ruin wanted.
And this was happening even though they hadn’t crossed the border of the Land of the First Dawn yet.

Lian kept his expression calm. This journey could be more complicated than he had expected. This feeling was so powerful that it reminded him of the time when the Heart of Ruin had encountered the Black Silence.
At that very moment, the escort commander’s voice came from the front of the convoy.
"We’ve arrived."
The ten Chosen turned to look at him.
The man pointed toward the massive curtain in front of them.
"Welcome to the Land of the First Dawn."
The young Vorhelm raised his head.
The curtain’s golden light fell across his face.
Even with all the power he now possessed, he couldn’t tell what was waiting for them on the other side of the light.
However, one truth remained unchanged.
In the Ruined Realm, nothing could be predicted with complete certainty.
Even a seven-day journey that was supposed to take place under military protection had nearly ended in a massive kidnapping.
So, what could happen in a land separated from the rest of the world by such a massive curtain?
He kept his gaze fixed on the golden light.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
Well... let’s see what’s on the other side.

chapters.title: Chapter 614: A Treasury of His Own
paragraphs: Golden light fell across the faces of the ten young Awakened.
In front of them stood a massive curtain of light, whose ends could be seen neither on the ground nor in the sky.

Streams of light descended from unknown heights and moved along the surface of the curtain, sometimes passing slowly by one another, and sometimes meeting at a single point and creating a brighter glow.
Lian raised his head slightly.
Even after several minutes, he still couldn’t tell how tall this structure really was.
The curtain was so vast that it covered a large part of the sky, and no matter how far he looked to either side, he could only see the endless stretch of golden light.
This really is strange.
He had seen teleportation gates, rifts between worlds, and very complex mana structures before, but none of them could compare to what stood in front of him in terms of size.
On the other hand, unlike many powerful structures, he couldn’t feel any threatening pressure coming from the curtain.
Even the mana around it was unusually calm.
"All permits have been approved."
The voice of one of the entrance officials caught everyone’s attention.

A man wearing the official uniform of the Awakened Association stood beside the passage, and after receiving the final confirmation, the ten Chosen were allowed to enter the designated area at the base of the curtain.
Lian briefly looked behind him.
The escort convoy had stopped some distance away, and the guard groups were still checking the remaining supplies and equipment.
Their mission was to safely escort the Chosen to the border of the Land of the First Dawn, from this point onward, the main exploration would begin.

"The map of the explored areas and the restrictions on collecting resources have been provided to you." The entrance official continued after checking the final marks. "As long as you operate within the permitted areas, you can choose your own routes, just make sure to report your location before the end of the day."
Rindo gave a slight nod.
Roderick also moved toward the passage without asking any questions.
Lian gave the curtain one last look before stepping forward with the other Chosen.
At the moment of contact, a gentle warmth settled on his skin.
There was no feeling of falling, no strong transfer pressure, and not even the brief dizziness he sometimes experienced when passing through spatial gates.
There was only pure mana flowing around his body for a moment.
The young Vorhelm took a second step, and streams of golden light passed by his shoulders, covering his vision for a fraction of a second.
But when he took his third step, the scene in front of him had completely changed.
A vast plain covered in tall, green grass stretched toward the slopes of distant hills, a clear river flowed through the grassland, and the golden light in the sky shone on the surface of the water.
Farther away, a forest of tall trees could be seen, their leaves were a bright golden color.
A gentle wind moved through the branches, and the small leaves made a soft sound whenever the wind blew.
White flowers grew among the grass.
Some stones were covered in layers of golden moss, and along the slopes, streams of water flowed down between white rocks.
He stood still for a few seconds, the air here felt noticeably different from the air outside the curtain.
It was neither cold nor hot, the temperature seemed so balanced that he felt comfortable even without using mana.
But the most important difference was not something he could see, the mana in the environment was unusually pure.
Lian took a calm breath.
Even without training, he could feel that absorbing energy naturally and recovering his mana reserves were easier in this environment.
For someone who had spent a long time working in the Ruined Realm, this difference was very noticeable.
He moved his gaze across the river, the water was so clear that he could see the white stones on its bed even from a fairly long distance.
Beside the river, several small birds were searching for food among the grass, but there were no clear signs of attacking monsters.
There were no remains of prey, no trees split open by huge claws, and not even any pressure from the presence of powerful monsters.
Is this really part of the Ruined Realm?
But what caught Lian’s attention more than all the beautiful scenery of the land was something in the sky.
At a great height in the distance, an enormous golden sun was shining, a sun that looked nothing like anything he had seen on Earth or others parts of Ruined realm

Unlike ordinary suns, its center was completely empty, and only a thick ring of golden light shone around the empty space, as if someone had pulled the heart out of the sun and left only its shining shell in the sky.
Thin lines of light moved along the ring, and a golden glow spread around it. Its light covered the entire land, but surprisingly, it did not produce any uncomfortable heat.
However, the longer Lian looked at it, the stranger the feeling inside him became.
That empty space in the center of the sun, surrounded by all that golden light, seemed far too unnatural
It was as if something important had been taken from there, something no one was supposed to realize was missing.
Lian stared at the enormous ring for a few more seconds, then turned his gaze back to the plains ahead.
The Hollow Sun...
They chose a suitable name for it.
He still did not know why, but among all the beauty of this land, the only thing that truly made him feel uneasy was that golden sun.
"Unbelievable..."
Noah’s voice came from the left.
The young Frenchman had placed his folded umbrella over his shoulder and was looking at the scenery with an obvious smile.
"The reports said this place was beautiful, but I didn’t think it would be this different."
Another Chosen nodded when he heard this.
Even Roderick spent longer than usual examining the scenery.
"At least the weather is really nice here." Lian raised the corner of his mouth.
Noah laughed.
"If the treasures are as good as the scenery, I think we have an amazing journey ahead of us."
The young Vorhelm looked toward the golden forest.
"I hope so."
Although unlike Noah, he had something that could answer this question very soon.
After their initial inspection of the area, the Chosen began choosing their own routes.
All ten of them were not supposed to travel as a single group.
The areas near the entrance had been explored many times over the past seven months, and there were relatively safe routes through the plains, springs, and the outer parts of the forest.
Some of the Chosen decided to head toward the recorded ancient sites.
Two others chose the northern springs, while another group planned to check the quality of the area’s mana before moving farther away from the entrance.
Lian preferred not to rush.
He still had no intention of spending valuable exploration time accompanying people whose goals were different from his own.
So after briefly checking the routes, he headed toward one of the low hills.
When he had moved far enough away from the others’ direct line of sight, he stopped beside a white rock and took the Celestial Book of Treasure out of his storage space.
The book’s cover gave off a gentle glow under the golden light of the surroundings.
He opened it.
Then his eyebrows rose slightly.
Several golden points had appeared on the map inside the book.
A considerable number of markers could be seen in different parts of the map.
Some were dim, while others shone more brightly, and a few points were also visible near the edge of the area shown on the map.
He looked at them for a few seconds before smiling.
"Well, well..."
Ever since he had obtained this book, he had used its ability to detect treasures many times.
But he usually had to travel a considerable distance to find a valuable resource.
Here?
Less than an hour had passed since he entered, and several resources had already been marked at relatively short distances.
It seems this place’s reputation is well deserved.
He compared the markers’ positions with the recorded routes in the area, the nearest point was beside one of the river’s branches.
The second marker was near the edge of the golden forest, and the third point was a little farther away, near one of the springs.
He thought about the time for a moment, a large part of the day still remained, and if he chose his routes carefully, he could probably find several valuable treasures before evening.
He closed the book and put it back into storage.
"Well, I’d better start with the nearest one."
The first destination was a shallow branch of the river.
In this area, water flowed between smooth stones, and several short trees with white roots grew along the riverbank.
After arriving, Lian briefly checked his surroundings.
At first glance, there was nothing special, just some green plants, white flowers, and patches of tall grass bending in the wind.
But when he looked at one of the stones near the water, he noticed golden lines among the plants.
He moved closer.

Between two stones, a small plant with narrow leaves was growing, golden lines stretched from the base of its stem to the tips of its leaves, and whenever water flowed past it, a faint light moved across their surfaces.
He knelt beside it.
He checked the information identified by the book.
[Dawnvein Orchid]
[Rank: B]
According to the description, after proper refinement, this plant could increase the quality of mana flow through the body’s channels for a limited time.
Lian examined its leaves for a moment.
Not bad.
Considering that some of his skills consumed a large amount of mana, any resource that could improve the performance of his mana channels was valuable to him.
Besides, selling it or keeping it would both be fine, even though he had considerable wealth, having more wealth was never a bad thing.
On the other hand, having the Celestial Book of Treasure and not trying to build something like the Celestial Treasury that the Vorhelms had would be foolish.
Since he had such a book, he should use it properly and build his own Treasury.
Since he had no plans to return to the Vorhelm Family or join other forces and families, perhaps establishing a major force of his own in the future would not be a bad decision.
And that would be when this Treasury would show its true value.
He carefully moved the soil around the plant aside, three specimens were growing between the stones, one was fully mature, while the other two appeared to be smaller and still growing.
After examining them, he picked all three and placed them in his storage space.

chapters.title: Chapter 615: A Different Kind of Treasure Hunter
paragraphs: The First Treasure.
For someone who had only spent a few minutes exploring this area, it was a very good start.
But Lian had no intention of being satisfied with this much.
The second destination was near one of the golden trees.
This tree was larger than the others, and its white roots extended out of the ground.
He followed the path marked by the book until he reached the northern side of the trunk, where a layer of transparent material had gathered between two roots.
From a distance, it looked more like ordinary tree resin.
But when he got closer, he noticed that very pure energy was flowing inside it, the material slowly glowed under the golden light, and tiny particles were floating in its center.
He examined it for a moment.
This time, he couldn’t identify the material’s exact name and rank, but the book’s reaction showed that it had considerable value.
He carefully examined the part of the material that had separated from the root.
Then he collected a suitable amount of it without causing serious damage to the tree’s main structure.
After closing the container, his gaze remained on the white roots.
The flow of energy inside them was unusual, instead of moving only from the soil into the tree, mana was moving in two directions at certain points.
Lian examined them more carefully for a moment but couldn’t reach any clear conclusion.
Perhaps this was a special feature of the tree species in this area, in any case, he had no good reason to spend more time on it for now.
He stood up and looked toward the golden forest.
If he could find even a few resources of this quality every day, the value of the treasures he collected would probably increase very quickly.
By this point, he had collected six B-rank plants and an A-rank blade that had been lying beside a tree since they entered the area.
But it still wasn’t enough.
Until nearly noon, he explored several more sections along the edge of the forest, some of the book’s markers pointed to resources that required special tools or time to collect.
Lian memorized their locations and passed them by for now, in one area, he also found a plant that didn’t seem to have reached maturity yet.
He decided to leave it alone.
If we stay here for a few more days, it might become more valuable.
His goal wasn’t to collect everything he saw, he wanted to obtain as much value as possible during his limited time here.
And to do that, he had to prioritize his opportunities, as he changed his route toward the next spring, a familiar figure in the distance caught his attention.
A young man with dark hair and a long spear in his hand was standing beside one of the stone paths.
Rindo.
He was examining the area’s map and occasionally looking toward the river.
Lian walked a few steps closer.
"Did you choose this route too?"
Rindo raised his head and gave a slight nod when he saw him.
"There are several important springs along this section, I want to check the connections between the routes and the mana conditions around them."
The young Vorhelm looked at the map.
"I also want to check one of the springs."
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds before closing the map.
"Then our routes are the same for now."
Lian nodded, there was no need for further conversation, and the two of them followed the stone path beside the river.
But they hadn’t walked for more than a few minutes when they heard a girl’s gentle voice from nearby.
"Excuse me... could you please avoid pulling that plant out by its roots for now?
Lian turned toward the voice. Beside the river, a girl with light brown hair was kneeling next to several small plants.
One of the exploration staff members was standing in front of her and seemed to be trying to pull a plant out of the soil.
The girl continued in a polite tone.
"I think it can grow again if the roots are left in place, you can take the upper part and leave the rest untouched."
The staff member looked at the plant for a moment before nodding.
The girl smiled.
"Thank you very much."
Lian watched the scene for a few seconds, then approached with Rindo, when the girl noticed their presence, she immediately stood up and brushed the dirt off her hands.
"Hello."
A friendly smile appeared on her face.
"Are you here to examine the spring too?"
"More or less." Lian nodded.
The girl looked at their clothes for a moment, then seemed to remember something and stood a little straighter.
"Sorry, I forgot to introduce myself, I’m Amélie Moreau, from the French National Academy."
Rindo also introduced himself in his usual calm tone.
"Rindo."
Lian gave a faint smile.
"Lian Vorhelm."
Amélie looked at him for a moment.
"Mr. Vorhelm?"
The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
"Just Lian is fine."
The girl hesitated for a moment before smiling.
"Okay... Lian."
She seemed to have heard his name in the news, but unlike what Lian expected from some people, she didn’t start asking about his ancestral mark or the events in Verendal.
Instead, she pointed toward the plants beside the river.
"I was examining a few types of medicinal plants, I think the springs in this area have some really good resources."
Lian looked at the plants.
"You seem to know them well."
Amélie gave a slightly embarrassed smile.
"A little, there are still many things I need to learn."
But when she explained the differences between two types of plants beside the river, he quickly realized that her "a little" was probably more than she thought.
She not only knew the medicinal properties of the plants, but could also explain their growing conditions, the best time to harvest them, and how water quality affected them.
Lian listened carefully.
She has good knowledge.
After finishing her explanation, Amélie looked between the two of them.
"By the way, which spring are you planning to visit?"
Rindo showed her their approximate destination on the map, and the girl looked surprised for a moment.
"That’s interesting! I was planning to take the same route."
Then, as if she was worried that her suggestion might bother them, she paused for a moment.
"If you don’t mind, maybe we could travel together for a while, of course, if you prefer to be alone, I completely understand."
Lian gave a slight shrug.
"I don’t mind."
Rindo checked the route again.
"We can travel together until the next spring."
Amélie’s face brightened.
"Thank you very much."
She gathered her belongings and put a small bag over her shoulder, then the three of them started moving along the river.
The path beside the river was quiet and smooth.
On the right, clear water flowed between white stones, and on the left, the golden trees gradually grew denser.
The farther they went, the more the light around them changed. The golden leaves reflected some of the light, and small patches of light moved across the ground and the surface of the water.
Amélie spent most of her time examining the plants growing along the path, sometimes she only gave them a quick glance and continued walking.
But whenever she saw an unusual specimen, she stopped for a few moments and examined it more carefully.
Lian noticed that unlike some Awakened who only cared about the rank and market value of resources, she examined even ordinary plants with interest.
Of course, that didn’t mean she ignored the value of the resources.
When they reached a group of blue flowers, the girl examined them briefly before speaking.
"These probably haven’t reached maturity yet, if we harvest them now, the quality of the medicinal material will be much lower."
Lian stood beside her.
"Then we should leave them alone."
Amélie nodded in agreement.
"Yeah, their value might be much higher in a few weeks."
Lian smiled.
At least she thinks logically about their value too.
He looked farther along the path, near one of the river’s bends, a tree with white roots was growing out of the ground.
Beside its roots, several small plants with thick leaves and dark green veins were growing.
He noticed that one of them was filled with a considerable amount of mana, so he approached and sat down beside the plant.
But just as he was about to pull it out of the soil, Amélie’s voice rang out.
"Excuse me, Lian."
He raised his head, and the girl walked a few steps closer.
"Could you please avoid pulling it out by its roots for now?"
Lian looked back at the plant.
"Why?"
Amélie knelt beside him and pointed at several thin strands between the roots.
"This plant is connected to the smaller specimens around it through underground roots, if we pull out the main root completely, the others will probably dry up too."
Lian looked at the smaller plants for a moment.
"But most of the energy is inside the root."
She nodded.
"That’s true, which is why completely harvesting it would be more valuable if you want to use it right away."
The girl paused before continuing in a polite but firm tone.
"But if you only take the upper part, the root can grow again, and maybe the next time someone comes here, there will be several mature specimens."

The farther they went, the more the light around them changed.
The golden leaves reflected some of the light, and small patches of light moved across the ground and the surface of the water.
Amélie spent most of her time examining the plants growing along the path, sometimes she only gave them a quick glance and continued walking.
But whenever she saw an unusual specimen, she stopped for a few moments and examined it more carefully.
Lian noticed that unlike some Awakened who only cared about the rank and market value of resources, she examined even ordinary plants with interest.
Of course, that didn’t mean she ignored the value of the resources.
When they reached a group of blue flowers, the girl examined them briefly before speaking.
"These probably haven’t reached maturity yet, if we harvest them now, the quality of the medicinal material will be much lower."
Lian stood beside her.
"Then we should leave them alone."
Amélie nodded in agreement.
"Yeah, their value might be much higher in a few weeks."
Lian smiled.
At least she thinks logically about their value too.
He looked farther along the path, near one of the river’s bends, a tree with white roots was growing out of the ground.
Beside its roots, several small plants with thick leaves and dark green veins were growing.
He noticed that one of them was filled with a considerable amount of mana, so he approached and sat down beside the plant.
But just as he was about to pull it out of the soil, Amélie’s voice rang out.
"Excuse me, Lian."
He raised his head, and the girl walked a few steps closer.
"Could you please avoid pulling it out by its roots for now?"
Lian looked back at the plant.
"Why?"
Amélie knelt beside him and pointed at several thin strands between the roots.
"This plant is connected to the smaller specimens around it through underground roots, if we pull out the main root completely, the others will probably dry up too."
Lian looked at the smaller plants for a moment.
"But most of the energy is inside the root."
She nodded.
"That’s true, which is why completely harvesting it would be more valuable if you want to use it right away."
The girl paused before continuing in a polite but firm tone.
"But if you only take the upper part, the root can grow again, and maybe the next time someone comes here, there will be several mature specimens."

chapters.title: Chapter 616: A Peaceful Break
paragraphs: Lian looked at her for a few seconds, at first glance, her suggestion seemed to come more from kindness toward the plants.
But when he examined the connected roots again, he realized that it wasn’t only about protecting the environment, if the root network remained intact, the plants could be harvested again.
"Okay."
Lian carefully cut off the upper part of the plant, then looked at the roots to make sure they hadn’t been damaged.
"Thank you very much." Amélie said with a smile.
Lian placed the harvested plant in his storage space.
"Of course, if I come back a few weeks later and find that someone has harvested all of them, it’ll be your fault."
The girl remained silent for a moment, then understood his tone and gave a short laugh.
"In that case, I hope they at least use them properly."
Rindo, who was a few steps ahead and checking the path, glanced at the two of them.
"If you’re done, we should keep moving."
Lian stood up.
"I’m done."
Amélie gathered her belongings and continued walking with them, farther along the path, the river split into two branches.
One branch continued along the forest, while the other passed through a group of white rocks.
Rindo stopped at the crossing for a moment, opened the map of the area, and checked the available routes.
"We can reach the spring about fifteen minutes earlier if we take the right path."
The young Vorhelm looked at the indicated route, the path on the right passed through rocky ground, but the slope wasn’t very steep.
In comparison, the path on the left continued along the river and seemed easier to walk on.
Amélie also examined the map before speaking.
"If we only want to reach the spring, the right path is shorter, but I think the left path would be better for examining plants."
Rindo looked at her.
"Do you have a reason for that?"
The girl pointed toward the river for a moment.
"Most of the medicinal plants we’ve seen so far were growing near water, if this branch has similar conditions, we’ll probably find more specimens."
Lian looked toward the left path, several faint markers from the book were also in that direction, so he agreed without any objections.
"I prefer the left path."
Rindo looked at both of them for a moment before closing the map.
"Then we’ll follow the river, but if the path takes too long, we’ll turn back."
Amélie smiled.
"Okay."
The decision was made.
And contrary to what they might have expected from the girl’s calm appearance, her suggestion not only didn’t waste their time, but also helped them find several interesting resources along the way.
One of these resources was a cluster of white flowers growing between the wet stones.
After examining them, Amélie realized that the plant’s leaves could be used to make a type of healing ointment.
But what caught Lian’s attention was the energy level of one of the clusters.
That specimen contained more mana than the others, and its leaves were also thicker compared to the other specimens.
He carefully harvested the mature cluster and, after examining it, discovered that it was an A-rank plant whose consumption could increase a person’s mana by 30% for five minutes.
Amélie also collected a few leaves from the other specimens.
In the next section of the path, Rindo noticed that the mana flow around the river increased sharply at a certain point.
So all three of them changed their route for a few minutes, and as a result, they found a small crack in one of the rocks, where purer water was flowing out.
Amélie collected a small amount of the water.
Rindo also collected a sample to check its quality.
Seeing this, Lian gave a faint smile.
Not bad.
All three of them had different goals.
But it seemed that these differences helped them notice things they might have overlooked if they had been alone.
In any case, he also collected some of the water, and in the end, he realized that it wasn’t ordinary water, it was mixed with a large amount of mana.
This water could be considered a treasure with a rank of around B, and drinking one bottle could restore about 5% of a person’s mana.
Amélie took only one bottle and refused to take any more, apologizing for stopping them from harvesting some of the plants along the way, she said she didn’t want anything in return.
Lian and Rindo divided the remaining water between themselves, and each of them ended up with around ten bottles.
Each of these bottles could be sold for at least around 500,000 dollars.
In the end, when the sun was getting close to the middle of the sky, they reached a section of the river where the current was calmer.
The golden trees cast soft shadows over the riverbank, and the flat stones beside the water seemed suitable for resting.
After checking the time, Rindo suggested taking a short break.
Amélie also agreed happily.
Lian sat down on one of the stones beside the river, the sound of the water could be heard nearby, and a gentle breeze moved through the golden leaves.
He closed his eyes for a moment.
Over the past few months, he had spent many days fighting, training, or dealing with unknown dangers.
Even the month he had spent in the Dragon Blood River had felt more like torture for his body and mind than rest.
But here? At least for now, there were no enemies.
No monsters, no disasters, and not even a mission that forced him to risk his life every few minutes.
He slowly breathed out, just an ordinary day, without any worries.
At the same time, Amélie took several packages of food out of her storage space and placed them on a clean piece of cloth.
Then she looked between Lian and Rindo.
"If you’d like, you can have some of these, I prepared them before we left."
"Did you make them yourself?" Lian looked at the food, Awakened at their level could go without eating for even a year without having any problems.
She nodded.
"Yes, though they’re very simple."
"They look good."
The girl smiled.
"Thank you."
"Thank you." Rindo thought for a moment, then took one and thanked her.
Amélie nodded with satisfaction, and then all three of them ate in silence for a while.
The silence wasn’t uncomfortable.
On the contrary, after several hours of walking through the forest and examining different resources, taking a short break beside the river felt pleasant.
But after a while, Lian looked at the plant samples beside Amélie, the girl was still examining them from time to time, even while resting, and he finally asked.
"Why are you so interested in medicinal plants?"
She raised her head.
"Me?"
"Yeah. Since I met you, you’ve spent more time looking for things that can be used to make medicine than looking for expensive treasures."
The girl thought for a moment, then carefully placed one of the small specimens inside her bag.
"I think it’s because I’ve always wanted to be able to do something after a battle too."
"After a battle?" Lian looked at her.
Amélie nodded.
"Many Awakened spend all their time trying to become stronger, better skills, more powerful weapons, higher levels... all of these things are important.
She looked toward the river for a moment.
"But when someone gets injured, it doesn’t matter how strong they were before, they might not even be able to move their own body."
Lian said nothing, and she continued.
"I’ve seen several times during training missions that some wounds can heal very quickly with simple treatment, but if no one notices them in time, they can become dangerous."
The girl paused briefly.
"That’s why I thought it might be better to learn things that could be useful in those moments."
He looked at her for a moment, her answer was simple.
But unlike the many idealistic statements he had heard from young people, she didn’t seem to be saying this just to make herself look good.
She was genuinely interested in this.
"And what if you can’t save everyone?"
Amélie remained silent for a few seconds, and her smile faded slightly, she seemed to take the question seriously before answering softly.
"Then I’ll start with someone I can help."
Lian tilted his head slightly.
She continued.

"I know it’s not always possible to save everyone, even the best healers have their limits, sometimes there isn’t enough mana, sometimes the injuries are too severe, and sometimes... we arrive too late."
She curled her fingers against her knee for a moment, but when she raised her head again, her expression was calm and steady.
"But just because I can’t save everyone doesn’t mean I shouldn’t try to help anyone."
For a few moments, the only sound was the flowing water.
Lian kept his gaze on the girl, then gave a faint smile.
"That’s not a bad way of thinking."
Amélie became a little embarrassed.
"Thank you."
But Rindo, who had mostly been listening until then, finally joined the conversation.
"Just don’t forget one thing."
Amélie looked at him.
"What?"
"If you put yourself in a situation where both of you could die just to save one person, without checking the situation first, then you haven’t really saved anyone."
She remained silent for a moment before slowly nodding.
"That’s true."
Rindo continued.
"Sometimes, retreating is also part of saving others, especially when you’re responsible for other people too."
The girl thought about his words for a few seconds before smiling.
"Yes, I still have a lot to learn."
Lian gave Rindo a brief glance, his friend still had the same serious tone, but what he had said wasn’t without reason.
He was the kind of person who took responsibility seriously, even in small situations.
Amélie also seemed to understand this, instead of being upset by Rindo’s warning, she accepted it carefully.
The young Vorhelm looked at both of them for a moment.
An interesting combination.
One was too responsible, while the other was too eager to help others.
And himself? He preferred to know what the result would be before making any decision.
After they finished eating, Amélie began gathering her belongings.
Rindo also stood up and checked the route on the map, it was time to move, they shouldn’t waste even a moment here.

chapters.title: Chapter 617: The Last Stop of the Day
paragraphs: They started moving again after their break.
Along the way, Amélie sometimes talked about the plants she had found, and Rindo gave short and clear answers to questions about the map or the route.
Lian mostly listened, but whenever something caught his attention, he asked questions.
Gradually, she also became more comfortable speaking.
She no longer apologized for every simple sentence, and sometimes, she even gave a short explanation before Lian could ask a question.
This small change interested Lian, he usually paid more attention to people’s abilities and motivations when meeting them for the first time.
But now, he had realized that despite her calm appearance, the young girl was very confident in the things she knew well.
When she talked about harvesting a plant or the quality of water, she didn’t hesitate or try to change her opinion just because of the other person’s social status.
And this quality made her a useful member of the group.
The time was approaching late afternoon.
The golden light on the forest leaves had become stronger, and the shadows of the trees stretched farther along the path.
Over the past few hours, Lian had found several more valuable resources, he had collected some of them and left others for further examination in the coming days.
During this time, he had managed to find and collect two A-rank resources, three B-rank resources, and one C-rank resource.
He had also left several others behind because their value was too low in comparison.
But just as he was about to suggest returning, he felt a very slight vibration from the Celestial Book of Treasure.
He slowed his steps for a moment.
While Rindo was busy checking the map and Amélie was looking at a plant beside the path, he secretly checked the book’s information.
A golden point had appeared farther away from the other markers, its glow was much stronger than that of the resources he had collected throughout the day.
He looked at its location for a few seconds.
What is this one?
The point was near one of the area’s recorded springs, a spring that, according to the map, was located along the southern edge of the golden forest.
He hid the book again and then looked at Rindo.
"There’s another spring nearby, right?"
Rindo raised his head.
"Which one?"
Lian pointed in the general direction of the destination.
Rindo checked the map.
"About twenty minutes away."
Lian nodded.
"Not bad, we can take a look before returning."
Rindo looked at the sun’s position for a moment.
"There isn’t much time left before the end of the day."
"We can keep the inspection short."
Rindo thought about the route for a few seconds, and before he could answer, Amélie, who had heard their conversation, came closer.
"Excuse me, are you talking about the southern spring?"
Lian nodded, and the girl became excited for a moment.
"I think a rare type of medicinal plant grows there, it was mentioned in some old reports about this area."
Then she continued with some hesitation.
"Of course, I’m not sure if any are still there, but if we have time, I’d like to see it too."
Rindo looked between the two of them and then closed the map.
"Thirty minutes to inspect the area, then we’ll head straight back."
"Deal." In the end, even if his friend hadn’t agreed, he would have gone alone.
"Thank you very much." Amélie also nodded happily.
And the three of them headed toward the last spring they would visit that day, the route to the southern spring passed through a less crowded part of the forest.

The trees in this area stood farther apart, and their white roots extended out of the ground in some places. Unlike the paths beside the river, the ground was drier, and only a narrow stream flowed between the rocks.
Along the way, Lian paid attention to the changes in the mana quality around him.
The energy was still pure, but its concentration was higher near certain rocks, he looked at one of the moss-covered stones for a moment.
Strange, it seems the mana flow moves a little differently here.
Of course, the difference wasn’t great enough to immediately suggest danger.
Throughout the day, he had also come across several small areas where more energy flowed because of the plants or materials growing there.
So he simply memorized the location and continued moving.
A while later, the faint sound of flowing water reached their ears.
Amélie raised her head.
"I think we’ve arrived."
They passed between two golden trees, and the small spring appeared in front of them, but the scene was different from what they had seen at the previous springs.
Most of its bed had dried up.
White stones lay among the cracked soil, and only a narrow stream of water flowed past an old pillar.
Along the dried-up bed, white roots could be seen, some of which were still moist.
But many of the plants around them had lost their natural color.
Lian walked a few steps forward and fixed his gaze on the central pillar.
The pillar was almost two meters tall, but its upper part was broken. Golden moss had grown over the lower sections, and several old cracks could be seen along its surface.
What caught his attention the most was a mark carved near the highest intact part of the pillar.
It was a simple circle, but its center was empty.
He raised his head slightly.
The unusual sun of this land was still shining in the sky, a golden ring with an empty center.
The resemblance was clear.
Rindo had noticed it too.
"It’s the same mark as the one we see in the sky."
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
For a few seconds, both of them looked at the pillar, Rindo ran his fingertips along one of the old cracks.
"This pillar is probably connected to the history of this land."
"That’s possible." The young Vorhelm replied.
He still knew nothing about the true origin of the Hollow Sun.
Although it was strange that the sun in the sky was hollow, they had heard about it before and hadn’t paid much attention to it, besides, this entire land was strange.
But the fact that the same mark appeared on an old pillar suggested that the shape of the sun had probably held special meaning for the people who once lived here or built this place.
However, he couldn’t draw any further conclusions based on this resemblance alone.
At the same time, Amélie was kneeling beside the spring’s bed, the girl carefully examined one of the withered plants and then moved aside several strands of the white roots around it.
"These are still alive."
"Are you sure?" Lian looked at her.
She nodded.
"Yes. The roots are still absorbing energy, but it seems they aren’t getting enough water."
She followed the narrow stream of water for a few moments and then pointed toward the area behind the pillar.
"I think the main flow comes from that side, something might be blocking its path."
Rindo also came closer, he looked at the stones around the pillar for a few seconds.
"We should check the situation before moving anything."
Amélie immediately nodded.
"That’s right."
Lian also agreed, he wasn’t in a hurry.
Although the Celestial Book of Treasure showed that a valuable resource was located near this very pillar, he still didn’t know exactly what it was.
And if collecting it required him to tamper with part of the old structure, he preferred to check the possible dangers first.
Rindo also took his spear from his back.
But instead of striking the stones, he held its tip a short distance above the spring’s bed and released a small amount of mana.
The flow of energy moved along the stone’s surface and then spread among several white roots.
He carefully examined the reaction, in most areas, the mana flowed without any obstacles, but near the base of the pillar, a small amount of energy gathered and struggled to continue along its path.
"Here."
He pointed at a large stone trapped between two roots.
Lian walked closer, the stone was behind the pillar, and its lower part was buried in the soil.
From the condition of the surrounding area, it was clear that the stone had remained in the same position for a long time.
Amélie also came closer and examined the paths of the roots.
"If we remove this stone, the water will probably start flowing again."
Rindo nodded.
"Possibly, but we mustn’t put pressure on the pillar itself."
The young Vorhelm kept his gaze on the stone and then activated True Sequence.
The energy flows around him became clearer.
Several thin mana paths ran along the white roots, and some of them extended deep underground.
Near the large stone, these paths collided with one another, making their flow unstable.
But the structure continued deep underground, and he couldn’t see where it ended, he frowned slightly for a moment.
The structure was very complex.
And that didn’t make sense, was such a complex structure really necessary to stop the water from flowing? Or could it have another purpose...?

The point was near one of the area’s recorded springs, a spring that, according to the map, was located along the southern edge of the golden forest.
He hid the book again and then looked at Rindo.
"There’s another spring nearby, right?"
Rindo raised his head.
"Which one?"
Lian pointed in the general direction of the destination.
Rindo checked the map.
"About twenty minutes away."
Lian nodded.
"Not bad, we can take a look before returning."
Rindo looked at the sun’s position for a moment.
"There isn’t much time left before the end of the day."
"We can keep the inspection short."
Rindo thought about the route for a few seconds, and before he could answer, Amélie, who had heard their conversation, came closer.
"Excuse me, are you talking about the southern spring?"
Lian nodded, and the girl became excited for a moment.
"I think a rare type of medicinal plant grows there, it was mentioned in some old reports about this area."
Then she continued with some hesitation.
"Of course, I’m not sure if any are still there, but if we have time, I’d like to see it too."
Rindo looked between the two of them and then closed the map.
"Thirty minutes to inspect the area, then we’ll head straight back."
"Deal." In the end, even if his friend hadn’t agreed, he would have gone alone.
"Thank you very much." Amélie also nodded happily.
And the three of them headed toward the last spring they would visit that day, the route to the southern spring passed through a less crowded part of the forest.
The trees in this area stood farther apart, and their white roots extended out of the ground in some places.
Unlike the paths beside the river, the ground was drier, and only a narrow stream flowed between the rocks.
Along the way, Lian paid attention to the changes in the mana quality around him.
The energy was still pure, but its concentration was higher near certain rocks, he looked at one of the moss-covered stones for a moment.
Strange, it seems the mana flow moves a little differently here.
Of course, the difference wasn’t great enough to immediately suggest danger.
Throughout the day, he had also come across several small areas where more energy flowed because of the plants or materials growing there.
So he simply memorized the location and continued moving.
A while later, the faint sound of flowing water reached their ears.
Amélie raised her head.
"I think we’ve arrived."
They passed between two golden trees, and the small spring appeared in front of them, but the scene was different from what they had seen at the previous springs.
Most of its bed had dried up.
White stones lay among the cracked soil, and only a narrow stream of water flowed past an old pillar.
Along the dried-up bed, white roots could be seen, some of which were still moist.
But many of the plants around them had lost their natural color.
Lian walked a few steps forward and fixed his gaze on the central pillar.
The pillar was almost two meters tall, but its upper part was broken.
Golden moss had grown over the lower sections, and several old cracks could be seen along its surface.
What caught his attention the most was a mark carved near the highest intact part of the pillar.
It was a simple circle, but its center was empty.
He raised his head slightly.
The unusual sun of this land was still shining in the sky, a golden ring with an empty center.
The resemblance was clear.
Rindo had noticed it too.
"It’s the same mark as the one we see in the sky."
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
For a few seconds, both of them looked at the pillar, Rindo ran his fingertips along one of the old cracks.
"This pillar is probably connected to the history of this land."
"That’s possible." The young Vorhelm replied.
He still knew nothing about the true origin of the Hollow Sun.
Although it was strange that the sun in the sky was hollow, they had heard about it before and hadn’t paid much attention to it, besides, this entire land was strange.
But the fact that the same mark appeared on an old pillar suggested that the shape of the sun had probably held special meaning for the people who once lived here or built this place.
However, he couldn’t draw any further conclusions based on this resemblance alone.
At the same time, Amélie was kneeling beside the spring’s bed, the girl carefully examined one of the withered plants and then moved aside several strands of the white roots around it.
"These are still alive."
"Are you sure?" Lian looked at her.
She nodded.
"Yes.
The roots are still absorbing energy, but it seems they aren’t getting enough water."
She followed the narrow stream of water for a few moments and then pointed toward the area behind the pillar.
"I think the main flow comes from that side, something might be blocking its path."
Rindo also came closer, he looked at the stones around the pillar for a few seconds.
"We should check the situation before moving anything."
Amélie immediately nodded.
"That’s right."
Lian also agreed, he wasn’t in a hurry.
Although the Celestial Book of Treasure showed that a valuable resource was located near this very pillar, he still didn’t know exactly what it was.
And if collecting it required him to tamper with part of the old structure, he preferred to check the possible dangers first.
Rindo also took his spear from his back.
But instead of striking the stones, he held its tip a short distance above the spring’s bed and released a small amount of mana.
The flow of energy moved along the stone’s surface and then spread among several white roots.
He carefully examined the reaction, in most areas, the mana flowed without any obstacles, but near the base of the pillar, a small amount of energy gathered and struggled to continue along its path.
"Here."
He pointed at a large stone trapped between two roots.
Lian walked closer, the stone was behind the pillar, and its lower part was buried in the soil.
From the condition of the surrounding area, it was clear that the stone had remained in the same position for a long time.
Amélie also came closer and examined the paths of the roots.
"If we remove this stone, the water will probably start flowing again."
Rindo nodded.
"Possibly, but we mustn’t put pressure on the pillar itself."
The young Vorhelm kept his gaze on the stone and then activated True Sequence.
The energy flows around him became clearer.
Several thin mana paths ran along the white roots, and some of them extended deep underground.
Near the large stone, these paths collided with one another, making their flow unstable.
But the structure continued deep underground, and he couldn’t see where it ended, he frowned slightly for a moment.
The structure was very complex.
And that didn’t make sense, was such a complex structure really necessary to stop the water from flowing?
Or could it have another purpose...?

chapters.title: Chapter 618: The Core of a Fallen Star ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: However, complexity alone did not mean something was dangerous.
Some plants and cultivated springs also had very advanced mana structures.
More importantly, there were no clear signs of an offensive array or an active defensive mechanism.
Lian looked at Rindo.
"I think if we just move the stone, the water will flow again."
Rindo examined the structure around them for a few seconds before replying.
"As long as we don’t damage the pillar or the main roots, there probably won’t be a problem."
Hearing this, Amélie looked at the withered plants.
"I can hold the roots aside so they won’t get damaged while we move the stone."
Lian nodded.
"Good."
All three of them got to work. The task was not very difficult, but it required more care than they had first expected.
Rindo used the tip of his spear to loosen some of the smaller stones around them.
Amélie carefully held the white roots aside and informed Lian whenever she felt that too much pressure was being placed on them.
Lian moved the larger stones without striking the pillar directly.
His current physical strength was so great that even stones weighing several hundred kilograms were not much of a problem for him.
But strength was not the issue here.
He had to make sure that the roots did not break when he removed the stone and that no extra pressure was placed on the pillar.
So he worked more carefully.
After a few minutes, a small passage opened behind the pillar, and the sound of flowing water grew slightly louder.
Seeing this, Amélie smiled.
"I think we’re making progress."
Rindo looked at the flow of mana.
"The main stone is still there."
Lian nodded. The large stone was trapped between two roots, so he placed his hands beneath its edge and slowly applied force.
The stone moved a few centimeters.
Rindo immediately checked the direction of the pressure.
"A little to the right, if you pull it straight up, you’ll put pressure on the root behind it."
The young Vorhelm changed the direction of his movement, while Amélie held the roots aside.
Finally, the stone came free from the ground.
Lian placed it a little farther away, and almost immediately, the sound of flowing water grew louder.
The thin stream that had previously struggled to pass by the pillar now flowed freely between the stones.
However, something else caught his attention, at the spot where the large stone had been, he noticed a small object among the golden-colored deposits.
Its surface was glowing faintly.
Found you.

The object was about the size of his palm and had an irregular shape, it seemed to be made of an extremely dense material, but its outer surface was so smooth that it was difficult to identify what it was.
He did not pick it up immediately.
First, he checked the flow of mana around it once more, but there were no obvious signs of a dangerous mechanism activating.
The energy inside the object was also calm and stable, so he took it out from among the deposits, feeling its weight in his hand for a moment.
It was much heavier than he had expected from its size.
[ Core of the Fallen Star ]
[ Rank: S ]
[ Description: The user can manipulate gravity within a specific area. ]
[ Increasing gravity presses enemies against the ground and slows their movements. ]
[ Decreasing gravity increases the user’s jumping ability and mobility.
Changing the direction of gravity allows the user to walk on walls or change the direction of their fall. ]
[ The treasure’s limits are determined by the user’s power, with enough mana, the gravity of an entire world can be completely destroyed or manipulated at will. ]
’Oh?’ His eyes lit up with surprise.
This was his greatest find of the day, an S-rank treasure that granted the power to control gravity.
And with enough mana, he could even manipulate the gravity of an entire world? Although he knew this place was called the Paradise of Treasures, an artifact with such power was still a surprise.
He placed the object in his storage space and then looked at the spring again.
The water was flowing faster past the pillar.
At first, only a small part of the dried-up ground became wet.
But a few moments later, the water returned to its old path and spread between the white stones.
Amélie happily knelt beside one of the plants, faint golden lines were moving along its roots.
The leaves that had been withered just a few minutes ago slowly began to return to their normal state.
"We did it!"
The girl’s voice was so happy that Lian instinctively looked at her.
She was looking at the spring with a clear smile on her face.
It seemed that finding a few healthy plants made her just as happy as finding an expensive treasure made Lian.
Rindo also checked the flow of mana and nodded after a few seconds.
"It seems stable for now."
The young Vorhelm brushed the dust off his hands.
"Then we’re done here."
Amélie raised her head.
"Thank you so much, if this spring starts flowing again, maybe this part of the forest will become as green as the other areas in a while."
Lian looked at the plants around them.
"I hope so." He was also satisfied with the result.
He had found a valuable treasure, and they had also managed to clear the water’s path without damaging the pillar.
Overall, it was a good result for their last destination of the day.
As he examined the surroundings, his eyes fell on Rindo.
"I think we still have a few minutes."
"Ten minutes, then we have to return." Rindo looked at the position of the sun.
Lian nodded, he had also obtained what he wanted and had no reason to stay here any longer, especially since the book was no longer showing any other artifacts in this area.
Amélie was also happily examining the plants that had regained access to the water, the girl found several mature specimens and carefully collected parts of them.
However, as she had said earlier, she left the main roots untouched, when she finished, she divided several samples among three small containers.
Then she held one out to Lian.
"This is for you."
Lian looked at her.
"What for?"
"You helped too, I think we should share the things we found here."
He looked at the plant sample for a moment.
"You don’t have to, you know more about its uses than we do."
She shook her head slightly.
"But what if you need it later?"
She gave a small smile.
"Besides, you said we shouldn’t waste valuable resources."
Lian looked at her for a few seconds before laughing.
"Well, it seems you remember my words quite well."
He accepted it and thanked her.
"Thanks."
She nodded with satisfaction and then gave another sample to Rindo.
Rindo also accepted it after a brief inspection and placed it in his storage space. At the same time, the girl happily began explaining the plant’s possible uses.
"If I can properly study its structure, maybe I can use it to make a better healing medicine, although I’m still not sure how it will react with ordinary materials.
"Even so, the plant itself is a B-rank medicinal plant, as long as you don’t have any fatal injuries, it can heal you, if I work on it a little, maybe I can turn it into an A-rank one."
"Then you’ll be quite busy once you return to France." Lian looked at her.
Amélie smiled.
"I hope so."
She looked at the spring for a moment before continuing in a calmer voice.
"To be honest, I’m glad I joined you two today."
"Why?"

"Well... I thought most of the Chosen would only care about competing with each other, especially after I found out that some of them came from very powerful families or ancient guilds." She looked a little embarrassed.
She glanced briefly at Lian.
"But I learned a lot today, both about resources and about examining the surroundings."
Then she looked at Rindo.
"And also that it’s better to examine the situation more carefully before making a decision."
"You also had useful information." Rindo remained silent for a moment before replying.
Amélie seemed not to have expected such a response and looked surprised for a moment, then a warm smile appeared on her face.
"Thank you."
"If you find any interesting samples tomorrow, let me know." Lian looked at the plants beside the spring, after all, he was not going to travel with them tomorrow.
There were several areas where he suspected he might find other S-rank treasures, and he planned to go there.
"Of course." Amélie immediately nodded, then she thought for a moment before continuing.
"Maybe we can also examine some of the other springs, I think if we choose the right routes, we can find some really good resources."
"That’s not a bad idea." Lian gave a faint smile.
Rindo also nodded without any objections, apparently, he thought their journey together today had produced acceptable results.
For a few moments, all three of them prepared to return.
Lian was thinking about the treasures that were still marked on the book’s map, Rindo wanted to compare today’s information with the maps of other areas.
And Amélie was apparently already making plans to examine the plants tomorrow.
None of them were in a hurry.
The day was almost over, and everything had gone well.
At least, until now.
Amélie was the first to notice the change.
The girl was kneeling beside the spring and gathering her remaining belongings when her gaze became fixed on the flow of water.
For a moment, she slightly furrowed her brows.
"That’s strange..."
Lian turned his head.
"What happened?"
"I think the flow has weakened again." Amélie pointed at the water.
Lian moved closer, the water was still flowing past the pillar, but its speed had decreased slightly compared to a few minutes ago.
He examined the path for a moment.
Rindo also came closer, his eyes fixed on the stones in the streambed.
"The pressure has changed."
The young Vorhelm raised his head.
"How much?"
"Not much, but part of the flow has also changed direction." Rindo stood beside the pillar and examined the surroundings more carefully.
Lian also activated True Sequence.
For a few seconds, the mana lines around the spring appeared before his eyes, at first, there seemed to be nothing important about the change.
But when he followed the underground paths, he noticed that some of the energy was flowing deeper into the ground instead of moving along the roots.
What is this? He was still examining it when a familiar sound came from among the trees and interrupted him.
The singing of birds.
