chapters.title: Chapter 619: The Hollow Sun ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian raised his head for a moment.
A few minutes ago, the sounds of small birds could be heard throughout the forest, but now there was no sound at all.
Even the birds sitting on the branches farther away had fallen silent.
Amélie noticed it as well.
"Why has it become so quiet?"
Rindo did not answer, he took his eyes off the pillar and looked at the surrounding trees.
The wind was still blowing.
Lian could feel the air moving across his face, but the golden leaves on the trees were no longer moving.
Not even a single leaf.
It was as if the entire forest had stopped in the middle of a moment.
He slowly stood up and looked at the sky.
The Hollow Sun was still high in the distance, the same enormous golden ring with an empty center.
But something about its light had changed, the glow inside the ring weakened for a moment, and then an extremely thin line of light moved along its edge.
He narrowed his eyes slightly.
Wait...
Something was taking shape in the empty center of the sun, at first, only a dark line could be seen.
Thin and vertical.
But the line slowly grew wider, and its edges moved apart, revealing a black structure inside the golden ring.
Rindo also raised his head, his hand remained on his weapon.
"What... is that?" Amélie looked at the sky in disbelief.
Neither of them had a clear answer, because at that very moment, the black line in the center of the sun opened, and something resembling an enormous pupil appeared within the golden light.
The Hollow Sun had turned into a giant eye.
The golden rings around it moved slowly.
Lines of light flowed along their surfaces, and the black pupil was so large that it could be clearly seen even from a great distance.
Lian remained motionless for several seconds, he had faced many powerful beings before.
He had even experienced the pressure of the presence of the Demon of End, but what he felt now was completely different.
It was neither anger, a thirst for blood, nor even the direct threat of a hunter, instead, it was the feeling of being watched by something that seemed to have control over everything around it.
He felt as if he were under the gaze of an indescribable being, something beyond his understanding.
An entity that seemed to have existed since the beginning of creation and possessed the power to judge everything.
It was as if all of existence, from the smallest particle to the largest star, meant nothing before its gaze, and there was only one thing expected of it.
To deliver the final judgment!
At that very moment, a voice spread throughout the land, a voice that came from no specific direction and did not need to be loud.
It was as if they could hear it directly inside their minds.
"The Judgment System has been taken out of suspension."
Lian frowned.
Judgment?
Rindo took his spear from his back.
Meanwhile, Amélie was still staring at the sky in disbelief.
A few seconds passed, and then the same voice was heard again.
"Unregistered presences have been detected."
The golden rings of the sun rotated slightly, and then a narrow beam of light appeared on the ground in front of Amélie.
She instinctively took a step back.
"What...?"
The golden light moved with her, and the girl stopped, looking down at the ground, but the beam was no longer limited to the stones in front of her and slowly began to spread around her body.
Rindo immediately moved his spear forward.
"Amélie, get out of the light!"
The girl took several steps to the left without hesitation, but the light continued to follow her, she quickly stepped back for a moment, but the same thing happened again.
It was as if the beam was no longer connected to a specific spot on the ground, but was directly connected to her.
Lian narrowed his eyes, and at that moment, the sun’s emotionless voice sounded again.
"Suspect identified."
It paused briefly.
"Identity: Amélie Moreau."
Amélie froze.
She had heard her own name.
For several seconds, she only stared at the sky, then she asked in a trembling voice,
She received no answer, instead, the golden light around her body became denser.
Lian took a step forward.
"Rindo, watch our surroundings."
His friend gave a small nod, he had also realized that what was happening before them was different from an ordinary skill.
But neither of them knew what the light was actually meant to do.
Then the voice continued.
"First charge: Unauthorized entry into the domain of the condemned."
Amélie blinked.
The domain of the condemned?
"Second charge: Participation in the tampering with the containment structure."
Rindo looked at the old pillar and then looked at her again.
But before he had a chance to examine the connection between these two things, the third charge was announced.
"Third charge: Taking property belonging to the Mother."
She remained motionless for several seconds, the words she was hearing made no sense to her.
She had only collected medicinal plants and tried to reopen the path of a spring with two other people.
She had not seen anyone who was imprisoned, had not heard of any law that forbade entry, and did not even know that something called the Mother existed in this land.
Her hands slowly began to tremble.
"I’m... sorry."
She looked up at the sky.
"I really didn’t know, if I did something I wasn’t supposed to do, I can make up for it."
But the sun’s black pupil showed no reaction.
"Amélie, calm down, we still don’t know how this system works." Rindo said in a firm voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 620: Mother And Father?
paragraphs: The sound of flowing water could still be heard among the white stones.
The spring, which had almost dried up just a few minutes ago, was now flowing calmly past the old pillar.
The white roots were absorbing moisture again, and the withered plants along the riverbed were slowly returning to their natural color.
Everything was just as it had been before the Hollow Sun awakened.
There was only one difference.
Amélie Moreau was no longer there.

Lian slowly lowered his right hand, the last strands of golden light had disappeared between his fingers, and not even a trace of the energy that had surrounded the girl’s body and soul a few moments ago remained.
He stared at the spot where Amélie had been standing for a while.
There was no body, no blood had been spilled on the stones, and there wasn’t even a bit of ash to show that someone had lost their life here.
All of the girl’s belongings had been stored in her personal storage space, and with her destruction, no items had been left in the area.
If someone arrived here a few minutes later, they would probably never guess what had happened.
A short distance away, Rindo was also standing still.

His spear was still in his right hand, and the fingers of that hand were still a little numb after their brief contact with the power of Judgment, he opened and closed his fingers several times, but his gaze never left the place where the girl had died.
Neither of them spoke.
Even after all the deadly battles they had been through, witnessing her death was different from most things they had seen until that day.
No enemy had attacked her, she hadn’t had a chance to fight, and she hadn’t even known which law she had broken.
A voice from the sky had simply announced her name, and a few moments later, her existence had disappeared.
Finally, Rindo lowered his spear.
"Lian."
The young Vorhelm turned his head slightly.
"Hmm?"
"Is there no trace of her left?"
Without answering immediately, he activated True Sequence again.

The Mana flows around the spring appeared before his perception, the energy in the white roots, the gentle movement of the water, and the weak Mana remains he had released while trying to interrupt the Judgment were still detectable.
But at the place where she had been executed? There was no life energy, and no structure remained.
Even the golden connections of the Judgment had disappeared so completely that examining their traces seemed almost impossible.
He deactivated the skill after a few seconds.
"No, there’s nothing left to recover, even most of the energy used to carry out the Judgment has disappeared."
Rindo lowered his gaze, looking at the wet stones in front of him for a few moments.
Then he slowly breathed out and returned his spear to its normal position.
"I see."
Silence settled between them again, and Lian turned his gaze toward the spring.
He could still remember Amélie’s happy smile, when she had knelt beside the plants after the water started flowing again and excitedly talked about making better medicine.
She had even made plans for the next day, they were supposed to collect more samples and perhaps examine a few other springs.
But all those plans had disappeared within a few seconds.
He slowly breathed out.
What a ridiculous death.
He didn’t mean that the girl’s death was unimportant, on the contrary, what made the situation even more disturbing was how meaningless it seemed from a human point of view.
Amélie hadn’t intended to hurt anyone, and she hadn’t even entered the area to obtain a forbidden treasure.
Yet an unknown being in the sky had accused her of crimes that she couldn’t understand.
Then it had carried out the Judgment without giving her the slightest chance to defend herself.
Lian raised his head again, the Hollow Sun was still high above the land, far away in the sky.
But it no longer looked like the beautiful sun from a few hours ago.
The huge golden rings around its center were moving slowly, and a large, completely open black pupil was in the middle of them.
However, there was no sign that the Hollow Sun was paying direct attention to Lian or Rindo.
It was as if they no longer mattered to it after the Judgment had been carried out.
At least for now.
Lian looked away from the sky, he still didn’t know exactly what the Hollow Sun was.
It wasn’t even clear whether he should consider it a living being, an ancient structure, or some kind of enormous system.
But its behavior had revealed several clear abilities, it could identify people.
It announced specific accusations and activated a power after issuing a Judgment, a power that could directly affect the target’s body and soul.
This behavior was unlike an ordinary monster attack, it was more like a system that had been set up in advance.
He remembered the words he had heard during the trial.
"Unauthorized entry into the domain of the condemned."
"Participation in tampering with the containment structure."
And the third accusation.
"Taking property belonging to the Mother."
He slightly furrowed his brows.
Mother? This word had caught his attention from the moment the accusation was announced.
The first two accusations referred to specific actions, but the third was about ownership.
If the Mother referred to a specific person or being, why was such a title used in the Judgment system? Did it refer to a being that owned this land?
Or perhaps it was a title given to the ones who had created the structure?
He even remembered the "Father", the being that had created the Five Calamities, could there be some kind of connection between them?
Mother and Father?
Lian still didn’t have enough information to answer, but he decided to remember these words.
There was another question.
Why Amélie?
All three of them had been in the same place, all three had entered the Land of the First Dawn, and all three had taken part in examining and reopening the spring’s water flow.
He had even personally taken the Core of the Fallen Star from beneath the pillar.
In terms of collecting resources, he had obtained far more treasures than Amélie or anyone else.
Yet the Hollow Sun hadn’t paid any attention to him, instead, it had chosen that girl as its first target.
So either the Judgment’s criteria went beyond these accusations, or the order in which people were selected followed another rule.
Perhaps the Hollow Sun was examining everyone present one by one.
Perhaps the severity of the accusations mattered, or perhaps certain actions caused someone to be given a higher priority.
Or perhaps the way this structure understood sin and crime was completely different from the way humans understood them.
In any case, one thing was clear.
If that same light ever chose Lian as its target, he still had no reliable way to stop it, and this matter was far more important than any other question.
Rindo noticed his long silence and looked at him.
"What are you thinking about?"
Lian placed his hands behind his back.
"Why it chose only her."
Rindo remained silent for a few seconds, then turned his gaze toward the stone pillar.
"Do you think it has something to do with this spring?"
"Maybe, but not necessarily in the way it seems."
The young Vorhelm walked toward the pillar.
"The Hollow Sun awakened around the same time the energy flow here changed, but that only shows that there might be a connection between the two events, not that we know the exact cause."
Rindo nodded.
"That’s true."
Lian continued.
"Besides, this area has been explored for seven months, it’s unlikely that we’re the first people to examine a spring or take something from beside an old pillar."
The student council president kept his gaze on the engraved symbol.
"Then we need to find out what made this one different from the others."
"Exactly."
The young Vorhelm activated True Sequence again, this time focusing more on the pillar and the white roots around it.
The Mana flow had changed compared to how it had been before the Hollow Sun awakened, previously, a large part of the energy had moved along the roots and spread among the plants and the springbed.
But now? Some of that energy was moving deep underground through narrow paths.
He tried to follow the flow, the paths passed beneath the base of the pillar and disappeared at a depth beyond the range of his perception.
However, another small difference caught his attention.
In some places, the golden moss around the Hollow Sun symbol had lost its color.
He moved his fingertips close to the surface of the pillar, but didn’t touch the symbol, before the awakening, energy had flowed outward from this place. Now, some of it was flowing downward.
This difference might be important.
Especially when he remembered the white roots and the two-way Mana flows he had seen near the golden trees that morning.
Could these two phenomena be connected?
Perhaps.
But he couldn’t understand the structure of the entire land from a pillar and a few roots.
He memorized the pillar’s location and condition, he could return here when he had the chance and compare his observations with similar places.
Of course, that was only if he still had the chance to do so by then.
At that moment, the brightness of the surroundings changed for a few seconds.
Lian raised his head.
The Hollow Sun’s outer ring had turned slightly, and the black pupil in its center was slowly moving from one part of the sky to another.
It seemed to be examining the entire land.
Rindo also noticed the change, and his hand moved toward his spear.
That strange sun was doing something again.
( Scene Visualization )

The student council president kept his gaze on the engraved symbol.
"Then we need to find out what made this one different from the others."
"Exactly."
The young Vorhelm activated True Sequence again, this time focusing more on the pillar and the white roots around it.
The Mana flow had changed compared to how it had been before the Hollow Sun awakened, previously, a large part of the energy had moved along the roots and spread among the plants and the springbed.
But now?
Some of that energy was moving deep underground through narrow paths.
He tried to follow the flow, the paths passed beneath the base of the pillar and disappeared at a depth beyond the range of his perception.
However, another small difference caught his attention.
In some places, the golden moss around the Hollow Sun symbol had lost its color.
He moved his fingertips close to the surface of the pillar, but didn’t touch the symbol, before the awakening, energy had flowed outward from this place.
Now, some of it was flowing downward.
This difference might be important.
Especially when he remembered the white roots and the two-way Mana flows he had seen near the golden trees that morning.
Could these two phenomena be connected?
Perhaps.
But he couldn’t understand the structure of the entire land from a pillar and a few roots.
He memorized the pillar’s location and condition, he could return here when he had the chance and compare his observations with similar places.
Of course, that was only if he still had the chance to do so by then.
At that moment, the brightness of the surroundings changed for a few seconds.
Lian raised his head.
The Hollow Sun’s outer ring had turned slightly, and the black pupil in its center was slowly moving from one part of the sky to another.
It seemed to be examining the entire land.
Rindo also noticed the change, and his hand moved toward his spear.
That strange sun was doing something again.
( Scene Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 621: Twenty-Four Hours Until Death
paragraphs: "The first judgment has been completed."
Lian kept his gaze fixed on the sun, while Rindo waited a short distance away.
The voice continued.
"All presences within the judgment area have been registered."
At that moment, a very faint wave of golden light moved across the entire forest.
It passed by the pillar, fell on the surface of the spring, and then passed through Lian and Rindo’s bodies.
For a fraction of a second, Lian felt something touch his presence, but there was no physical pressure or pain, and even the rhythm of his breathing remained unchanged.
However, the feeling of being identified was completely clear, so he immediately checked the energy flows around his body.
No lasting connection like the one that had trapped Amélie had formed, so this time, it was only recording them.
The golden light passed through them and moved toward the more distant parts of the forest, and a few seconds later, the voice of the sun sounded again.
"The next judgment will begin in twenty-four hours."
"All Sinners Must Taste Death"
Rindo remained motionless for a moment before slowly repeating the words.
"Twenty-four hours..."
Lian let out a short breath.
So it will happen again.
He turned his gaze toward the golden rings, and if they took the sun’s words literally, only one day remained until the next trial.
However, they still did not know how many people would be condemned each time, only one person might be chosen, or perhaps several people.
There was even a possibility that someone might be cleared of all charges during one judgment, only to be condemned for a different reason during another.
They knew none of these rules, and they had twenty-four hours without knowing the criteria for selection or having any way to stop the sentence.
The young Vorhelm lowered the corner of his mouth slightly.
"This situation really sucks."
Of course, it was still unclear whether they had to remain in this land until the next judgment, as they could leave through the same curtain they had passed through that morning.
And if that was possible, he saw no reason to stay here and face this unknown danger.
Lian looked at Rindo.
"We need to head back to the entrance."
Rindo immediately nodded.
"I agree." Despite all the value this land offered, neither of them wanted to be the next person to be judged and sentenced to death.
"First, we’ll check the exit, if we can still pass through the curtain, there’s no reason to stay here."
Rindo placed his spear on his back.
"And if we can’t?"
"Then we’ll have to figure out what we’re dealing with before the next judgment." Lian glanced at the sun.
He took one last look at the stone pillar, then began walking back with his friend.
The return path was the same one they had taken a few hours earlier, but the farther they moved away from the spring, the more Lian noticed changes in the environment.
The forest was still beautiful, the golden leaves were shining on the branches, and the river was still flowing along its old path, but it no longer gave him the same feeling of peace as before.
Previously, the pure Mana in the area had been spread almost evenly throughout the environment, but now, thin and irregular flows could be seen among the white roots in some places.
As Lian passed by one of the large trees, he slowed his steps for a few seconds.
This one’s direction has changed too.
He did not place his hand on the tree trunk, but he could still sense the weak energy flow along the exposed roots from that distance.
Instead of moving toward the branches, part of the Mana was flowing downward.
The tree still looked completely healthy, and even its leaves had not lost their color, but the energy flow inside it was different from what he had seen that morning.
So the change isn’t limited to the spring.
He remembered this observation and continued walking with Rindo, while his friend also checked the area using his map and the markers he had recorded along the way.
"The Mana flow has changed in several places, these paths were more stable this morning." He spoke after a while.
This showed that the energy flow in the land was now working differently from how it had that morning.
"I noticed." Lian nodded.
"Do you think it’s connected to the sun?"
"I think so, the changes happened at almost the same time."
He looked at the sky for a moment, the sun’s black pupil was still open, and although its light was no longer shining directly on them, the feeling of being watched by that thing remained.
"But I still don’t know whether the sun caused the changes in the flows or whether both are the result of something else."
Rindo did not answer, as he also knew that this difference was important.
The sun might control the entire structure of this area, or perhaps it was part of a larger system that had become active again after a long time.
In any case, it was still too early to reach a conclusion.
About half an hour later, they received the first emergency messages through their communication devices, which were small magical devices made using several complex formations.
The devices had been given to them by the academy so they could stay in contact with the officials throughout their stay and report any incidents that occurred.
The rough voice of one of the exploration officials could be heard through the shared channel.
"All units inside the land, report your status. Any group that has observed an unusual environmental change must record its location and the time it happened."
Several replies came almost at the same time.
"Northern Spring Investigation Group, the sun has changed its shape, but we have no casualties so far."
"Western Mapping Unit, contact with the outer base has been lost. We’re returning to the entrance."
"Government Resource Team, the Mana flow in our area has become unstable, the cause is still unknown."
Lian listened to the voices for a moment, and some people were trying to ask the officials about the nature of the sun.
Others were complaining about losing contact with the outside world, but no one had a clear answer yet.
Rindo activated his communication device.
"This is Rindo, representative of the academy’s expedition, I’m returning to the entrance with Lian Vorhelm."
"Message received, are both of you safe?" The coordination officer replied a few seconds later.
"Yes."
Rindo paused briefly before continuing.
"But one of the Chosen from the French National Academy has died. Amélie Moreau."
There was silence for a few moments.
"Repeat that, what was the cause of death?
"The entity that appeared in the sky identified her, then announced several charges and carried out her execution. We’ll provide the details after we arrive."
This time, the silence lasted longer before the official’s voice returned in a more serious tone.
"Report received., send us your location and return directly to the entrance area."
Rindo sent their approximate location and then ended the communication.
Lian turned his gaze toward the path, and the news of Amélie’s death would probably spread among the officials and the other Chosen very soon.
However, this was unavoidable, if another judgment was going to take place, everyone present needed to know what kind of danger they were facing.
And contrary to what they had first thought, the number of people at risk was not limited to the ten Chosen.
During the past seven months, several officially Awakened members of the country’s Awakened Association had been working in the Land of the First Dawn.
Some were responsible for investigating resources, while others were carrying out mapping work.
Others had been assigned research missions and the protection of exploration areas under the government’s direct supervision.
These people had their own special permits, and their presence was independent of the expedition involving the ten Chosen.
Lian had seen some of them in the areas near the curtain since his arrival, but only now did he understand the importance of this.
If the sun had registered everyone present, then there were far more accused people than just the ten Chosen.
And if it could issue a death sentence every twenty-four hours, then this was no longer just a dangerous exploration mission.
All the human forces inside this area might become involved in a threat that none of them had enough information to deal with.
As they got closer to the entrance area, the change in the light on the horizon became more obvious.
At first, he thought it was because of the sun’s position.
However, when they left the last part of the forest and the massive golden curtain came into view again, he realized he had been wrong.
The curtain was no longer the same as it had been that morning.
Back then, strands of light had moved slowly across its surface.
The layers sometimes moved apart from each other, and it had even been possible to see the slow movement of energy along their surfaces.
But now, all those movements had stopped.
The golden strands had become so tightly packed that their individual boundaries could no longer be seen, and the curtain had turned into a single, solid surface.
Its color had also changed, the bright gold of the morning had been replaced by a dense, golden-white glow.
Rindo slowed his steps.
"This doesn’t even look like a curtain anymore."
The young Vorhelm looked up toward the heights, the wall still extended beyond the clouds, and from where they stood, no end could be seen.
"Yeah."
For a moment, he remembered what it had felt like to pass through the curtain.
Back then, he had only felt a gentle warmth on his skin, and after three steps, he had entered the Land of the First Dawn.
But the structure in front of him now looked completely different.
"We need to take a closer look."
They both moved toward the entrance area, where a group of Awakened members from the Awakened Association and government forces had gathered near the wall.
There were more of them than there had been that morning.
Some exploration units that had been working in nearby areas had returned here after receiving the warnings.
Several people were standing in front of communication equipment, trying to contact the outside centers.
And judging by their frightened and worried expressions, it seemed there was no good news.

chapters.title: Chapter 622: No Way Out
paragraphs: In one section, official mages and researchers were examining the surface of the wall.
A group of guards had also been stationed around the area to prevent people from gathering in an uncontrolled manner.
As Lian walked past them, he heard parts of their scattered conversations.
"The permits aren’t reacting at all."
"Is the connection to the outside still down?"
"Yeah, only the channels within the area are working."
"Then do the people outside know what’s happening?"
"We don’t know, we still haven’t received any replies."
He thought about the last sentence for a moment.
If the external communications were down, the officials outside the curtain might still not have accurate information about the situation inside.

Of course, it was possible that the change in the wall’s appearance could also be seen from the outside, but whether the people outside knew about the sun’s awakening or Amélie’s death was another matter.
Rindo walked toward one of the officials at the entrance.
The man appeared to be the same person who had checked the Chosen’s entry permits that morning.
"Has the exit situation been confirmed?"
"None of the passageways are working for now, and leaving is impossible." The official raised his head.
"Since when?" Rindo asked.
"Almost at the same time the sun changed. At first, the flow of the curtain slowed down, then its structure became compressed, and all the passageways closed."
The man looked clearly exhausted, but he was still trying to speak calmly.
"Everyone has tried to leave, but it doesn’t work at all."
"I’ll try." Lian looked at the wall.
The official hesitated for a moment before nodding.
"Just please don’t use any offensive skills without coordination. We still don’t know how this structure will react."
"There is no need to attack it."
He then walked toward the wall, and from up close, its golden surface looked even stranger, not a single wave moved across it.
There were no gaps between the strands of light, and unlike that morning, he could no longer feel the gentle flow of Mana across its surface.
Lian reached out with his right hand, and his fingers touched a hard barrier, so he applied more pressure for a moment.
However, the wall’s surface did not change even slightly, and the feeling of touching it was more like touching very smooth stone than energy.
He pulled his hand back.
Then he activated True Sequence.
The flows and structure of the thing in front of him became visible, and he almost immediately realized that the wall’s structure was far more complex than he had imagined.
Multiple layers of energy were stacked on top of one another, some extending upward, while others went deep into the structure to an unknown depth.
Some were also so dense that it was difficult to identify their flows.
He tried to follow one of the paths.
However, after a few moments, he realized that the farther he went into the structure, the more new paths appeared in front of him.
What an incredible structure.
He did not know who had created this wall.
But just by observing a small part of it, he could understand that breaking such a structure with a punch or an offensive skill was almost meaningless.
Even if he managed to destroy one layer, he had no idea how many more layers existed behind it, and more importantly, he still did not know what would happen if he damaged the wall.
Lian deactivated the skill, but he did not immediately step back, and two different kinds of energy, both black, formed around two of his fingers.
Eclipse Energy.
End Energy.
His fingers touched the wall, and for a moment, it seemed that the structures on its surface had begun to break apart.
However, it took only a few seconds for the layers behind them to literally devour his two demonic energies.
’Well, this is new.’ Even he was surprised for a moment, as he had not expected something to be able to destroy the power of two Demons so easily.
He moved away from the surface and looked up, as flying over the wall did not seem like a reliable solution either.
The structure’s actual height was unknown, and its upper part disappeared beyond the clouds.
Even the Wings of God, despite their extremely high flight speed, could not guarantee that he would be able to bypass such a barrier from above.
On the other hand, there was no sign that the wall ended at a certain height.
Something that could destroy the power of two Demons so easily certainly could not be bypassed simply by flying over it.
So leaving through this route is impossible for now.
He turned back toward Rindo.
"Its structure has completely changed, I can’t even determine the actual depth of its layers."
"Can we break it?" Rindo looked at the wall.
Lian shrugged slightly.
"With enough power, anything is possible, but for now, we don’t know how much power it would take, or what would happen if we damaged it."
Rindo nodded, as he found this answer reasonable.
Neither of them wanted to attack a structure that surrounded the entire land without understanding it well enough.
The young Vorhelm looked at the people around them for a moment.
"Well, it seems we have no way out for now."
Rindo stared at the height of the wall.
"And we don’t know how long that will last."
At that moment, a familiar voice came from behind them.
"Lian! Rindo!"
Both of them turned around.
Noah Laurent was walking toward them through the crowd.
His long, folded umbrella was in his right hand, and unlike his usual behavior, he did not have a very bright smile on his face.
When he came closer, he let out a short breath.
"I finally found you two."
His gaze moved between them.
"Ever since that thing appeared in the sky, I’ve been trying to figure out where you were."
"We were near the southern springs." Lian nodded.
"Oh? So Amélie was with you? As far as I know, she went that way too." Noah paused for a moment before asking.
Rindo looked at him.
"Yes."
The young Frenchman looked behind them for a moment, as if expecting the girl to appear from the crowd.
"Ever since that sun suddenly changed, I’ve been trying to contact her, but I haven’t heard anything."
When he turned his gaze back to the two of them, he noticed their silence, and his faint smile disappeared.
"What happened?"
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds before answering in a calm but completely direct tone.
"Amélie is dead."
Noah froze, and for a moment, he did not even seem to understand the meaning of the sentence.
Then his eyebrows drew together slightly.
"What?"
"The thing that awakened in the sky identified Amélie. It made several accusations and then carried out her death sentence." Rindo continued.
The young Frenchman turned his gaze toward Lian.
"Is that... real?
"We saw it ourselves." Lian nodded.
Silence fell for a few seconds, Noah shifted his fingers around the handle of his umbrella before slowly asking.
"How?"
The young Vorhelm looked at the sun’s black pupil for a moment.
"An energy structure connected to her body and soul, and after the sentence was announced, that same structure destroyed her existence. No body remained, not even a trace that we could recover."
The young Frenchman’s gaze slowly lowered, he stared at the ground for a few moments before gripping the handle of his umbrella more tightly.
"I talked to her this morning."
His voice had become much quieter than before.
"Before we chose our routes, she asked me if I would like to see a sample if she found a good medicinal plant."
A very small smile appeared on his face, but rather than showing happiness, it looked more like he was remembering an ordinary moment.
"I told her I probably didn’t know much about plants, but she said it didn’t matter, she would explain everything herself."
Noah looked at the golden wall for a moment.
"She even wanted to make medicine from some of the samples after we returned."
"She spent the entire day doing exactly that." Lian kept his gaze on him.
"Really?"
"Yeah, she even found several resources whose value we probably wouldn’t have noticed without her." The young Vorhelm paused for a moment before continuing.
"For someone I’d only just met, she knew far more about plants than I expected."
"Yeah... that sounds exactly like her." Noah let out a slow breath.
Silence fell for a few seconds.
The sound of officials talking and equipment clashing could be heard around them, but none of the three paid any attention to it.
"Can I ask you something?" The young Frenchman finally raised his head.
"Ask." Lian replied.
The Frenchman hesitated for a few moments before speaking in a low voice.
"When it happened, was there no way to stop it?"
His question was neither hostile nor did it sound like an accusation, he seemed to genuinely want to know what could be done against such a danger.
Lian also let out a sigh.

"We tried, much harder than you might think, we used everything we had, Rindo tried to cut the energy path, while I examined the structure of the sentence and managed to disrupt part of its connection for a moment."
He had also used the Wings of God and even Eclipse Energy, he had made use of everything at his disposal, but it had still been useless.
The sentence had been carried out in the end.
And when the sentence was carried out and he experienced a small part of the power of the Hollow Sun, he understood that with their current power, they had no chance against that entity.
"So you managed to affect it?" Noah raised his gaze.
"A small part of it, yeah, but the main flow was being supplied from somewhere beyond our reach, the sentence was carried out before I could fully examine its path."
The young Frenchman thought about this explanation for a few seconds before asking.
"So if someone else is chosen, we still don’t know how to stop it?" They had all heard the sun’s final words.
And now that he understood how powerful the sun was, he could not stop himself from worrying.
"Not for now." Rindo answered.
This time, Noah said nothing, and his gaze moved toward the sun, whose black pupil was still at the center of the golden ring.
However, what interested Lian was the change in the young Frenchman’s behavior, he was no longer trying to lighten the mood with a smile or a pleasant remark.
Instead, he seemed to be putting together the information he had heard.
He said nothing for a few seconds before quietly murmuring.
"So tomorrow, at this same time..."
He left the sentence unfinished, as there was no need to continue, all three of them knew what he meant.
"Well, at least we know one thing." After a while, Noah looked at Lian again.
"What?" Lian raised an eyebrow.

"Just please don’t use any offensive skills without coordination.
We still don’t know how this structure will react."
"There is no need to attack it."
He then walked toward the wall, and from up close, its golden surface looked even stranger, not a single wave moved across it.
There were no gaps between the strands of light, and unlike that morning, he could no longer feel the gentle flow of Mana across its surface.
Lian reached out with his right hand, and his fingers touched a hard barrier, so he applied more pressure for a moment.
However, the wall’s surface did not change even slightly, and the feeling of touching it was more like touching very smooth stone than energy.
He pulled his hand back.
Then he activated True Sequence.
The flows and structure of the thing in front of him became visible, and he almost immediately realized that the wall’s structure was far more complex than he had imagined.
Multiple layers of energy were stacked on top of one another, some extending upward, while others went deep into the structure to an unknown depth.
Some were also so dense that it was difficult to identify their flows.
He tried to follow one of the paths.
However, after a few moments, he realized that the farther he went into the structure, the more new paths appeared in front of him.
What an incredible structure.
He did not know who had created this wall.
But just by observing a small part of it, he could understand that breaking such a structure with a punch or an offensive skill was almost meaningless.
Even if he managed to destroy one layer, he had no idea how many more layers existed behind it, and more importantly, he still did not know what would happen if he damaged the wall.
Lian deactivated the skill, but he did not immediately step back, and two different kinds of energy, both black, formed around two of his fingers.
Eclipse Energy.
End Energy.
His fingers touched the wall, and for a moment, it seemed that the structures on its surface had begun to break apart.
However, it took only a few seconds for the layers behind them to literally devour his two demonic energies.
’Well, this is new.’ Even he was surprised for a moment, as he had not expected something to be able to destroy the power of two Demons so easily.
He moved away from the surface and looked up, as flying over the wall did not seem like a reliable solution either.
The structure’s actual height was unknown, and its upper part disappeared beyond the clouds.
Even the Wings of God, despite their extremely high flight speed, could not guarantee that he would be able to bypass such a barrier from above.
On the other hand, there was no sign that the wall ended at a certain height.
Something that could destroy the power of two Demons so easily certainly could not be bypassed simply by flying over it.
So leaving through this route is impossible for now.
He turned back toward Rindo.
"Its structure has completely changed, I can’t even determine the actual depth of its layers."
"Can we break it?" Rindo looked at the wall.
Lian shrugged slightly.
"With enough power, anything is possible, but for now, we don’t know how much power it would take, or what would happen if we damaged it."
Rindo nodded, as he found this answer reasonable.
Neither of them wanted to attack a structure that surrounded the entire land without understanding it well enough.
The young Vorhelm looked at the people around them for a moment.
"Well, it seems we have no way out for now."
Rindo stared at the height of the wall.
"And we don’t know how long that will last."
At that moment, a familiar voice came from behind them.
"Lian!
Rindo!"
Both of them turned around.
Noah Laurent was walking toward them through the crowd.
His long, folded umbrella was in his right hand, and unlike his usual behavior, he did not have a very bright smile on his face.
When he came closer, he let out a short breath.
"I finally found you two."
His gaze moved between them.
"Ever since that thing appeared in the sky, I’ve been trying to figure out where you were."
"We were near the southern springs." Lian nodded.
"Oh?
So Amélie was with you?
As far as I know, she went that way too." Noah paused for a moment before asking.
Rindo looked at him.
"Yes."
The young Frenchman looked behind them for a moment, as if expecting the girl to appear from the crowd.
"Ever since that sun suddenly changed, I’ve been trying to contact her, but I haven’t heard anything."
When he turned his gaze back to the two of them, he noticed their silence, and his faint smile disappeared.
"What happened?"
Rindo looked at him for a few seconds before answering in a calm but completely direct tone.
"Amélie is dead."
Noah froze, and for a moment, he did not even seem to understand the meaning of the sentence.
Then his eyebrows drew together slightly.
"What?"
"The thing that awakened in the sky identified Amélie.
It made several accusations and then carried out her death sentence." Rindo continued.
The young Frenchman turned his gaze toward Lian.
"Is that... real?
"We saw it ourselves." Lian nodded.
Silence fell for a few seconds, Noah shifted his fingers around the handle of his umbrella before slowly asking.
"How?"
The young Vorhelm looked at the sun’s black pupil for a moment.
"An energy structure connected to her body and soul, and after the sentence was announced, that same structure destroyed her existence.
No body remained, not even a trace that we could recover."
The young Frenchman’s gaze slowly lowered, he stared at the ground for a few moments before gripping the handle of his umbrella more tightly.
"I talked to her this morning."
His voice had become much quieter than before.
"Before we chose our routes, she asked me if I would like to see a sample if she found a good medicinal plant."
A very small smile appeared on his face, but rather than showing happiness, it looked more like he was remembering an ordinary moment.
"I told her I probably didn’t know much about plants, but she said it didn’t matter, she would explain everything herself."
Noah looked at the golden wall for a moment.
"She even wanted to make medicine from some of the samples after we returned."
"She spent the entire day doing exactly that." Lian kept his gaze on him.
"Really?"
"Yeah, she even found several resources whose value we probably wouldn’t have noticed without her." The young Vorhelm paused for a moment before continuing.
"For someone I’d only just met, she knew far more about plants than I expected."
"Yeah... that sounds exactly like her." Noah let out a slow breath.
Silence fell for a few seconds.
The sound of officials talking and equipment clashing could be heard around them, but none of the three paid any attention to it.
"Can I ask you something?" The young Frenchman finally raised his head.
"Ask." Lian replied.
The Frenchman hesitated for a few moments before speaking in a low voice.
"When it happened, was there no way to stop it?"
His question was neither hostile nor did it sound like an accusation, he seemed to genuinely want to know what could be done against such a danger.
Lian also let out a sigh.

"We tried, much harder than you might think, we used everything we had, Rindo tried to cut the energy path, while I examined the structure of the sentence and managed to disrupt part of its connection for a moment."
He had also used the Wings of God and even Eclipse Energy, he had made use of everything at his disposal, but it had still been useless.
The sentence had been carried out in the end.
And when the sentence was carried out and he experienced a small part of the power of the Hollow Sun, he understood that with their current power, they had no chance against that entity.
"So you managed to affect it?" Noah raised his gaze.
"A small part of it, yeah, but the main flow was being supplied from somewhere beyond our reach, the sentence was carried out before I could fully examine its path."
The young Frenchman thought about this explanation for a few seconds before asking.
"So if someone else is chosen, we still don’t know how to stop it?" They had all heard the sun’s final words.
And now that he understood how powerful the sun was, he could not stop himself from worrying.
"Not for now." Rindo answered.
This time, Noah said nothing, and his gaze moved toward the sun, whose black pupil was still at the center of the golden ring.
However, what interested Lian was the change in the young Frenchman’s behavior, he was no longer trying to lighten the mood with a smile or a pleasant remark.
Instead, he seemed to be putting together the information he had heard.
He said nothing for a few seconds before quietly murmuring.
"So tomorrow, at this same time..."
He left the sentence unfinished, as there was no need to continue, all three of them knew what he meant.
"Well, at least we know one thing." After a while, Noah looked at Lian again.
"What?" Lian raised an eyebrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 623: A World Full of Questions
paragraphs: "That we have time to learn something before the next judgment."
Noah paused for a moment.
"I know one day isn’t a lot of time, but it’s better than not knowing when it might happen again."
"I more or less think the same way." Lian looked at him.
"So, what’s your plan now?"
"At first, I wanted to make sure the exit was sealed, now we need to find out what’s happening in other areas and check the Mana flow in the rest of the region."
When they entered the Land of the First Dawn that morning, the Mana flow here had been incredibly good, but on their way back, they had noticed that it was changing.
"From what I’ve heard, the changes aren’t limited to your area." Noah nodded.
"Do you know something?" Rindo looked at him.

"Some members of the Awakened Association are gathering information from different areas, I spoke with them before finding you two, apparently, the Mana flow has also changed in some of the northern springs."
Lian narrowed his eyes.
"The same change we saw."
"One group also reported that the light from some plants in the western forest had become weaker, but it’s still unclear whether it’s related to the sun."
"We need to compare the times when these changes happened." Rindo nodded.
"Exactly. If they all happened at almost the same time, there must be some connection." Noah looked at him.
Lian looked at him for a few seconds, it was a reasonable suggestion, and more importantly, Noah wasn’t trying to give a definite answer without having all the information.
He only wanted to gather the available evidence.
"That’s a good idea."
"I’m glad I could help." The young Frenchman smiled and then looked at the wall behind them.
"By the way, have they found a way out here yet?"
Rindo shook his head.
"No."
"The curtain’s structure has changed, and we have no way out for now."
"So we’re really trapped." Noah let out a short sigh, remained silent for a moment, and then looked between the two of them again.
"I don’t know how much I can help, but I can talk to the Association members and the other Chosen, maybe we can gather more information."
"That would be a great help." Lian nodded.
"So, are we working together for now?" The young Frenchman gave them a gentle smile.
"As long as we have a common goal, definitely." Rindo replied in his usual serious tone.
Noah nodded without the slightest sign of displeasure.
"That’s enough for me."
Lian looked at him for a moment.
Despite everything that had happened, Noah still had the same quality that had caught his attention at Base #3.
He could communicate with different people, but more importantly, he knew when to speak and when to simply listen.
And now, when cooperation between different groups had become important, such a personality could be very useful.
But why was he trying so hard to get close to them?
A while later, all three of them went to a section of the entrance area that the Awakened Association members were using to collect exploration reports.
Several large maps had been placed on temporary tables, and the officials were marking the locations of active groups with small markers.
In another corner, government staff were checking messages received from more distant areas.
Despite the obvious concern among the people present, the overall order of the place was still being maintained.
Lian considered this a good sign.
If the official forces lost control of themselves, the situation could turn into chaos even before the next judgment.
He walked toward one of the maps.
"How many areas have reported changes in the Mana flow so far?"
One of the officials raised his head and, after recognizing the emblem of his expedition, pointed to a section of the map.
"We have four confirmed reports, two from the northern springs, one near the western forest, and one from the southern section."
He looked at the markers, the distance between the locations was considerable.
If all these changes had happened at almost the same time, the chance that they were simply the result of local events became lower.
"Do we know the exact times?" he asked.
The man checked several reports.
"Almost at the same time the sun changed its shape, although there are a few minutes of difference between some reports."
"Then they’re connected." Lian nodded, he had already been somewhat sure about this, they just wanted to make sure their guess wasn’t wrong.
Rindo moved closer and looked at the recorded locations.
"Mark the locations of the springs too. Especially the places where white roots are present."
"White roots?" The official looked at him for a moment.

"At one of the southern springs, we noticed that some of the Mana started moving deeper into the ground after the sun awakened, we want to see whether the same thing has happened in other places." Lian explained.
The man immediately signaled to one of the staff members.
"Separate the reports related to the springs."
"So you think the Mana flow moving into the ground and that sun are connected?" Noah asked from beside the table.
The young Vorhelm looked at the map for a moment.
"It’s possible, three things happened at almost the same time, and at some point, coincidence stops making sense." He pointed at the markers one by one.
"The sun changed from its previous state, the outer curtain turned into a wall, and the energy flow in some parts of the land changed."
Noah moved his gaze across the map, and Lian continued.
"If all three are parts of a larger structure, maybe by examining one of them, we can learn something about the other two."
"But we still don’t know where the flows begin or where they lead." Rindo nodded.
"That’s right."
"That’s why it’s only a theory for now." Lian raised his head.
If the movement of the Mana flow downward and into the ground was truly connected to the sun’s awakening, then understanding this structure might help them.
Especially when he considered that the Hollow Sun possessed power that none of them yet knew how to fight against.
Afterward, Rindo gave the officials the details about Amélie’s trial.
When he explained the three accusations that had been announced, several people exchanged surprised looks, and one of the researchers asked.
"The domain of the condemned?"
"Those were the exact words it used."
The man thought for a moment.
"As far as I know, no area with that name has been recorded on any official map."
"We hadn’t heard anything about it either." Lian nodded, there was another point, but he did not mention it yet because he had no evidence to support it.
However, he thought that the domain of the condemned might refer to the Land of the First Dawn.
But if that was the case, a question came to mind, why did it call this place the domain of the condemned?
The researcher looked at the report again.
"And the third accusation... property belonging to the Mother?"
This time, even some of the other staff members turned toward them.
Noah frowned slightly.
"The Mother? Does that mean it’s someone’s name?"
"We don’t know." Lian answered again.
"Maybe it means the owner of this land."
"It’s possible, but we have nothing to confirm it yet."
The young Frenchman thought about this for a few seconds before looking at the sun.
"If it’s really a judge, there must be some rules, but we don’t even know what those rules are."
"And until we learn the rules, we can’t predict who will be chosen next." Rindo replied in a serious tone.
A brief silence followed, this was a worrying matter for everyone present.
Each of them had gathered resources or examined structures during their time in the Land of the First Dawn.
If collecting plants, entering unknown areas, or interfering with ancient relics counted as crimes, then a large number of them might be at risk of being condemned.
But it was still unclear what order the sun followed when choosing people.
"For now, it’s better to assume that no one is exempt from judgment, at least until we prove otherwise." Lian said after a few moments.
One of the officials nodded.
"We’ll pass the necessary warning to the exploration groups."
The young Vorhelm looked at the map again, this decision would not remove the danger, but at least it could stop more people from approaching unknown structures without a good reason.
It would be better not to touch the treasures in this land from now on, at least if they didn’t want to die.
After the initial investigation ended, the three of them left the temporary building, and the golden light was still shining across a large part of the plain.
However, the black pupil of the Hollow Sun was still clearly visible even from this distance.
Noah looked at the sky for a moment.
"I’m still not used to seeing that thing above our heads."
"I don’t think anyone will get used to it anytime soon." Lian gave him a brief glance.
The young Frenchman gave a very slight smile, but he soon became serious again.
"Well, what should we do now?"
Rindo opened the map.

"The officials are gathering reports from more distant areas, I want to compare the Mana flow information with the current situation, if the changes continue, and I also want to see whether there’s another way out."
Lian nodded.
"Good."
Then he looked toward the southern part of the plain.
"I want to examine one of the Mana flows near the curtain, I still don’t know how the wall and the underground flows are connected."
"Then what about me?" Noah asked.
Lian looked at him for a moment.
"You have better connections with the other Chosen, try to find out how they’re doing, especially those who haven’t returned from more distant areas yet."
"Okay, but I think it’s better if we don’t get too far away from each other for now." The young Frenchman nodded and added.
"Because we still don’t know what has changed, and if something like Amélie’s trial starts again, maybe we can at least warn each other and perhaps find a way to stop it."
Lian thought for a few seconds.
It was a reasonable suggestion.
Although he could handle many ordinary dangers on his own, having several people with different abilities could be useful when facing an unknown structure.
Especially now that only one day remained until the next judgment, and even he was helpless against the power of that sun.

chapters.title: Chapter 624: The Ground Is No Longer Safe ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian nodded, and Noah smiled with satisfaction.
"Great."
Rindo did not object either, and then all three headed toward the southern part of the entrance area.
A few minutes later, while walking along the stone path, Lian checked his resources.
He still had the healing potions and Mana recovery potions he had bought before the expedition.
In addition, he had collected a considerable amount of plants and resources from the Land of the First Dawn during the first day.
Some of them had extremely high monetary value, but their importance was no longer limited to their selling price.
Plants that could restore Mana were essential resources in a situation where the exit was sealed.
Healing materials might also become more important later, along with the new treasure he had taken from beneath the pillar, the Core of the Fallen Star.
An S-rank treasure that granted the ability to manipulate gravity.
He had not yet had the chance to fully test its abilities, and according to the treasure’s description, its final effect depended on the user’s power and Mana.
However, the fact that someone with enough Mana reserves could even change the gravity of an entire world did not mean that he could do the same thing right now.
Even so, even limited control over gravity in a small area could have many uses, especially when moving around, crossing obstacles, or fighting enemies who depended on high mobility.
Lian gave a faint smile for a moment.
’This is a really good treasure.’
However, he had no intention of activating its ability in an unfamiliar environment without testing it first, he still needed to check its Mana consumption and the actual range of its effects.
He turned his attention back to the path.
’For now, I need to figure out what’s going on with this land beneath our feet.’
They moved away from the main entrance area and reached a part of the plain where several golden trees grew along the path.
On the left, the ground gradually sloped down toward the river.
On the right, there was a group of white rocks, with thin roots visible between their cracks.
Every few minutes, Rindo checked their position on the map, while Noah used his communication device to keep track of the nearby groups.
Lian paid more attention to the Mana flow beneath the ground, and in some places, the energy was still moving naturally.
However, the closer they got to the rocky areas, the more narrow paths leading downward he could sense.
’The same pattern again.’
He stopped beside one of the white roots for a moment, but before he could examine it further, he felt a brief vibration beneath his feet.
Several small stones fell from beside the rocks.
Noah raised his head.
"Did you feel that?"
Rindo nodded.
"Yeah."
Lian looked down at the ground, the vibration had lasted only about a second, and its strength was not particularly great, but something about it caught his attention.
The pressure had come from a specific direction, as if part of the ground had shifted deep underground for a moment.
A few seconds passed.
Then a second vibration occurred, and this time, it was stronger.
The sound of breaking stone came from the right, and one of the golden trees near the rocks swayed slightly from side to side.
"Move away from the rocks." Rindo immediately prepared his spear.
All three took several steps toward the more open part of the plain, and at that moment, a long, cracking sound came from beneath the ground.
Krrrrrk!
A thin crack appeared on the surface of the soil.
At first, it was only a few meters long, but it quickly spread along the stone path.
Small rocks moved to both sides, and the crack widened enough for the soil between them to start collapsing.
"I don’t think this is a normal earthquake." Noah looked at the crack.
Lian had noticed it too, instead of spreading in an irregular pattern, the crack was moving along a specific path.
At one point, it even changed direction and continued almost in a straight line toward another part of the plain.
’It’s as if the ground already had a specific fracture line.’

Lian nodded.

Lian nodded.

Four events.

"What is it?"
Lian raised his hand slightly.
"Wait a moment."

He furrowed his brows slightly.
What the hell is this?
What the fucking hell is going on here?

chapters.title: Chapter 625: The Withered ( GT Bonus - )
paragraphs: "Did you sense something?" Rindo looked at him and asked quietly.
Lian kept his eyes on the crack.
"Yeah. There’s something down there, something alive."
"A monster?" Noah took his folded umbrella off his shoulder.
"I don’t know yet."
At that moment, the sound of scraping became clearer.
Krrrrrk...
A small stone broke off from the edge of the crack and fell down,
Then a second stone fell, and a few seconds later, something appeared from the darkness.
At first, only a few long fingers could be seen, fingers with gray, cracked skin, each of them unnaturally long.
Their joints were clearly visible, and some of them bent in directions that did not match the natural structure of a human hand.
The fingers gripped the edge of the rock, and then a thin, extremely long arm emerged from inside the crack.
Dark lines could be seen on its skin, looking more like cracks in stone than wounds.
The creature pushed itself upward.
Part of its shoulder appeared, and then its head rose from the darkness.
Lian looked at the thing in front of him for several seconds, at first glance, the creature had a distant resemblance to a human.
However, almost all the proportions of its body were unnatural, its head was smaller than normal, and an extremely thin neck connected it to a long, bony torso.
The skin on its face was dark gray, and it had no clear nose, only a thin bony bump in the center of its face, while an uneven mouth stretched from beneath it toward part of its cheek.
Several rows of thin, uneven teeth could be seen inside its mouth, but its eyes were even stranger.
Two deep, dark sockets with extremely faint lights shining at the back of them.
The creature remained motionless for a few moments, then opened its mouth, and the sound of its breathing was more like air passing through a broken pipe.
Then, with an irregular movement, it pulled more of itself out of the crack, and when the rest of its body finally emerged, its true shape became clear.
It had an almost human torso, but it was extremely long and thin.
Its rib cage was visible beneath its skin, and its raised ribs ran along both sides of its body.
Two extremely long arms extended from its shoulders, but there were four more limbs on the lower part of its torso.
These limbs looked more like the long legs of a spider, each had several joints and bent at unusual angles.
The creature used all of them to support its body weight, so when it finally settled onto the rocks, it looked more like a giant spider with a human upper body than an ordinary monster.
Noah slowly let out a breath for a moment.
"What kind of creature is this...?"
Rindo also raised his spear, but Lian still did not move, because the creature’s behavior was even stranger than its appearance.

After climbing out, instead of attacking, it remained completely motionless for several seconds, then tried to stand on two legs, but its lower limbs bent in the wrong directions, and its body fell to one side.
The creature supported itself with its long arms and tried to stand again... and failed again.
It was as if it did not even know how to use its own body, it looked at its long fingers for a moment, then brought one of them close to its face.
It opened and closed the finger several times, and finally muttered something in a hoarse voice.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
’It can talk?’
The creature opened its mouth again, but this time, only an unclear sound came from its throat, then it began touching its own face with its long fingers.
Its nails scraped across its cracked skin, making a dry sound, as if it were trying to remember the shape of its face.
Or perhaps it was searching for something that no longer existed.
The young Vorhelm paid attention to the creature’s Mana flow for a moment, the energy inside its body was irregular.
Some parts held large amounts of Mana, but other parts seemed almost empty, even the connection between its physical movements and its energy flow was unusual.
’This isn’t a natural monster.’
He still did not know exactly what kind of creature he was facing, but even the monsters he had seen usually had more recognizable movement patterns.
This one seemed to have lost some of its natural control over its body, and before he could examine it further, another sound came from the left side of the crack.
This time, several large stones broke away from the wall, and an extremely tall shadow moved through the darkness.
Noah immediately prepared his umbrella.
Rindo also turned his spear toward the newly opened section of the crack.
A few moments later, the second creature emerged, and this one was much taller than the first.
Its body was about four and a half meters tall, but it was so thin that at first glance, it looked more like a stretched shadow than a living creature.
Its skin was completely black, not the natural black color of skin, but a color similar to stone that had burned in a fire for a long time, the blackest black imaginable.
Its body was covered in tiny cracks, and a very faint purple light could be seen inside some of them.
Its arms reached almost to its knees, and its long, thin, bony fingers were so long that when it bent its body, they almost touched the ground.
Its legs were also extremely long, and their joints were positioned in ways that made its stance look unnatural.
However, the most frightening part of its appearance was its face, or rather, what should have been its face.
There was no visible mouth, no nose, and not even a clear bump that could suggest its facial structure had once been human.
There was only a smooth, black surface, with extremely faint purple lights shining at two points on it.
The creature stood motionless for several seconds, then its head tilted slightly to the right before its body straightened with a fast, stiff movement.
However, the movement was so uneven that it seemed as if the space between the two positions had simply disappeared.
Lian took a closer look for a moment.
’Its movements are strange too.’
The creature took a step forward, and its feet slowly touched the rocks, then it stopped completely for several seconds.
After that, its neck began to turn, and without moving its shoulders, its head turned almost all the way toward the back of its body.
The movement came with a dry sound.
Crack... crack...
Then it returned to its original position.
Noah glanced at Lian for a moment.
"Have you ever seen anything like this?"
"No."
Of course, there were many strange creatures in the Ruined Realm, but something about the behavior of these two creatures made Lian feel that this was not simply a difference in race or appearance.
Their movements were unnatural, their reactions to the environment did not seem logical either, and most importantly, neither of them had tried to attack yet.
At the same time, more sounds came from underground, and from another crack a short distance away, a creature with white, cracked skin pulled itself out.
Its body was almost human, but its arms were much longer than its legs.
One of its shoulders was lower than the other, and its neck was bent so far backward that its face was almost looking at the sky.
To move, the creature placed its hands on the ground and pulled its body forward.
It moved several meters before stopping, and then its cracked lips began to move.
"I don’t want to..."
Its voice was weak.
"I don’t want to... I don’t want to..."
It repeated the words again and again, without making it clear who it was talking to.
A little farther away, another creature emerged from a crack, with a large part of its face covered by a layer of hard, black skin.
It had four arms, but one of them grew unnaturally from the back of its torso.
As it moved, that extra arm kept dragging along the ground, and its fingers opened and closed without moving in coordination with its other limbs.
The creature looked around for a moment, then fell to its knees and began digging into the soil.
It dug hurriedly with irregular movements, as if it wanted to return underground, but the more soil it moved aside, the more confused its movements became.
Lian carefully observed all of this behavior.
’Strange.’
If these creatures had emerged from underground to hunt, why were some of them trying to go back down?
Why could one of them not even walk properly?
And why were some of them repeating words that sounded more like forgotten memories than the roars of monsters?
He looked at the first spider-like creature for a moment, it was still running its long fingers over its face.
Sometimes its mouth opened, but most of the sounds that came out were unclear.
’Maybe they were intelligent creatures before.’
This possibility came to Lian’s mind, although he still had no evidence to support it, they might be an unknown race.
Perhaps they were creatures whose bodies and minds had changed because of some kind of corruption or severe damage.
However, the longer he watched them, the less likely it seemed that their condition was natural.
Especially when he noticed that some of them looked directly at the sky after emerging, instead of paying attention to their surroundings or the people present.
At the same sun that had awakened a few hours ago.
’Does that mean they have seen it before?’
At that moment, the tall, black creature stopped moving completely, and the purple lights on its face remained still for several seconds.
Then its head slowly rose until it was looking directly at the Hollow Sun.
Lian noticed that its body had started trembling, not like a creature preparing to attack, but like someone who had recognized something terrifying.
Its extremely long arms tightened at its sides, and its fingers slowly curled up as its dark nails scraped across the surface of the rock.
Noah, who had kept his umbrella ready for defense until then, narrowed his eyes.
"What is it afraid of?"
Rindo did not answer.
Lian continued examining the creature as well.
What stood before him was different from all his initial theories.
A creature with a terrifying appearance, a body that seemed to have lost much of its natural structure, and an unusual presence that made it difficult to even determine the exact state of its Mana.
But now, that same creature was afraid of looking at the sun.
Finally, a sound came from deep inside its black body.
It was hoarse and weak, and so uneven that it seemed to have to search through its mind to form each word.
Its body trembled again, and its head tilted slightly to one side, while the purple lights on its face weakened for a moment.
...Then it whispered in a clearer voice.
"Judge...?"
Lian narrowed his eyes.
’A judge?’
The creature looked at the sun again.
This time, its body trembled more violently, its fingers gripped the surface of the rock, and for a moment, it seemed as if it wanted to retreat.
But its long legs did not move, as if even its fear could not help it escape properly, and then the same hoarse voice sounded again.
"The judge... has awakened?"
For several seconds, no one said anything.
Rindo held his spear more tightly, and Noah lowered his umbrella slightly without taking his eyes off the creature.
And Lian shifted his gaze away from that terrifying body and looked at the Hollow Sun.
The black pupil was still at the center of the enormous golden rings.
But now, a new question had formed in his mind.
’So this creature recognizes it?’
Before he could ask anything, another scraping sound came from underground.
Then another, followed by several more sounds coming from different directions, long fingers appeared at the edges of cracks farther away.
Thin bodies moved between the rocks, and faint lights began appearing one after another in the depths of the earth.
Broken whispers rose from the darkness.
He slowly turned his head, until a few minutes ago, he had thought their biggest problems were the Hollow Sun and the sealed exit.
But now, something stood before him that none of the reports from the past seven months had mentioned.
Creatures with twisted bodies, confused minds, and memories that seemed to have lost large parts of their contents.
They were emerging from deep underground, and unlike ordinary monsters, some of them did not even know how to move.
Lian looked toward the darkness beneath the cracks.
Things were hidden deep beneath the Land of the First Dawn, and now, one after another, they were beginning to awaken.
( Scene Visualization )
