It moved several meters before stopping, and then its cracked lips began to move.
"I don’t want to..."
Its voice was weak.
"I don’t want to...
I don’t want to..."
It repeated the words again and again, without making it clear who it was talking to.
A little farther away, another creature emerged from a crack, with a large part of its face covered by a layer of hard, black skin.
It had four arms, but one of them grew unnaturally from the back of its torso.
As it moved, that extra arm kept dragging along the ground, and its fingers opened and closed without moving in coordination with its other limbs.
The creature looked around for a moment, then fell to its knees and began digging into the soil.
It dug hurriedly with irregular movements, as if it wanted to return underground, but the more soil it moved aside, the more confused its movements became.
Lian carefully observed all of this behavior.
’Strange.’
If these creatures had emerged from underground to hunt, why were some of them trying to go back down?
Why could one of them not even walk properly?
And why were some of them repeating words that sounded more like forgotten memories than the roars of monsters?
He looked at the first spider-like creature for a moment, it was still running its long fingers over its face.
Sometimes its mouth opened, but most of the sounds that came out were unclear.
’Maybe they were intelligent creatures before.’
This possibility came to Lian’s mind, although he still had no evidence to support it, they might be an unknown race.
Perhaps they were creatures whose bodies and minds had changed because of some kind of corruption or severe damage.
However, the longer he watched them, the less likely it seemed that their condition was natural.
Especially when he noticed that some of them looked directly at the sky after emerging, instead of paying attention to their surroundings or the people present.
At the same sun that had awakened a few hours ago.
’Does that mean they have seen it before?’
At that moment, the tall, black creature stopped moving completely, and the purple lights on its face remained still for several seconds.
Then its head slowly rose until it was looking directly at the Hollow Sun.
Lian noticed that its body had started trembling, not like a creature preparing to attack, but like someone who had recognized something terrifying.
Its extremely long arms tightened at its sides, and its fingers slowly curled up as its dark nails scraped across the surface of the rock.
Noah, who had kept his umbrella ready for defense until then, narrowed his eyes.
"What is it afraid of?"
Rindo did not answer.
Lian continued examining the creature as well.
What stood before him was different from all his initial theories.
A creature with a terrifying appearance, a body that seemed to have lost much of its natural structure, and an unusual presence that made it difficult to even determine the exact state of its Mana.
But now, that same creature was afraid of looking at the sun.
Finally, a sound came from deep inside its black body.
It was hoarse and weak, and so uneven that it seemed to have to search through its mind to form each word.
Its body trembled again, and its head tilted slightly to one side, while the purple lights on its face weakened for a moment.
...Then it whispered in a clearer voice.
"Judge...?"
Lian narrowed his eyes.
’A judge?’
The creature looked at the sun again.
This time, its body trembled more violently, its fingers gripped the surface of the rock, and for a moment, it seemed as if it wanted to retreat.
But its long legs did not move, as if even its fear could not help it escape properly, and then the same hoarse voice sounded again.
"The judge... has awakened?"
For several seconds, no one said anything.
Rindo held his spear more tightly, and Noah lowered his umbrella slightly without taking his eyes off the creature.
And Lian shifted his gaze away from that terrifying body and looked at the Hollow Sun.
The black pupil was still at the center of the enormous golden rings.
But now, a new question had formed in his mind.
’So this creature recognizes it?’
Before he could ask anything, another scraping sound came from underground.
Then another, followed by several more sounds coming from different directions, long fingers appeared at the edges of cracks farther away.
Thin bodies moved between the rocks, and faint lights began appearing one after another in the depths of the earth.
Broken whispers rose from the darkness.
He slowly turned his head, until a few minutes ago, he had thought their biggest problems were the Hollow Sun and the sealed exit.
But now, something stood before him that none of the reports from the past seven months had mentioned.
Creatures with twisted bodies, confused minds, and memories that seemed to have lost large parts of their contents.
They were emerging from deep underground, and unlike ordinary monsters, some of them did not even know how to move.
Lian looked toward the darkness beneath the cracks.
Things were hidden deep beneath the Land of the First Dawn, and now, one after another, they were beginning to awaken.
( Scene Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 626: The Withered II
paragraphs: "Judge... has awakened?"
The hoarse voice of the tall creature echoed among the broken rocks.
Lian kept his eyes on it.

The black creature, standing nearly four and a half meters tall, was still looking up at the sky, its long limbs trembling violently, and the two purple lights where its eyes should have been remained fixed on the Hollow Sun.
Around it, other creatures were also emerging from cracks in the ground.
Some had bodies similar to humans, but their arms were far too long, some moved across the ground using four or six limbs, and others could not even stand properly on their own feet.
He looked at the scene in front of him for a few seconds.
So it recognizes that sun.

He still did not know what these creatures were or why they had emerged from deep underground, but that one sentence showed that at least some of them knew something about the strange phenomenon in the sky.
Lian focused his attention on the nearest spider-like creature.
A semi-transparent window appeared in front of him.
[ Race: The Withered ]
[ Rank: Mutated ]
[ Level: 26 ]
His eyebrows rose slightly.
Mutated?
At the same moment, Noah also looked at the creature, and similar information appeared in front of him.
"Mutated? So these used to be other creatures?" The young Frenchman took his folded umbrella from his shoulder and moved his gaze over the creature’s unusual limbs.
Rindo also kept his spear ready.
"Most likely."
Lian gave a slight nod, as he was familiar with the concept of mutated creatures.

Unlike most monsters that belonged to a specific race from the beginning, mutated creatures were beings that had lost their original forms or nature and turned into something different because of extreme changes.
Such transformations did not always make them stronger.
Some mutated creatures gained new abilities, while others even lost the natural abilities of their original races.
This was not the first time he had encountered mutated creatures either, as he had previously encountered a race of them in the Dreadmaw Mountains.
However, what caught Lian’s attention was that the creatures in front of him did not look similar to one another.
One moved across the ground using six limbs, while another had a tall and thin body.
And the third creature, with white, cracked skin, was still trying to crawl back into the crack it had emerged from.
So they probably didn’t all belong to the same race before.
He turned his gaze back to the tall creature.
If he could obtain even a little information from it, perhaps some of the recent events would become clearer.
He took a step forward.
"Do you recognize that sun?"
The creature lowered its head for a moment, and the purple lights on its face settled on him.
Its neck tilted to one side with a stiff movement, and its extremely long fingers slowly opened and closed.
"Ju... Judge..."
Lian waited.
"Have you seen it before?"
The creature had no clear mouth, but a hoarse voice came from deep inside its body.
"Sh... shouldn’t..."
At that moment, one of the nearby spider-like creatures turned its head toward the young Vorhelm.
Its body tensed for a few seconds, then its four lower limbs pressed hard against the rocks.
Lian noticed the movement from the corner of his eye, but before the creature could reach him, something unexpected happened to the way it moved.
Its two hind legs bent at unnatural angles, and instead of moving straight forward, its body launched toward him from the right.
Its long, bony limb moved toward his neck.
Vorhelm only turned his upper body slightly, allowing the attacking limb to pass beside his shoulder, then moved his right fist forward.
Bang!
The punch struck the creature directly in the chest, its cracked skin sank inward, the bones beneath it broke, and the force of the blow passed through its body.
The Withered was thrown several meters backward and landed on a rock with a heavy sound.
It did not move again.
[ Level 26 Withered has been killed ]
[ EXP received ]
Lian glanced at the notification.

Since reaching the limit of twenty thousand stats during his first evolution, increasing his stats further was no longer possible, but experience could still raise his level and bring him closer to his second evolution.
And these creatures? Despite their terrifying appearances, they did not seem to pose much of a threat to his current strength.
Of course, he still needed to check the levels of the others.
Lian turned his gaze back toward the cracks.
More Withered were coming out.
And some of them reacted in completely different ways after seeing the first creature die.
One curled up on the ground, another began screaming, but several creatures that seemed to have less control over their behavior charged straight toward him.
He let out a calm breath.
"Well, it seems we can’t talk for now."
The first Withered to approach was a three-meter-tall creature with long arms and a face covered in bone plates.
[ Race: The Withered ]
[ Rank: Mutated ]
[ Level: 31 ]
The creature attacked with a hoarse sound, bringing its right arm down toward Lian from above.
However, compared to the enemies he had fought before, the speed of its attack was nothing special.
Without stepping back, Lian caught the creature’s wrist with his left hand, stopping its long limb on the spot.
The Withered tried to free its arm, but it did not have enough physical strength to do so.
The young Vorhelm punched the creature’s head with his right fist, and the sound of breaking bones rang out. Its black head bent to one side, and its huge body fell to the ground.
[ Level 31 Withered has been killed ]
[ EXP received ]
Lian released the broken wrist.
The first creature had not even fully hit the ground when another Withered approached from the left.
This one had four arms, with its two upper limbs being longer, and their fingers ended in hard claws.
He recognized its movement.
He took a short step forward and punched the middle of the creature’s body before it could complete its attack.
Its thin body caved in at the point of impact, a muffled sound came from its throat, and it was thrown several meters backward.
When it hit the ground, it was already dead, but the battle had only just begun.
Three more Withered emerged from the crack on the right.
One moved on all fours, another had a thin body with unusually long legs, and the third looked almost like a human whose face was mostly hidden beneath dark skin.
Lian glanced at their notifications.
[ Level 22 ].
And [ 34 ]
They’re still weak.
The first creature leaped at him.
Lian swung his fist toward its head, and the blow landed before its claws could reach his body, crushing its head.
The second tried to pass him from the side, but he took a short step and blocked its path before punching it in the chest.
The sound of breaking bones rang out.
The third stopped for a moment, but before it could change direction, Lian reached it and struck its face with his right fist.
Its body fell to the ground and did not get back up.
[ Level 22 Withered has been killed. ]
[ Level 29 Withered has been killed. ]
[ Level 34 Withered has been killed ]
[ EXP received ]
The young Vorhelm looked at the notifications for a moment, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
Not bad.
Although the Withered had different levels, most of them had trouble controlling their movements.
Even those that showed greater speed usually lost their balance after one or two movements.
In comparison, he not only had very high stats, but his indestructible body also greatly increased his physical attack and defense.
He did not need to use skills that consumed a lot of energy or the energy of his cores to defeat these creatures.
His ordinary punches were enough.
The sounds of bones breaking and bodies hitting the rocks echoed around the cracks.
Several more Withered climbed down from the edges of the rocks.
One of them leaped toward Lian with an irregular movement, but he had already noticed it.
He moved half a step to the right, and the creature passed beside him. Just as it was about to land on the ground, Lian’s fist struck the back of its neck.
A short cracking sound followed, and the Withered fell onto the rocks and remained motionless.
Farther away, another creature with extremely long limbs tried to approach him from behind.
But even before it reached him, Lian turned around and struck the creature’s head directly with his fist, sending it flying to one side.
The Withered fell to the ground and did not move again.
With every kill, an EXP notification appeared.
Lian paid no attention to them for a while, keeping his focus on the creatures that were still trying to attack him.
However, he had not forgotten one thing.
Not all the Withered behaved aggressively, as some of them were still standing motionless beside the cracks.
The white-skinned creature that had repeatedly said "I don’t want to" was now curled up behind one of the rocks.
And the tall, shadow-like figure, the same creature that had spoken the word Judge, was slowly moving away from the battle area.
Lian did not stop it from leaving, as he had no need to chase a creature that did not intend to fight just to gain EXP.
But that wasn’t the only thing.
It was the behavior of these creatures that interested him, and he wanted to understand the reason behind it.

chapters.title: Chapter 627: An Easy Hunt
paragraphs: But what about the enemies attacking them?
There was no reason to keep them alive.
At that moment, one of the larger Withered emerged from the southern crack, its body nearly four meters tall, with hard plates growing over its chest and shoulders.
Unlike most of the previous creatures, its movements seemed more coordinated.
\[ Race: The Withered \]
\[ Rank: Mutated \]
\[ Level: 45 \]
Lian looked at the information for a moment.
This one’s level is much higher than the others.
The creature let out a rough roar and charged straight at him, its right foot pressing hard against the stone.
Then it threw a massive punch toward his head.
The young Vorhelm caught the attacker’s wrist, and the impact sent a heavy force through his arm, but it did not even force him to take a step back.
With his other hand, he threw a straight punch at the Withered’s chest.
Bang!
The hard plates covering the creature’s body cracked.
The force of the punch passed through its natural armor and forced its four-meter-tall body to take a step back.
The Withered tried to regain its balance.
But Lian gave it no chance, taking a short step forward before driving his second punch straight into the creature’s head.
The bones in its face broke under the impact, and the large Withered was lifted off the ground before crashing heavily onto the rocks behind it.
\[ Level 45 Withered killed \]
\[ Experience received \]
He looked at the motionless creature.
Two punches.
For an enemy at level forty-five, it had not shown much resistance, though level was not the only factor that determined a monster’s strength.
Rank, race, body structure, skills, and evolution were also very important.
And despite their relatively high levels, these mutated creatures seemed to have lost a large part of their original abilities.
He looked around, and by this point, most of the Withered that had tried to attack him had been killed.
However, a few more creatures were still emerging from the cracks, and just as he was about to move toward them, a scream came from his right.
"Help!"
One of the staff members of the Awakened Association, who had come close to the crack to examine the changes in the ground, had become trapped in the path of a tall Withered while retreating.
The creature was about three meters tall, and its bony hands ended in hard claws.
\[ Race: The Withered \]
\[ Rank: Mutated \]
\[ Level: 37 \]
The staff member tried to move out of the creature’s attack path.
But his foot was stuck between two rocks, and the Withered raised its right hand, if its claws hit the man, they would probably tear through a large part of his body.
However, before the attack could be completed...
Clang!
A spear came in from the left.
Rindo turned his weapon and knocked the creature’s long arm off course, causing its claws to strike the rock beside the staff member’s feet instead of his body.
At the same moment, Noah opened his Twelve-Rib War Umbrella.
The metal surface of the umbrella moved between the staff member and the creature’s second attack.
A loud impact rang out.
Noah turned his wrist, directing the force of the attack to both sides, while grabbing the staff member’s arm with his free hand.
"Get up!"
The man struggled to free his foot, and the young Frenchman pulled him backward.
"Get behind that rock, it’s not safe here."
The staff member retreated without arguing.
Rindo continued using his spear to control the distance between himself and the creature, but before he had to launch another attack, Lian approached from the left.
His fist struck the Withered directly in the head, and a short cracking sound followed, the creature fell to the ground and remained motionless.
\[ Level 37 Withered killed \]
\[ Experience received \]
He glanced at Rindo and Noah.
Rindo simply nodded.
Noah closed his umbrella and looked toward the staff member, and after making sure the man had moved out of danger, he gave a small smile.
"Well, we couldn’t let you do all the work alone."
Lian did not answer and simply turned his attention back to the cracks.
A few more creatures could still be seen in the distance, but most of them were moving toward different parts of the plain instead of attacking.
It seemed that some of them had understood, even with their confused minds, that approaching the young Vorhelm was not a good choice after seeing the other Withered die.
The fight continued for a few more minutes.
Lian defeated the last of the attacking creatures with ordinary punches, and eventually, a relative silence returned to the area.
The bodies of more than twenty Withered were scattered around the cracks, with some lying on the ground with their skulls crushed.
Others had their chest bones broken by direct hits, while several more lay motionless farther away, beside the broken rocks.
However, he himself had not suffered any noticeable injuries.
Even the amount of mana he had used was almost nothing.
He checked his own status for a moment.
His level was still 29.
However, the experience he had gained had added a considerable amount to his progress.
"If I can find more of these creatures, I’ll probably be able to level up very soon," he murmured quietly.
This was a valuable opportunity.
Especially when he considered that he still needed to make more progress before reaching his second evolution.
But for now, there was something more important, he looked at one of the nearby corpses, and unlike ordinary monsters, the Withered had many differences in their physical structures.
Some had extra limbs, some had extremely long bodies, and others still retained signs of different body structures.
On one of the spider-like creature’s hands, he could see a deformed metal ring.
The ring had almost sunk into the skin of its finger, but it was still clear that it had once been made for an intelligent creature to wear.
He looked at it for a moment.
So they were probably something else before.
The System identified all of them as a single race, but the remaining signs on their bodies pointed to different pasts.
What could change different creatures into the same form?
He still had no answer, and examining a few corpses would not be enough to reach a reliable conclusion.
Lian stood up, and at that moment, an urgent message came from Noah’s communication device.
"All groups near the entrance area, we need support! Mutated creatures have emerged from the cracks around the Exploration Center!"
Noah immediately activated the communication device.
"Exact location?"
"Eastern section! Several groups of creatures are moving toward the equipment and support buildings!"
Lian looked at Rindo.
"Looks like it’s not just happening here."
Rindo placed his spear on his back.
"We should return."
Noah also reported their location without wasting time, and then all three of them began making their way back.
When they reached the entrance area, the situation there was very different from what it had been a few hours earlier.
The temporary buildings that had previously been used to check permits and store exploration equipment had now been turned into parts of a defensive base.
Heavy carts had been moved along the wider paths, and members of the Association were busy moving equipment crates, medical supplies, and food to the central area.
Several groups of guards had also been stationed at fixed intervals.
Around the main building, workers were strengthening the defensive barriers, while mages prepared protective formations on several stone slabs.
Lian stopped for a moment.
So they finally decided to establish a base here.

With the golden barrier closed and the dangers in the area increasing, this decision made sense. Keeping their forces spread out across a land where the ground was splitting apart would only increase the number of casualties.
On the other hand, the Association and government forces already had facilities near the entrance, and they could now use those same buildings and resources to establish a temporary base.
However, what caught his attention was the unexpected order in the area.
Despite everything that had happened over the past few hours, people were not moving around without a purpose.
Every group had a specific task.
The healers had been moved to the central area, the guards were taking up their assigned positions, and the communication officers were recording incoming reports on a large map.
This level of coordination under the current conditions was no small achievement.
"Looks like they finally found a proper commander," Noah said while looking at the busy forces.
Rindo had also noticed the order in the area.
"Better than having every group make its own decisions."
Lian nodded.
"Let’s see who’s in charge."
In front of one of the main buildings, several Association officers and government representatives had gathered around a large table.
In the center of the group stood a tall man with dark golden hair.
He wore a blue military uniform, with the official emblem of the country’s Awakened Association displayed on his shoulders.
He was probably no older than thirty-five, but the way he stood and the calm expression on his face belonged to someone with plenty of command experience.
With one hand resting on the map, he was examining a report from one of the officers.
"If we hold the eastern route here, how far is the second position from the medical center?"
"About four hundred meters," the officer answered.
The man moved his gaze across the map.
"That’s too far, move the route for transporting the wounded behind the equipment storage area, the middle section must also remain clear, I don’t want the carts blocking the rapid response teams."
"Understood." The officer nodded.
The man immediately turned to the next person.

With his other hand, he threw a straight punch at the Withered’s chest.
Bang!
The hard plates covering the creature’s body cracked.
The force of the punch passed through its natural armor and forced its four-meter-tall body to take a step back.
The Withered tried to regain its balance.
But Lian gave it no chance, taking a short step forward before driving his second punch straight into the creature’s head.
The bones in its face broke under the impact, and the large Withered was lifted off the ground before crashing heavily onto the rocks behind it.
\[ Level 45 Withered killed \]
\[ Experience received \]
He looked at the motionless creature.
Two punches.
For an enemy at level forty-five, it had not shown much resistance, though level was not the only factor that determined a monster’s strength.
Rank, race, body structure, skills, and evolution were also very important.
And despite their relatively high levels, these mutated creatures seemed to have lost a large part of their original abilities.
He looked around, and by this point, most of the Withered that had tried to attack him had been killed.
However, a few more creatures were still emerging from the cracks, and just as he was about to move toward them, a scream came from his right.
"Help!"
One of the staff members of the Awakened Association, who had come close to the crack to examine the changes in the ground, had become trapped in the path of a tall Withered while retreating.
The creature was about three meters tall, and its bony hands ended in hard claws.
\[ Race: The Withered \]
\[ Rank: Mutated \]
\[ Level: 37 \]
The staff member tried to move out of the creature’s attack path.
But his foot was stuck between two rocks, and the Withered raised its right hand, if its claws hit the man, they would probably tear through a large part of his body.
However, before the attack could be completed...
Clang!
A spear came in from the left.
Rindo turned his weapon and knocked the creature’s long arm off course, causing its claws to strike the rock beside the staff member’s feet instead of his body.
At the same moment, Noah opened his Twelve-Rib War Umbrella.
The metal surface of the umbrella moved between the staff member and the creature’s second attack.
A loud impact rang out.
Noah turned his wrist, directing the force of the attack to both sides, while grabbing the staff member’s arm with his free hand.
"Get up!"
The man struggled to free his foot, and the young Frenchman pulled him backward.
"Get behind that rock, it’s not safe here."
The staff member retreated without arguing.
Rindo continued using his spear to control the distance between himself and the creature, but before he had to launch another attack, Lian approached from the left.
His fist struck the Withered directly in the head, and a short cracking sound followed, the creature fell to the ground and remained motionless.
\[ Level 37 Withered killed \]
\[ Experience received \]
He glanced at Rindo and Noah.
Rindo simply nodded.
Noah closed his umbrella and looked toward the staff member, and after making sure the man had moved out of danger, he gave a small smile.
"Well, we couldn’t let you do all the work alone."
Lian did not answer and simply turned his attention back to the cracks.
A few more creatures could still be seen in the distance, but most of them were moving toward different parts of the plain instead of attacking.
It seemed that some of them had understood, even with their confused minds, that approaching the young Vorhelm was not a good choice after seeing the other Withered die.
The fight continued for a few more minutes.
Lian defeated the last of the attacking creatures with ordinary punches, and eventually, a relative silence returned to the area.
The bodies of more than twenty Withered were scattered around the cracks, with some lying on the ground with their skulls crushed.
Others had their chest bones broken by direct hits, while several more lay motionless farther away, beside the broken rocks.
However, he himself had not suffered any noticeable injuries.
Even the amount of mana he had used was almost nothing.
He checked his own status for a moment.
His level was still 29.
However, the experience he had gained had added a considerable amount to his progress.
"If I can find more of these creatures, I’ll probably be able to level up very soon," he murmured quietly.
This was a valuable opportunity.
Especially when he considered that he still needed to make more progress before reaching his second evolution.
But for now, there was something more important, he looked at one of the nearby corpses, and unlike ordinary monsters, the Withered had many differences in their physical structures.
Some had extra limbs, some had extremely long bodies, and others still retained signs of different body structures.
On one of the spider-like creature’s hands, he could see a deformed metal ring.
The ring had almost sunk into the skin of its finger, but it was still clear that it had once been made for an intelligent creature to wear.
He looked at it for a moment.
So they were probably something else before.
The System identified all of them as a single race, but the remaining signs on their bodies pointed to different pasts.
What could change different creatures into the same form?
He still had no answer, and examining a few corpses would not be enough to reach a reliable conclusion.
Lian stood up, and at that moment, an urgent message came from Noah’s communication device.
"All groups near the entrance area, we need support!
Mutated creatures have emerged from the cracks around the Exploration Center!"
Noah immediately activated the communication device.
"Exact location?"
"Eastern section!
Several groups of creatures are moving toward the equipment and support buildings!"
Lian looked at Rindo.
"Looks like it’s not just happening here."
Rindo placed his spear on his back.
"We should return."
Noah also reported their location without wasting time, and then all three of them began making their way back.
When they reached the entrance area, the situation there was very different from what it had been a few hours earlier.
The temporary buildings that had previously been used to check permits and store exploration equipment had now been turned into parts of a defensive base.
Heavy carts had been moved along the wider paths, and members of the Association were busy moving equipment crates, medical supplies, and food to the central area.
Several groups of guards had also been stationed at fixed intervals.
Around the main building, workers were strengthening the defensive barriers, while mages prepared protective formations on several stone slabs.
Lian stopped for a moment.
So they finally decided to establish a base here.
With the golden barrier closed and the dangers in the area increasing, this decision made sense.
Keeping their forces spread out across a land where the ground was splitting apart would only increase the number of casualties.
On the other hand, the Association and government forces already had facilities near the entrance, and they could now use those same buildings and resources to establish a temporary base.
However, what caught his attention was the unexpected order in the area.
Despite everything that had happened over the past few hours, people were not moving around without a purpose.
Every group had a specific task.
The healers had been moved to the central area, the guards were taking up their assigned positions, and the communication officers were recording incoming reports on a large map.
This level of coordination under the current conditions was no small achievement.
"Looks like they finally found a proper commander," Noah said while looking at the busy forces.
Rindo had also noticed the order in the area.
"Better than having every group make its own decisions."
Lian nodded.
"Let’s see who’s in charge."
In front of one of the main buildings, several Association officers and government representatives had gathered around a large table.
In the center of the group stood a tall man with dark golden hair.
He wore a blue military uniform, with the official emblem of the country’s Awakened Association displayed on his shoulders.
He was probably no older than thirty-five, but the way he stood and the calm expression on his face belonged to someone with plenty of command experience.
With one hand resting on the map, he was examining a report from one of the officers.
"If we hold the eastern route here, how far is the second position from the medical center?"
"About four hundred meters," the officer answered.
The man moved his gaze across the map.
"That’s too far, move the route for transporting the wounded behind the equipment storage area, the middle section must also remain clear, I don’t want the carts blocking the rapid response teams."
"Understood." The officer nodded.
The man immediately turned to the next person.

chapters.title: Chapter 628: We Must Survive
paragraphs: "Any news about the new cracks?"
"They’re still spreading, two have been reported in the southern area."
"Pull back the scouts in that section, no position is worth losing people over, especially when the ground beneath their feet isn’t stable."
Lian listened to the conversation for a few seconds.
Good.
Unlike some commanders he had seen before, this man did not only care about his people’s combat strength.
He also considered support routes, the movement of the wounded, and the possibility of losing ground when making his decisions.
At that moment, one of the officers noticed the three Chosen and walked over.
"Are you from the expedition group?"
"Yes. We returned to report the situation in the southern area." Rindo presented his identification badge.
After checking the badge, the man turned toward the commander.
"Commander Weston, three young Chosen have returned, and it seems they also fought some mutated creatures."
The blond-haired man raised his head, his gaze resting on Lian for a moment before moving to Rindo and Noah.
"Come closer."
When they approached, the man introduced himself.
"Alaric Weston, senior officer in charge of the Awakened Association’s security operations and temporary commander of this base."
Lian remembered his name.

It seemed this man was an Awakened at level forty-three, an experienced individual who had now taken command of the emergency operations after coordinating with government officials and the Association.
"How many creatures did you see?" Alaric asked without any introduction.
"There were about thirty near the cracks, most of them were between level twenty and forty-five."
"Did they all attack?"
"No, some had no intention of fighting at all, and we killed more than twenty of the ones that attacked us, the rest scattered."
Alaric looked at the map for a moment.
Rindo continued.
"They were all registered under the race name The Withered, but their appearances and movements were very different."
The commander thought for a few seconds before asking.
"Any injuries?"
"None of us were injured, one of the Association’s staff members almost got caught by one of them, but we got him out safely." Lian answered.
The man gave him a brief look.
"Good."
Then he placed his finger on the southern part of the map.
"But our forces can’t all deal with this many enemies, some of our staff members can’t even fight a level thirty mutated creature."
Lian agreed.
"That’s why it’s better to keep weaker groups away from the cracks."
Alaric nodded.
"Exactly."
Then he gestured to one of the officers.
"Send the enemy level information to all units, forces below the required level must not leave the second zone without support."
The officer immediately recorded the order, and Alaric looked at Lian again.
"Vorhelm, right?
"Yeah."
"I know your name and background, I’ve also read the report about the defense of Base #3, if you really managed to defeat that many mutated creatures in a short time, we might need your help here."
Lian turned his gaze toward the map.
"As long as it’s useful work, I don’t mind."
"That’s what I wanted to hear." The corner of the commander’s mouth lifted slightly.
Some time later, the forces at the emergency base gathered in the central area, although not all the guards left their positions.
Alaric had ordered only the representatives of each group and the forces whose duties had temporarily ended to attend and listen to the briefing.
Lian stood near one of the support buildings with Rindo and Noah.
Around them were Awakened Association members, government guards, exploration staff, and several Chosen who had returned to the entrance area.
Some were still tired, others had fresh wounds, and almost everyone glanced at the Hollow Sun every few minutes.
Its black pupil remained open above the land.
Alaric stood on a low platform, waited a few seconds for the scattered conversations to stop, and then spoke in a firm voice.
"As of this morning, the world we knew no longer exists."
No one spoke.
"The exit is closed, unknown creatures are coming out from beneath the ground, and something has appeared in the sky that can pass a death sentence without any warning."
His gaze moved across the people present.
"I won’t calm you down with empty promises, we still don’t know how to get out of here, and we don’t know who the next judgment will target."
Several people in the crowd lowered their heads.
But the commander continued.
"What we do know is that we’re still alive, and we still have equipment. We still have forces that can fight and people who can treat the wounded."
He pointed toward the buildings behind him.
"Until we find a way out, this is our base, not because it’s the safest place in the world, but because we can defend it."
Then his expression became more serious.
"No one is forced to pretend they’re not afraid, being afraid in this situation is normal, but what we cannot do is abandon our duties."
The man paused for a moment.
"There are people behind these walls who may still not know what’s happened to us, and on this side of the walls, there are people who cannot defend themselves."
His voice became slightly firmer.

"If the combat forces retreat, those people will die, if the healers abandon their duties, the wounded will die, and if every one of us only thinks about saving ourselves, this base won’t last even a single day."
A heavy silence fell over the area, and Alaric lowered his hand.
"Our duty today isn’t to defeat that sun."
His gaze moved toward the massive golden ring for a moment before returning to the people in front of him.
"Our duty is to make sure there are still people alive here tomorrow who can find a way to defeat it."
For a few moments, no one spoke, and then one of the Association’s officers answered in a firm voice.
"Understood, Commander."
Several others nodded as well, but the most important change was not just in their reactions.
When Alaric began assigning duties, the people moved toward their designated areas in a more organized way.
Their fear had not disappeared, but at least now they knew what they needed to do.
Lian watched the scene.
He’s a good commander.
He had seen many powerful people before, but physical strength and leadership were two different things.
And Alaric seemed to have considerable skill in the latter.
After the gathering ended, the commander explained the base’s defensive plan to the group leaders.
The base had been divided into three main zones, the central area was where essential supplies, communication equipment, healers, and non-combat staff were kept.
The middle ring was assigned to the guards and combat groups.
In the outer zone, scouts were responsible for reporting the movements of The Withered, cracks in the ground, and any unusual changes in the environment.
However, unlike ordinary bases, simply building defensive barriers was not enough here.
After all, the enemies could emerge from beneath the ground.
For this reason, Alaric had ordered some guards to focus on checking changes in the ground’s surface and the flow of mana beneath it instead of watching the entrance routes.
He had also designated two specific routes for transporting the wounded and carrying out emergency retreats.
Rindo accepted the responsibility of working with the route coordination and perimeter defense teams.
Noah was assigned to the rescue and protection of support staff, but when it was Lian’s turn, Alaric moved his gaze across the map.
"I’m not going to assign you to a fixed position."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Why?"
The commander pointed toward the eastern part of the map.
"Because if thirty of those creatures attack from one direction and you can eliminate them in a few minutes, keeping you behind a wall would be a waste of your strength."
Then he pointed toward another section.
"Rapid Response Force, whenever a defensive line is in danger of breaking, you’ll go there."
Lian looked at the marked routes for a moment.
"That makes sense."
However, something caught his attention.
Part of the retreat route passed right beside an area of land that had not yet been fully examined.
He pointed at the map.
"We also need another retreat route."
Alaric looked at him.
"Why?"
"If the ground beneath this section cracks, you’ll lose both the main route and the outer defensive ring at the same time, at that point, transporting the wounded will become almost impossible."
The commander looked at the map for a few seconds before gesturing to one of the officers.
"Mark an alternative route behind the equipment storage area, check the ground’s stability first, and then mark the route."
"Yes, Commander." The officer nodded.
Alaric looked at Lian again.
"That was a good point."
"I’d prefer to still have a way to move when we need to save someone." The young Vorhelm added with a smile.
The blond-haired man gave a small smile.
"Same here."
The preparations at the base continued until nightfall.
Different groups were stationed at designated points, and several temporary watchtowers were set up around the middle ring.
The wounded who had been injured during the first attacks by The Withered were moved to the medical area, while food supplies and essential potions were also recorded and stored separately.
However, despite this new order, the condition of the ground continued to worsen.

chapters.title: Chapter 629: A New Way to Kill
paragraphs: In the southern area, several small cracks had continued to spread.
One of the old routes had been completely blocked, and farther away, hot steam was rising from between the broken rocks.
Lian was standing in the eastern part of the base when an alert sounded from his communication device.
"Emergency report! The route connecting the two southern positions is splitting apart!"
He immediately replied.
"Send me the location."
A few seconds later, a new marker appeared on the map.
It was not far away.
He moved without wasting any time, and when he arrived, a large part of the stone path had split apart.
The two sides of the crack were several meters apart, and red molten rock could be seen deep below, hot steam was rising between the rocks and drying out the plants near the edge.
On the opposite side, six support staff members were trapped.
The ground behind them was also slowly collapsing.
One of the guards was trying to cross the crack using his movement skill.
But the great distance and unstable edges made it impossible for him to find a safe way to help the others cross.
Lian examined the situation for a moment, A few meters apart, and both sides still have solid rocks.
The solution was simple.
He raised his right hand.
\[ Frost Dominion \]
The air around him quickly became cold.
The moisture in the environment turned into small ice crystals, and a white layer of ice formed over the rocks near the crack.
Then the ice began to spread from both sides, thick branches of ice formed along the solid rocks and extended toward the center.
A few seconds later, the two sides connected.
He released more mana to make the structure thicker so it could support the weight of several people.
In a short time, an ice bridge had formed between the two edges.
"Cross one by one!" His voice echoed through the hot steam.
The first guard immediately started moving, followed by the second and then the others.
He maintained the flow of cold energy, but just as the third person reached the middle of the bridge, a faint cracking sound came from beneath it.
He lowered his gaze.
The hot steam from the molten rock had reached the underside of the ice, drops of water were falling from the edges of the bridge, and white steam was rising along the crack.
Damn it, it’s hotter than I thought.
Lian poured more mana into the structure, and the small cracks on the bridge’s surface closed, but at the same time, another part of the lower layer began to melt.
The molten rock was still a considerable distance from the bridge.
However, the heat rising from the depths was enough to slowly destroy the ice structure.
"Move faster!"
The last two guards crossed the bridge carefully but without stopping.
At that moment, the sound of cracking ice rang out.
Lian released more cold energy, and the structure became solid again for a few seconds, and finally, the last person reached safety.
He lowered his hand, and the flow of mana stopped.
A few moments later, the middle section of the ice bridge cracked under the constant heat.
Crack!
Thick pieces of ice broke away from both sides, then fell into the white steam and red glow of the molten rock, and the sound of their impact could be heard from deep inside the crack.
The young Vorhelm looked at the remains of the bridge for a moment.
"So even my ice can’t withstand this heat for very long."
Of course, if he used all his strength to reinforce the structure, he might be able to keep it standing for longer.
But doing so would require a constant supply of mana, and as the temperature increased, the amount of mana needed would also increase.
Keeping a bridge standing for a few minutes was possible.
But permanently sealing the massive cracks in the land, with molten rock rising from their depths, was a completely different matter.
Some time later, Alaric arrived at the location with several officers, and the commander first checked the condition of the six rescued people.
After making sure they were all safe, he walked toward the crack.
"Did you make that ice bridge?"
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
Alaric looked at the remaining steam.
"Can you make it again?"
"I can, but it won’t last."
He pointed toward the red glow deep below.
"The higher the molten rock rises, the more mana I’ll have to use to keep it standing, for now, I can buy us a few minutes, but I can’t seal all the cracks in this area with ice."
Alaric looked at the crack for a moment and then nodded.
"A few minutes can mean the difference between life and death when transporting the wounded or rescuing a group."
He turned toward the officer beside him.
"Remove this route from the map of permanent routes, if we need it again, we’ll only use it for emergency transport."
The officer recorded the order.
Lian looked at the commander for a moment.
Even after seeing the power of Frost Dominion, the man had no intention of building the entire defense plan around its constant use.
A few minutes later, all the forces in that section had moved to their alternative positions, and the first night continued with the base still standing.
But farther away, more cracks could be seen in the darkness beneath the golden light of the Hollow Sun.
On the morning of the second day, the Land of First Dawn no longer looked completely like the paradise Lian had seen when he first arrived.
The golden trees still shone across the plains, and clear rivers still flowed through the grasslands, but large cracks had appeared in the ground in some areas.
Hot steam was rising from parts of these cracks.
Several old routes had been blocked, and some trees near the unstable areas had tilted because the soil around their roots had fallen away.
However, a large part of the area was still beautiful.
This contrast made the scene even stranger.
A short distance away from a green forest, the ground had split open, and the red light of molten rock could be seen deep below.
As Lian left his resting place, he looked at the sky for a moment, the Hollow Sun was still at the same height.
Its black pupil remained open, and the golden rings around it were moving slowly.
Almost one night had passed since the first judgment, and only a few hours remained until the next one.
He took a calm breath.
"It’s better to use this opportunity."
He now intended to examine something that had occupied his mind for a long time.
The Corrupt Sun talent.
During the attack by the black vultures, he had managed to destroy the mana structure of the Reverse Reflection Array by using it.
But that battle had caused a new question to form in his mind.
If I can control corrupt light this precisely, why should I only use it to destroy arrays?
Until now, he had focused mostly on the talent’s ability to wear things down, but perhaps he could use the same energy in other forms as well.
Especially in combat.
After informing the communication unit of his approximate location, he moved away from the main base, though he had no intention of going into a dangerous area.
He only wanted to practice in a quiet part of the rocky ground near the base, a place where he could return quickly if he received an emergency message.
Some time later, Lian reached an area surrounded by several tall, white rocks.
The ground was relatively stable.
There were no active cracks nearby, and he could not sense any dangerous creatures through his perception either.
He stopped between two rocks.
Then he looked at the golden light shining down from the sky, even after the Hollow Sun had awakened, the light in the environment still flowed normally across most areas.
And that was enough for the Corrupt Sun talent.
Lian raised his right hand and released a small amount of mana, at that moment, a very thin strand of the light around his fingers changed color.
The bright golden light turned into a faint black shade, and a corrupt aura formed along the path of the light.
He examined it for a moment.
So far, it’s the same as before.
He had already used this ability to corrupt energy flows, but this time, he tried to concentrate the energy in a very small point.
At first, the strand of light became thinner for a moment.
But when he applied more pressure, its structure became unstable and scattered before reaching the target.
A dark mark remained on the surface of the rock in front of him.
He looked at it.
"Too much focus makes me lose control of its path."
He tried again, this time reducing the amount of energy and keeping the path of the light shorter.
The corrupt light became thinner, and he pointed his index finger at the rock in front of him before directing the energy along a straight path.
Hiss...
A dark beam of light shot out from his finger like a laser, reached the rock’s surface, and left a shallow line on it.
Lian looked at the result for a moment, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
This is interesting.
The concentrated impact had managed to wear away the rock, and this was with him using only a very small amount of mana.
But the real advantage of this method was something else.
Speed and focus.
The corrupt light could reach a specific point almost without requiring any large physical movement, and if the target had a mana barrier, the talent’s main effect would also work at the same time.
He could take any of the lines of light and reflections in the sky, corrupt them, and then control them however he wanted.
He realized that he could now shoot beams of corrupt light like lasers, causing his targets to break apart and fall to pieces on the spot.
There was no limit to the number of shots he could fire at the same time, he could shoot hundreds of beams of light.
Of course, the mana limit still existed.
He also realized that he could place a beam of corrupt light on a target and activate it whenever and wherever he wanted, causing the target to break apart.
It was like a special skill used by Assassin classes.
Lian repeated the experiment several more times.

sentences.text: In the southern area, several small cracks had continued to spread.
One of the old routes had been completely blocked, and farther away, hot steam was rising from between the broken rocks.
Lian was standing in the eastern part of the base when an alert sounded from his communication device.
"Emergency report!
The route connecting the two southern positions is splitting apart!"
He immediately replied.
"Send me the location."
A few seconds later, a new marker appeared on the map.
It was not far away.
He moved without wasting any time, and when he arrived, a large part of the stone path had split apart.
The two sides of the crack were several meters apart, and red molten rock could be seen deep below, hot steam was rising between the rocks and drying out the plants near the edge.
On the opposite side, six support staff members were trapped.
The ground behind them was also slowly collapsing.
One of the guards was trying to cross the crack using his movement skill.
But the great distance and unstable edges made it impossible for him to find a safe way to help the others cross.
Lian examined the situation for a moment, A few meters apart, and both sides still have solid rocks.
The solution was simple.
He raised his right hand.
\[ Frost Dominion \]
The air around him quickly became cold.
The moisture in the environment turned into small ice crystals, and a white layer of ice formed over the rocks near the crack.
Then the ice began to spread from both sides, thick branches of ice formed along the solid rocks and extended toward the center.
A few seconds later, the two sides connected.
He released more mana to make the structure thicker so it could support the weight of several people.
In a short time, an ice bridge had formed between the two edges.
"Cross one by one!" His voice echoed through the hot steam.
The first guard immediately started moving, followed by the second and then the others.
He maintained the flow of cold energy, but just as the third person reached the middle of the bridge, a faint cracking sound came from beneath it.
He lowered his gaze.
The hot steam from the molten rock had reached the underside of the ice, drops of water were falling from the edges of the bridge, and white steam was rising along the crack.
Damn it, it’s hotter than I thought.
Lian poured more mana into the structure, and the small cracks on the bridge’s surface closed, but at the same time, another part of the lower layer began to melt.
The molten rock was still a considerable distance from the bridge.
However, the heat rising from the depths was enough to slowly destroy the ice structure.
"Move faster!"
The last two guards crossed the bridge carefully but without stopping.
At that moment, the sound of cracking ice rang out.
Lian released more cold energy, and the structure became solid again for a few seconds, and finally, the last person reached safety.
He lowered his hand, and the flow of mana stopped.
A few moments later, the middle section of the ice bridge cracked under the constant heat.
Crack!
Thick pieces of ice broke away from both sides, then fell into the white steam and red glow of the molten rock, and the sound of their impact could be heard from deep inside the crack.
The young Vorhelm looked at the remains of the bridge for a moment.
"So even my ice can’t withstand this heat for very long."
Of course, if he used all his strength to reinforce the structure, he might be able to keep it standing for longer.
But doing so would require a constant supply of mana, and as the temperature increased, the amount of mana needed would also increase.
Keeping a bridge standing for a few minutes was possible.
But permanently sealing the massive cracks in the land, with molten rock rising from their depths, was a completely different matter.
Some time later, Alaric arrived at the location with several officers, and the commander first checked the condition of the six rescued people.
After making sure they were all safe, he walked toward the crack.
"Did you make that ice bridge?"
Lian nodded.
"Yeah."
Alaric looked at the remaining steam.
"Can you make it again?"
"I can, but it won’t last."
He pointed toward the red glow deep below.
"The higher the molten rock rises, the more mana I’ll have to use to keep it standing, for now, I can buy us a few minutes, but I can’t seal all the cracks in this area with ice."
Alaric looked at the crack for a moment and then nodded.
"A few minutes can mean the difference between life and death when transporting the wounded or rescuing a group."
He turned toward the officer beside him.
"Remove this route from the map of permanent routes, if we need it again, we’ll only use it for emergency transport."
The officer recorded the order.
Lian looked at the commander for a moment.
Even after seeing the power of Frost Dominion, the man had no intention of building the entire defense plan around its constant use.
A few minutes later, all the forces in that section had moved to their alternative positions, and the first night continued with the base still standing.
But farther away, more cracks could be seen in the darkness beneath the golden light of the Hollow Sun.
On the morning of the second day, the Land of First Dawn no longer looked completely like the paradise Lian had seen when he first arrived.
The golden trees still shone across the plains, and clear rivers still flowed through the grasslands, but large cracks had appeared in the ground in some areas.
Hot steam was rising from parts of these cracks.
Several old routes had been blocked, and some trees near the unstable areas had tilted because the soil around their roots had fallen away.
However, a large part of the area was still beautiful.
This contrast made the scene even stranger.
A short distance away from a green forest, the ground had split open, and the red light of molten rock could be seen deep below.

chapters.title: Chapter 630: The Sun No Monster Can Face ( Ps Bonus - )
paragraphs: When the path of the light was short, it was easier to control, but as the distance increased, maintaining his focus became more difficult.
Of course, he could solve this problem by practicing and using more mana, so it was a problem that could be solved, just at a small cost.
He also tried to fire beams like the ones the Leviathan had fired, and although it was a little more difficult, it was still possible.

He only realized that creating very large beams also consumed a lot of mana, but considering how much destructive power they had, especially when combined with End Energy and Eclipse, it was worth it.
Lian lowered his hand for a moment, and he was satisfied with this result as well.
He had now discovered another use for his talent, which he could turn into a more effective attack method with more practice.
He continued experimenting with his talent.
For a moment, he thought about another possible use for it.
If an enemy had a very powerful defensive barrier, perhaps he could weaken part of it with Corrupt Light before launching his main attack.
Of course, this method still required time, enough light, and precise energy control, so he could not use it without limits in every situation.
But it was worth learning.
Very much worth it.
The third experiment was more interesting to Lian.
He fought most of his battles with his fists.
So if he could combine Corrupt Light with physical attacks, his talent would become much more useful.
He raised his right hand and gathered a small amount of Corrupt Light around his knuckles.
At first, a very thin layer of energy formed over his skin, but when he threw a test punch into the air, the flow of light broke apart.
Part of the energy scattered, while the rest fell behind the movement of his arm.
Lian looked at his hand for a moment.
It’s harder to coordinate it with fast movements.
He tried again, but this time, instead of keeping the energy active throughout the entire movement, he decided to focus it right before impact.
His fist moved toward the rock in front of him, and during the final part of its path, Corrupt Light gathered around his knuckles.
Bang!
His fist struck the rock and completely shattered it, sending large and small pieces flying in every direction.
However, this result did not show him anything new, because he could have shattered the same rock even without Corrupt Light.
So this time, he decided to test it on an even larger rock and created several layers of mana around it as defensive barriers.
His fist struck the stone surface, producing a short impact sound, but at the same time, Corrupt Light at the point of contact penetrated the defensive layers.
The mana covering the impact area began to break down.
And before the defensive flow could transfer the force of the punch to other parts, part of its structure was destroyed.
Lian pulled his hand back and looked at the point of impact.
This time, the result was clear, the physical impact had damaged the rock and completely shattered it, but before that, Corrupt Light had destroyed all the defensive layers.
This is much better.
If he used this combination against an enemy with strong defenses, he might be able to put two different kinds of pressure on them at the same time.
Physical force and the erosion of their defenses.
Of course, he still needed to improve his control.

During fast attacks, if he did not release the Corrupt Light at the right moment, a large part of the energy would be wasted before impact, but even this basic version was useful for a fighter who mostly fought with his fists.
For a moment, Lian thought about his skill, Disaster Suppression Fist.
If he combined the two, the destructive power of his punches would become terrifying, and he doubted that ordinary defenses would have any effect against his fists anymore.
He lowered his right hand.
He now understood several new ways to use Corrupt Sun.
He gave a faint smile, at least it was worth practicing, so after finishing his experiments, he sat on one of the white rocks for a while.
His gaze moved toward the sky.
The Hollow Sun was still high in the distance, its enormous black pupil remained open, and the golden rings around it continued to rotate slowly.
For a moment, he thought about the events of the previous day.

Amelie had been killed without having a chance to defend herself, the golden barrier had turned into an impenetrable wall, the ground was splitting apart, and creatures with mutated bodies were emerging from the depths.
Among all these events, one thing still seemed strange to him.
The Withered’s fear of the sun.
He remembered the tall, black creature whose entire body had started shaking when it saw the sun’s pupil.
That creature even knew the name Judge.
But why?
Had it encountered the sun in the past?
Or were all The Withered instinctively afraid of the sun’s power?
Lian thought for a moment.
"Maybe it wouldn’t hurt to ask another monster too."
At the moment, he had three special members in his colony.
Despite their strength, the first two members did not know much about the history or unknown structures of the Ruined Realm.
However, the third member, the Dreadmaw Sovereign, was an Unholy-rank monster that had ruled its own territory for more than thirty years.
Its intelligence and experience were different from those of ordinary monsters, so perhaps it knew something about the Hollow Sun or the surrounding area.
Of course, there was no guarantee, but there was no harm in asking.
Then he activated the Hive Dominion talent.
Thousands of points of light appeared in front of him, and the particles slowly came together, forming the enormous body of the colony’s third special member a few seconds later.
As soon as the Dreadmaw Sovereign appeared, it raised its head, looked around for a moment, and then fixed its gaze on Lian.
"So you finally decided to summon me?" Its voice still carried the same roughness and pride as before.
"I have a question."
Three furrowed its bony eyebrows for a moment.
"I hope you didn’t drag me away from my rest just to ask some worthless question."
Ignoring its tone, Lian pointed toward the sky.
"Do you know what that is?"
The Sovereign raised its head, and at that very moment, its entire body went stiff, it did not move for several seconds, and even its breathing stopped.
Its red eyes remained fixed on the enormous rings of the Hollow Sun.
At first, Lian thought the creature had recognized something, but he soon realized that something else was happening.
The Sovereign’s enormous fingers began to tremble.
The muscles in its arms tightened, and its nails dug so deeply into its own palms that dark blood ran between its fingers.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
What happened?
Three took a step backward, its movement was unsteady, its right foot dragged across the rock, and it almost lost its balance for a moment.
It tried to look away from the sky, but it seemed that something deep inside it would not allow it to lower its head.
A short, broken breath escaped its throat.
"That..."
Its hand moved toward its chest.
"What is that...?"
"You’re supposed to tell me." The young Vorhelm did not move from his place.
But this time, the Dreadmaw Sovereign gave no proud answer, instead, it shook its head violently.
"I don’t know!"
Its voice was broken, and this was what truly caught its master’s attention.
He had never heard the Dreadmaw Sovereign speak in such a tone before, this was the same creature that had ruled its mountain for thirty years.
The same monster that had killed many people and carried out terrible experiments to create a human body for itself.
And even when it was defeated by Lian and Seris, it had never completely set aside its pride.
But now, its body was shaking so badly that it could barely stand properly, its knees bent, and it dropped onto one knee with a heavy sound.
Thud!
The stone beneath its knee cracked, and the Sovereign placed its hand on the ground to keep itself from falling completely.
But its fingers were still trembling.
Through the Colony Link, Lian felt a strong change in its emotional state.
Fear.

But it was not ordinary fear, nor was it the feeling of danger one experienced when facing a powerful enemy, instead, it was a deep and almost paralyzing terror that seemed to come from somewhere beyond the creature’s conscious control.
The Sovereign wanted to run away.
Its entire being was demanding it.
But it could not even figure out which direction it should move in.
Lian paid attention to this feeling for a moment, even through the link, its intensity was abnormal.
Interesting...
He had seen weaker monsters feel pressure and fear when facing creatures of higher ranks before.
But this time, the situation was much more serious, Three had not even been attacked yet, and the Hollow Sun had shown no direct interest in it.
Even so, simply looking at it was enough to make an Unholy-rank creature react this way.
Lian walked a few steps closer.
"Three."
The monster struggled to turn its head slightly.
"Have you ever seen anything like that before?"
Three took several short, broken breaths and then shook its head.
"No... never..."
"Then why are you so afraid?"
The Sovereign opened its mouth, but no words came out for several seconds, and the muscles in its neck remained tense... Finally, it answered in a hoarse voice.
"I don’t know..."
It pressed its fingers against the stone.
"It’s just... I feel that if that thing looks at me..."
Its sentence remained unfinished.
Lian waited, but the Sovereign could not continue, instead, it struggled to lower its head, its eyes still trembling.
"I don’t want to stay here." It said in a much quieter voice.
Lian looked at it for several seconds.
Then The Withered probably felt the same way.
He could now understand their reaction to some extent, they had been unusually terrified when they saw the sun.
Some had tried to return underground, while others had been unable to move from their places, and now, an intelligent Unholy-rank creature was showing a similar reaction.
This showed that the Hollow Sun’s effect on monster-like creatures could be much deeper than Lian had imagined.
"Do you know anything about this land or that sun? Even a legend or an old name?" he asked one last time.
"No... nothing..." Three shook its head with difficulty.
Then it continued in an almost pleading voice.
"Send me back."
The young Vorhelm did not insist any further.
He activated Colony Sovereign, and the monster’s enormous body turned into thousands of points of light, which disappeared a few moments later.
Three had returned to the Colony House.
Lian remained in the same place for a while, his gaze fixed on the sun’s black pupil.
So even an Unholy-rank creature can’t stand its presence.
This alone did not reveal the Hollow Sun’s true power.
But it was a serious warning.
He let out a calm breath, it seemed that the situation was more complicated and worse than any of them had thought.

Some had tried to return underground, while others had been unable to move from their places, and now, an intelligent Unholy-rank creature was showing a similar reaction.
This showed that the Hollow Sun’s effect on monster-like creatures could be much deeper than Lian had imagined.
"Do you know anything about this land or that sun?
Even a legend or an old name?" he asked one last time.
"No... nothing..." Three shook its head with difficulty.
Then it continued in an almost pleading voice.
"Send me back."
The young Vorhelm did not insist any further.
He activated Colony Sovereign, and the monster’s enormous body turned into thousands of points of light, which disappeared a few moments later.
Three had returned to the Colony House.
Lian remained in the same place for a while, his gaze fixed on the sun’s black pupil.
So even an Unholy-rank creature can’t stand its presence.
This alone did not reveal the Hollow Sun’s true power.
But it was a serious warning.
He let out a calm breath, it seemed that the situation was more complicated and worse than any of them had thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 631: Level 30 ( GT Bonus - )
paragraphs: He did not know how the Judgment System chose its targets.
And until he obtained more information, there was no reason to expose his subordinates to an unknown danger.
A few moments later, his communication device vibrated.
It was a message from the base.
"Rapid Response Unit, attention, a group of The Withered has been spotted moving within the eastern area, immediate support is required."
Lian took his eyes off the sun.
It seemed his break was over, so he headed toward the base.
When he reached the eastern area of the base, the first group of The Withered had already emerged from the cracks near the defensive position.
The guards were stationed on temporary platforms, and several mages stood behind them, ready to provide support, but unlike last night, no one was attacking the enemies without a clear plan.
Alaric’s orders were being sent to different sections through the communication devices.
"Unit Two, move twenty meters back, low-level personnel, stay away from the main route, and hold the enemies back until support arrives."
Several guards immediately changed their positions, and in the distance, a tall creature emerged from a crack.
Its body was covered in hard, black plates, and its two extremely long arms dragged along the ground as it moved.
[ Race: The Withered ]
[ Rank: Mutated ]
[ Level: 43 ]
The man immediately reported the information.
"Level 43 target! Approaching from the eastern section!"
Several guards with lower levels moved backward.
At that moment, Lian entered the battlefield from the side of the defensive position, keeping his eyes on the large creature.
Level 43.
Then he looked at several other Withered that were moving at a shorter distance.
Almost all of them were within the level range of the creatures he had fought before.
He simply quickened his steps.
The first Withered let out a rough growl when it saw Lian, its body bent forward, and its long claws moved toward the young Vorhelm.
Without stopping, Lian entered its attack range and threw his right fist forward.
Bang!
The creature’s head broke under the impact, and its body fell to the ground.
He did not even wait for it to fall completely.
The second Withered had approached from the right.
Lian took a short step toward it and punched the creature in the chest with his left fist, the sound of bones breaking rang out.
The Withered’s thin body was lifted off the ground and thrown several meters backward, and when it hit the ground, it no longer moved.
[ Level 34 Withered killed ]
[ Level 38 Withered killed ]
[ Exp received ]
He ignored the notifications.
Several meters away, three more creatures had emerged from the cracks.
One of them moved on all fours, while the other two had tall, human-like bodies.
But before they could reach the defensive forces, Lian stood in front of them.
The first creature leaped at him, but he struck its head with a direct punch.
The second tried to pass from the left, but he grabbed its wrist and struck its face with his other hand.
The third creature stopped for a moment, as if it wanted to choose another path after seeing its companions die.
But its body was still moving toward the defensive forces.
Lian closed the distance and punched the creature in the chest, a few moments later, all three were lying on the ground.
From behind the defensive position, one of the guards watched the scene in disbelief.
He had fought level 40 monsters before and knew that even experienced groups could be in danger when facing such creatures.
But the young man in front of him treated them like ordinary enemies.
Without using any powerful skills, without stopping to recover mana, and with almost no injuries, he slaughtered them.
The guard let out a quiet breath.
Is that really Lian Vorhelm?
He had heard the reports about Verendal and the recent events, but seeing such power up close was a completely different matter.
At that moment, the level 43 Withered reached Lian.
Its body was larger than those of the other creatures, and the hard plates on its shoulders made a dry sound as it moved.
The creature raised its right arm with a heavy movement.
Then it swung at the young Vorhelm’s head, but he caught its wrist.
The enormous limb stopped right there, and without the slightest change in his expression, Lian punched the middle of the creature’s chest with his right fist.
Bang!
The sound of hard plates cracking rang out.
The Withered took a step backward, but before it could completely lose its balance, Lian moved.
His second punch struck it directly in the face, the creature’s head bent backward, and its large body fell to the ground.
[ Level 43 Withered killed ]
[ Exp received ]
He had still not leveled up.
But considering the number of creatures he had killed since yesterday, he felt that he was not far from the next level.
Of course, in the current situation, the only issue was not hunting monsters, if the base was destroyed, many staff members and low-level personnel would lose their lives.
And he still needed these people’s resources and reports to gather information about the Hollow Sun.
So it was better not to let the creatures pass through the defensive line.
Farther away, another group of The Withered was moving toward the northern section of the eastern position.
This time, the guards had spotted them before they arrived.
"Four targets! Two level 35, one level 40, and one level 44!"
The voice of the officer in charge rang through the communication device.
Lian looked toward their location, the distance was not great, and he moved without delay.
The first Withered spread its long claws as he approached.
But he finished it with a direct punch to the head, the second tried to pass by his side, but Vorhelm blocked its path with a single step and punched it hard in the chest.
The third creature did not even get the chance to complete its attack.
Lian reached it with a quick movement and crushed its head with a direct punch, and finally, the level 44 Withered stood in front of him.
This one had a long, black body, and most of its face had no clear features.
Two faint lights shone from the upper part of its head.
The creature looked at Lian for a moment and then swung its long arm toward him.
The young Vorhelm only turned his body slightly, the claws passed by his shoulder, and at that very moment, his right fist struck the Withered’s head.
Bang!
The structure of the creature’s skull broke, its body fell to the ground, and before the final kill notification could even finish appearing, another window appeared in front of Lian.
[ Level Up! ]
Lian remained still for a moment, then a faint smile appeared on his face.
Finally.
After a long period of fighting and hunting, his level had finally reached thirty, and he was now one step closer to his second evolution.
He looked at his status for a moment, now he only had to keep this progress going.
The current Withered were suitable enemies, but it was still unclear what other creatures existed in the depths of the Land Of First Dawn.
Lian closed the window.
Then he looked toward the last part of the battlefield, where several more Withered were retreating.
Without hesitation, he used [ Corrupt Sun ], corrupted several lines of light in the sky with End Energy, and sent those lines of light toward the monsters.
The creatures that were fleeing from him were struck by the lines of light without even realizing they were under attack.
However, nothing loud happened, End Energy entered their bodies, and all the structures and organs inside their bodies reached their end... and stopped functioning.
[ You killed a level 27 Withered ]
[ You killed a level 31 Withered ]
[ You killed a level 43 Withered ]
[ You killed a ... ]
A few minutes later, Alaric contacted him through the communication device.
"Vorhelm, what’s the status of the eastern position?"
"It’s safe for now, all the creatures that attacked have been killed," Lian replied.
"Any injuries?"
"Among the forces in the area when I arrived, there are no new injuries, but a few people were already wounded."
"What about the ground?" The commander fell silent for a moment before asking.
Lian looked at the crack near the defensive position, the red glow of molten rock was still visible deep inside it.
"It’s still getting wider, if this continues, you should move the position farther back."
"Then we’ll prepare the second position, we’ll move the forces in stages."
Lian nodded.
"Okay."
The communication ended.

He looked at the crack for a moment, at least this commander understands that we can’t hold everything in place by force, in a situation like this, flexibility might be even more important than raw power.
Because The Withered were not the only problem, the ground beneath their feet had also become an enemy.
Over the following hours, the base went on alert several more times.
The lookouts reported the levels and locations of The Withered before they could get close.
Combat groups were assigned to suitable positions based on their abilities, while lower-level personnel were responsible for moving supplies or protecting the staff.
