chapters.title: Chapter 632: The Second Judgment ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: Rindo spent most of his time in the route coordination section.
By checking geological reports and the locations of the cracks, he identified several routes that were more likely to become unstable.
Noah also moved around different parts of the base with the rescue team.
His combat umbrella was sometimes used to repel attacks from The Withered, but he spent most of his time moving vulnerable staff members to safety and helping the support forces.
Lian observed both of them from a distance several times.
Rindo was still the same organized and serious person.
Even during emergencies, he rarely raised his voice and preferred to give information in a clear and brief manner.
Despite his friendly appearance, Noah also showed great focus during combat, he could switch from talking to a worried staff member to fighting an attacking Withered in an instant.
And after the danger had passed, he could return to helping the person in front of him with the same calm attitude as before.
Lian smiled for a moment.
These two are doing their jobs well too.
After all, he had more important problems to deal with, and as evening approached, the activity of The Withered around the base decreased slightly.
Of course, this did not mean the danger had passed.
Reports from more distant areas showed that mutated creatures were still emerging from different cracks.
Some groups had even spotted The Withered at level 45
However, there were still no signs of any creature that could directly threaten his current strength, which gave him a good opportunity to gain EXP.
But considering that almost twenty-four hours had passed since the first Judgment, he preferred not to move too far away from the main base.
He still did not know what would happen during the next Judgment.
Would only one person be chosen?
Or would there be several?
And would the Judge only condemn humans, or were mutated creatures also included in its judgments?
These questions remained unanswered.
Lian was standing near one of the central positions when Rindo and Noah joined him.
After checking the latest reports, Rindo placed his spear across his back.

"Most of the groups have returned, a few units are still operating in more distant areas, but they’ve been warned, however, some of the Chosen haven’t returned, and it’s unclear whether they’re still alive or have gone too far away."
Lian nodded.
"Good." Of the ten Chosen, only one had officially died so far, and including them, five were currently at the base.
Four others were also away from the base, they had received information about two of them being in distant areas, while there was no news about the other two.
One of those two missing people was Roderick.
Noah looked toward the sun.
"Who do you think it’ll choose this time?"
"We don’t know." Rindo answered without hesitation.
The young Frenchman looked at him for a moment before turning back to Lian.
"What do you think?"
Vorhelm placed his hands behind his back.
"We don’t even know whether only one person will be condemned each time."
Noah remained silent for several seconds, then his gaze returned to the golden ring in the sky.
"Then I hope what we saw yesterday was the worst it can do."
Lian did not answer, because there was no clear reason to hold such hope.
During the first Judgment, the Hollow Sun had chosen only Amelie.
But none of them knew whether this was a fixed rule or simply the result of that particular Judgment.
On the other hand, Three’s reaction when it saw the sun was still on his mind.
An Unholy-rank monster had become so terrified just by looking at the Judge that it could not even stand properly.
If such a creature was that afraid of the sun, then the Judge’s true power was probably far greater than anything they had seen so far.
This made Lian even more cautious about the next Judgment.
At that moment, Alaric approached them from among a group of nearby guards, he was checking the status of the central positions one last time.
When he reached the three Chosen, he gave them a brief look.
"Is everything ready?"
"The defensive groups are in their assigned positions." Rindo answered.
"The medical section and the wounded transfer teams are ready, and the non-combat staff have also been moved into the central area." Noah continued.
Alaric nodded and then looked at Lian.
"Vorhelm?"
"The Rapid Response Unit is ready."
The commander nodded and looked at the Hollow Sun for a moment, then he turned back to them.
"We still don’t know how the Judgment chooses its targets, so for now, no unit is allowed to leave the defensive area without orders."
He paused briefly.
"If the ground starts collapsing, keep the evacuation routes open, rescuing people is more important than holding our positions."
Rindo nodded.
Noah also gave a brief reply.
After receiving the latest reports, Alaric returned to the central section, while the three Chosen remained in their positions.
The final minutes passed slowly.
A gentle wind moved through the golden trees.
Farther away, hot steam rose from several cracks in the ground and cast shadows over parts of the plains.
The guards stood at their assigned positions, some held their weapons tightly, while others kept watching the Hollow Sun without stopping.
In the central area, the healers stood beside their equipment, and the Association staff waited for possible orders.
No one knew exactly what was about to happen, but everyone knew the time was near.
Lian checked his status for a moment.
[ Name: Lian Vorhelm ]
[ Level: 30 ]
[ First Evolution: Completed ]
He took a quick look at the information.
Over the past day, he had managed to increase his level and gain better control over his Corrupt Sun talent.
But none of these improvements had given him a way to stop the Judge’s sentence yet.
He closed the window.
His gaze turned toward the sky.
Almost twenty-four hours.
The Hollow Sun’s black pupil was still open, and the golden rings around it continued to move slowly.
But then, the birds stopped making sounds.
Lian immediately noticed the change, the golden trees that had been moving in the wind just moments ago became still.
The leaves remained in the same positions, and even the sounds of small insects disappeared from the grassland.
Rindo raised his head.
"It’s starting."
Noah tightened his grip on the handle of his folded umbrella, and at that moment, Alaric’s voice came through the base’s communication devices.
"All units, hold your positions."
No one moved.
Even the guards standing on the temporary towers turned their gazes toward the sky.
The young Vorhelm let out a calm breath.
It’s time for the second round.
At the center of the enormous golden ring, the Hollow Sun’s black pupil slowly narrowed, for a moment, it seemed as if the eye was closing.
But then the golden rings began to rotate, one clockwise and the other in the opposite direction.
Strands of light moved along their surfaces, and a huge light spread across the entire land.
Lian watched the scene without moving, he still did not know how the Judge would choose its next target.
But this time, he intended to observe every change in energy and every detail of how the Judgment began.
Perhaps he could find a new clue, and even if he could not stop the sentence, he could at least learn more about how it worked.
At that moment, the black pupil opened completely once again, but this time, unlike the previous day, its gaze was directed straight downward.
Toward the golden plains, toward the cracks in the ground, and toward all the creatures trapped within the enormous walls of the Land Of First Dawn.
For several seconds, complete silence filled the area.
Then the same enormous, emotionless voice rang out across the sky.
"The Second Judgment has begun."

But this time, he intended to observe every change in energy and every detail of how the Judgment began.
Perhaps he could find a new clue, and even if he could not stop the sentence, he could at least learn more about how it worked.
At that moment, the black pupil opened completely once again, but this time, unlike the previous day, its gaze was directed straight downward.
Toward the golden plains, toward the cracks in the ground, and toward all the creatures trapped within the enormous walls of the Land Of First Dawn.
For several seconds, complete silence filled the area.
Then the same enormous, emotionless voice rang out across the sky.
"The Second Judgment has begun."

chapters.title: Chapter 633: Guilty Before Today
paragraphs: "The Second Judgment has begun."
The enormous voice of the Hollow Sun spread across the entire Land Of First Dawn.

However, contrary to what everyone expected, nothing happened after the announcement, no beam of light descended from the sky, no explosion occurred, and not even the slightest change could be seen in the base’s defensive positions.
Only a heavy silence had settled over the surrounding plains, a silence so unnatural that even the sound of the guards’ armor seemed far too loud.
Lian had his head raised.
In the distant sky, the enormous golden rings rotated around a black pupil, and the sunlight still lit up the entire land, but it no longer had the calm and pleasant warmth of the first day.
It was as if every ray of light was part of the gaze of a being watching the entire land.
Around him, the guards stood with their weapons ready, and the staff of the Awakened Association stared at the sky with worry.
One young employee’s hands were clearly shaking, and every few seconds, he looked at himself, as if he expected the same golden light that had destroyed Amélie Moreau to appear on his body.
At that moment, Alaric’s voice came through the base’s communication devices.
"All units, hold your positions, no one moves without an order, and no one is allowed to launch an attack to test the Sun’s reaction, for now, just observe and report."
His voice was firm, without any sign of haste or fear.
Lian briefly glanced toward the central area.
The commander was standing in front of the large map of the base, although Alaric was only level 43 and had no power to fight the Sun directly, he could still perform a more important task.
Preventing the fear that might tear the base’s forces apart before the Judgment itself began.
He’s a good commander.
He looked at the sky again and activated \[True Sequence\].
The flows of mana became clearer to his perception, the surrounding energy was still pure and dense, but now, very faint strands of golden light were moving through different layers of the air.
He followed one of them for a few seconds and noticed a small difference, these strands were not simply passing by objects.
When they reached a living being, they reacted with the mana flowing around its body for a fraction of a second before continuing along their path.
They caused no damage and formed no permanent connections.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
"So it’s checking everyone," he murmured.

During the first Judgment, all his attention had been focused on trying to cut the connections attached to Amélie’s body and soul, and back then, he had no chance to examine the stages before those connections were formed.
But this time, no one had been chosen yet.
"So the identification stage is separate from the execution of the sentence," he said, although this was something he could have guessed.
However, he did not know exactly what the Sun was examining, perhaps people’s identities, the structure of their souls, or even information related to their past.
But at least one difference was clear.
The light moving through the surroundings was not yet the same complex and deadly structure that had brought about Amélie’s destruction the day before.
"Lian."
Noah’s voice caught his attention.
The young Frenchman was standing to his left, holding his folded combat umbrella.
"Look over there."
Lian turned his head.
A short distance away, the golden light had stopped over one of the young guards for a moment.
The man was holding a long spear, but when he noticed the light on his body, he stepped back in fear until his back hit the stone wall.
"No... I didn’t do anything..."
Just when it seemed that he could no longer control himself, the golden light passed through his body.
Nothing else happened.
The guard leaned against the wall, breathing in short, broken breaths.
Noah slowly breathed out.
"I thought it had chosen him."
The young Vorhelm continued to follow the flow of light.
"Not yet, this is different from what we saw when Amélie was executed."
Rindo was standing to their right, keeping his spear ready.
"Then I hope you can tell the difference when the next stage begins."
"That’s why I’m watching," Lian replied.
But at that very moment, the movement of the Sun’s pupil changed.
The golden rings slowed down, and the black pupil, which had been focused on the central area of the base until then, turned toward the cracked plain outside the defensive perimeter.
He noticed the change in the direction of the energy.
Has it chosen someone?
A few moments later, he got his answer.
About a hundred meters from the defensive line, a gray creature was sitting among several rocks.
One of The Withered.
Its body was nearly three meters tall, with extremely long arms and skin covered in deep cracks, its uneven mouth stretched almost to one corner of its face.
The creature had hidden its head between its two bony hands, it was neither approaching the human forces nor making any attempt to attack.
One of the guards outside checked the creature’s information.
[Race: The Withered]
[Rank: Mutated]
[Level: 32]
The man reported through the communication device.
"The target is a level 32 Withered, it hasn’t shown any aggressive behavior so far."
Lian saw the same information, but before he could examine any other changes in the flow of mana, the Judge’s voice sounded again.
"Previous identity identified."
He paused.
Previous identity?
The Sun’s voice continued.
"Sareven."
The gray creature remained motionless.
For several seconds, even its fingers did not move... then it slowly raised its head, and its uneven mouth opened and closed several times.
A hoarse sound came from its throat, and the creature placed its long fingers on its face.
It seemed to have heard a name that had once meant a great deal to it, but now, even remembering its full form was difficult.
Lian narrowed his eyes.
The system had identified the creature as one of The Withered, but the Hollow Sun apparently knew another identity it had once possessed.
An identity from before its mutation.
"So it really was a different creature before," another one of his guesses had been confirmed.
But how had the Judge been able to identify its previous identity?
Was it through the structure of its soul?
Or perhaps it had known the creature before?
The Sun’s next words did not give him time to think any further.
"First accusation: Violation of a previous order."
Upon hearing this sentence, the creature shook its head violently and tried to stand up.
"Second accusation: Leaving the designated area."
Sareven struggled to stand on its uneven legs, but almost immediately lost its balance and fell onto all fours.
However, it did not stop and began to crawl, heading straight toward a crack several meters away.
"Third accusation: Disobedience to the state of stillness."

The Judge’s voice did not change, it showed no anger, no satisfaction, and not even the slightest sign of paying attention to the condemned creature’s struggle, as if it was simply carrying out its task.
But when Lian heard the third accusation, he narrowed his eyes further.
The state of stillness?
This term was different from the accusations made against Amélie the day before.
Back then, the accusations had involved unauthorized entry, tampering with the containment structure, and taking property that belonged to the Mother.
But now, the Judge was talking about an old order, a designated area, and a state known as stillness.
So this creature was already under a sentence before today?
In front of him, Sareven continued dragging itself across the rocks.
For a moment, it turned its head toward the sky.
"Again... no..."
Then it increased its speed... but it was already too late.
"Sentence: Execution."
A golden beam descended from the sky, not like a normal attack, but as if the light already knew the condemned creature’s exact location before it even reached the ground.
Sareven tried to throw itself into the crack, but a ring of light continued to follow its body.
Lian immediately focused his attention on \[True Sequence\].
Several thin strands of light connected to the Withered’s body, and more complex paths immediately appeared, linking to Sareven’s soul structure.
The same structure I saw on Amélie.
He quickly examined the paths.
Some only acted as initial connections, but the main paths spread through the condemned creature’s very existence.
At the same time, Sareven had reached the edge of the crack, its fingers clung to the rocks, and part of its body had already moved down into the opening.
But before it could reach the darkness below, golden light appeared inside its body.
The creature opened its mouth.
For a fraction of a second, the light grew brighter, and something strange happened.
Within the light, the shadow of a different body appeared.
Not the three-meter-tall, distorted body, but a shorter form, with more normal proportions and a head that was not tilted to one side.
It was as if that was the Withered’s original form... or at least the appearance it had possessed in the past.
Lian immediately focused on the image, but before he could make out any more details, it disappeared.
Then—

chapters.title: Chapter 634: More Than One Condemned
paragraphs: Then Sareven’s body began to collapse from the inside.
Its long fingers separated from the rocks, and its physical structure disappeared among the golden strands without any noticeable explosion.
A few moments later, no trace of it remained.
But Lian still had his eyes fixed on the execution site.
Wait...
Not all the energy from the sentence had disappeared along with the condemned creature.
After the process ended, some of the golden strands moved downward.
Not toward the Sun, but toward the ground.
The strands passed through the surrounding rocks and went deep underground.
He tried to follow them, but their paths soon moved beyond the range of his perception.
"That same downward flow again," he frowned slightly.
Near the southern spring, some of the energy from the white roots had also moved downward after the Sun awakened.
During the previous day, he had also seen several other energy flows moving underground.
Now, after the sentence had been carried out, he had seen another flow moving in the same direction.
Does that mean the execution of a sentence isn’t only meant to destroy the target?
Perhaps some of the energy was being used in an underground structure, or it had a purpose that Lian did not know about yet.
Could it be related to the cracks in the ground and The Withered emerging from underground?
He recorded the location and timing of the energy’s movement in his mind.
"Finally, I found something new."
But before he could share his thoughts with the others, something else happened.
At the base, several people let out sighs of relief.
One of the young guards placed his hand on his chest.
"So this time, it wasn’t one of us..."
The man had not even finished his sentence when the Sun’s golden rings began to rotate again.
This time, the black pupil did not choose just one location.
Several thin strands of golden light spread in different directions, one toward the western forest, another toward the northern plains, and several more toward distant areas.
Then the same enormous, emotionless voice was heard.
"The remaining condemned have been identified."
Noah looked up at the sky.
"Wait..."
But before he could say anything else, the first report came through the base’s communication device.
"Northern unit! A Withered has been caught under the golden light!"
A few seconds later, another voice was heard.
"Western area reporting! One of the Mutated creatures has been chosen here too!"
Then came a third message.
"Two more targets have been identified in the distance! Both are under the Judgment beams!"
Noah looked at Lian.
"So it’s not just one person..."
"It never said it would only choose one person each time," the young Vorhelm replied without taking his eyes off the sky.
Rindo frowned.
"So the number of sentences isn’t limited to one person."
Lian nodded.
At the same time, several other Withered that had remained near the cracks began to react strongly.
One curled up on the ground, another placed its long hands over its head, and a four-legged creature crawled toward a crack while repeating the same words.
"Not me... not me..."
But none of them had been chosen as condemned targets yet.
It seems they know what happens next.
The memory of summoning Three came back to Lian’s mind.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign had also been terrified when it saw the Hollow Sun, even though it claimed that it had never seen that Sun before.
Perhaps the Judge’s very presence caused a special reaction in the creatures’ bodies, some kind of instinctive response.
Of course, it was still too early to draw a conclusion.
Lian turned his attention back to one of the condemned Withered near the western position.
The golden light was focused on a long creature with black skin that was trying to hide behind a rock.
This time, he decided to conduct a short experiment.
He kept \[True Sequence\] active and identified one of the secondary strands of the sentence.
Then he released a small amount of the power of Corrupt Sun.
A thin strand of the surrounding light darkened and followed a short reflected path until it reached the secondary strand of the sentence.
For a fraction of a second, the golden energy changed color, and part of its structure began to break down.
But a fresh flow of energy immediately entered from the main source and repaired the damaged strand.
Lian cut off his energy.
"Just as I expected."
He had managed to affect one of the secondary paths, but as long as the main flow continued to feed the structure with much greater power, local damage was not enough.
"So if I want to actually stop a sentence, I need to understand the main source, or at least find a way to cut its connection to the target."
A few moments later, the golden light grew stronger, and the Withered’s body collapsed from the inside.
This time, Lian also saw some of the remaining energy moving toward the ground.
Again.
This was no longer just an accidental observation.
In other areas, the sentences were also carried out.
Several Withered were destroyed in the north, and two more creatures were condemned in the west.
Reconnaissance teams in more distant areas also reported golden beams, but there were no confirmed reports of any other humans being executed.
Finally, the Sun’s golden rings began to slow down.
"The Second Judgment is complete."
Silence lasted for a few seconds, and then the next sentence was announced.
"Next Judgment: In twenty-four hours."
The golden light around the condemned targets disappeared, and the leaves of the trees began to move again.
It was as if only a brief natural event had occurred, but several more creatures had now disappeared from the land.
Lian slowly breathed out.
"So we have another day."
It was a strange feeling, not knowing whether they would still be alive tomorrow, yet having to enjoy the present day as if it were their last.
At least this time, he had gained more information.
The Judge could choose several condemned targets at the same time, identify the previous identities of The Withered, and send some of its energy deep underground after carrying out a sentence.
But he still had no way to save the next condemned target.
What kind of thing are you, really?
After the Judgment ended, a discussion slowly spread among the base’s staff.
"It didn’t choose any humans this time..."
"Maybe those creatures are its main targets."
"Could it be that it won’t bother us anymore?"
Lian heard part of these conversations.
What a quick conclusion.
Only one day earlier, Amélie had been executed in front of their eyes.
The fact that several Withered had been condemned did not mean that humans were safe.
At that moment, Alaric approached him.
"Vorhelm, did you notice anything?"
Lian nodded.

"A few things, first, the identification stage is different from the execution of the sentence, before a target is chosen, a weak flow of energy passes around the people, but after the selection, more complex structures connect to the condemned target’s body and soul."
"Can you tell who has been chosen before the sentence is issued?" the commander asked.
"Probably, once the main connection is formed, but I still don’t know how much time we have, and there probably isn’t much."
"What about cutting the connection?
"Not yet, I managed to stop one of the strands of light targeting the creature for a moment, but the main source repaired it much faster."
Lian paused briefly.
"There’s something else, after the sentence is carried out, some of the energy moves toward the ground, I’ve seen it twice."
Alaric paid closer attention.
"Where does it go?"

"I don’t know, but its direction is similar to the energy flows that, according to our investigations, move toward the inside of the ground, they might be related to the cracks and The Withered emerging from underground."
"Then we need to compare the geological reports with the times when the sentences were carried out."
"Exactly."
At that moment, one of the nearby officers approached.
"Commander, the initial Judgment reports are ready, all confirmed cases involved Mutated creatures."
Alaric took the report.
"Have we received responses from all areas?"
"No, we still haven’t been able to contact several units."
"Then we still can’t say that no humans have been condemned."
"Send out a notice, include only the confirmed results, I don’t want rumors about humans being immune spreading among the forces," he then told the officer.
"Understood."
The officer walked away.
Alaric looked at Lian again.
"Were today’s accusations related to Amélie’s accusations?"
"The wording was different, Amélie was accused of unauthorized entry, tampering with the containment structure, and taking property that belonged to the Mother."
Alaric frowned.
"The Mother?"
"That’s the exact term it used."
"And today?"
"Violation of a previous order, leaving the designated area, and disobedience to the state of stillness."
"It seems both sets of accusations refer to rules we don’t know about," the commander remained silent for a few seconds before adding.
Lian nodded.
The word "Mother" was still one of the strangest parts of the first Judgment, but now another term had been added to it.
Stillness.
He still did not know what the Judge meant by it, but at least he had more clues for his investigation.
He felt that he needed a book containing the rules and laws of the Hollow Sun, because the laws as understood by them and the laws of that Sun seemed to be completely different.
Just as Alaric was about to return, the warning sound of his communication device rang out.
"Commander! Emergency in the eastern section!"
"Report."
"The ground beneath the first position is sinking! The rate of collapse is increasing!"
"Is the second position ready?"
"Yes, Commander, but several people and some equipment are still at the first position."
"Begin the evacuation, abandon the heavy equipment," Alaric replied without hesitation.
"Commander, two defense units are still there, if we lose them—"
"I know what we’ll lose, get the troops out."
He ended the communication and looked at Lian.
"We might need the rapid-response force."
Lian nodded.
"I’m ready."
The eastern position was not far from the center of the base.
This area had been marked as one of the unstable locations since the previous day, and most of the troops and essential equipment had already been moved to the second position.
However, two large defense units and several metal boxes were still near the main platform.
After receiving the evacuation order, the guards began to retreat.

"So if I want to actually stop a sentence, I need to understand the main source, or at least find a way to cut its connection to the target."
A few moments later, the golden light grew stronger, and the Withered’s body collapsed from the inside.
This time, Lian also saw some of the remaining energy moving toward the ground.
Again.
This was no longer just an accidental observation.
In other areas, the sentences were also carried out.
Several Withered were destroyed in the north, and two more creatures were condemned in the west.
Reconnaissance teams in more distant areas also reported golden beams, but there were no confirmed reports of any other humans being executed.
Finally, the Sun’s golden rings began to slow down.
"The Second Judgment is complete."
Silence lasted for a few seconds, and then the next sentence was announced.
"Next Judgment: In twenty-four hours."
The golden light around the condemned targets disappeared, and the leaves of the trees began to move again.
It was as if only a brief natural event had occurred, but several more creatures had now disappeared from the land.
Lian slowly breathed out.
"So we have another day."
It was a strange feeling, not knowing whether they would still be alive tomorrow, yet having to enjoy the present day as if it were their last.
At least this time, he had gained more information.
The Judge could choose several condemned targets at the same time, identify the previous identities of The Withered, and send some of its energy deep underground after carrying out a sentence.
But he still had no way to save the next condemned target.
What kind of thing are you, really?
After the Judgment ended, a discussion slowly spread among the base’s staff.
"It didn’t choose any humans this time..."
"Maybe those creatures are its main targets."
"Could it be that it won’t bother us anymore?"
Lian heard part of these conversations.
What a quick conclusion.
Only one day earlier, Amélie had been executed in front of their eyes.
The fact that several Withered had been condemned did not mean that humans were safe.
At that moment, Alaric approached him.
"Vorhelm, did you notice anything?"
Lian nodded.

"A few things, first, the identification stage is different from the execution of the sentence, before a target is chosen, a weak flow of energy passes around the people, but after the selection, more complex structures connect to the condemned target’s body and soul."
"Can you tell who has been chosen before the sentence is issued?" the commander asked.
"Probably, once the main connection is formed, but I still don’t know how much time we have, and there probably isn’t much."
"What about cutting the connection?
"Not yet, I managed to stop one of the strands of light targeting the creature for a moment, but the main source repaired it much faster."
Lian paused briefly.
"There’s something else, after the sentence is carried out, some of the energy moves toward the ground, I’ve seen it twice."
Alaric paid closer attention.
"Where does it go?"

"I don’t know, but its direction is similar to the energy flows that, according to our investigations, move toward the inside of the ground, they might be related to the cracks and The Withered emerging from underground."
"Then we need to compare the geological reports with the times when the sentences were carried out."
"Exactly."
At that moment, one of the nearby officers approached.
"Commander, the initial Judgment reports are ready, all confirmed cases involved Mutated creatures."
Alaric took the report.
"Have we received responses from all areas?"
"No, we still haven’t been able to contact several units."
"Then we still can’t say that no humans have been condemned."
"Send out a notice, include only the confirmed results, I don’t want rumors about humans being immune spreading among the forces," he then told the officer.
"Understood."
The officer walked away.
Alaric looked at Lian again.
"Were today’s accusations related to Amélie’s accusations?"
"The wording was different, Amélie was accused of unauthorized entry, tampering with the containment structure, and taking property that belonged to the Mother."
Alaric frowned.
"The Mother?"
"That’s the exact term it used."
"And today?"
"Violation of a previous order, leaving the designated area, and disobedience to the state of stillness."
"It seems both sets of accusations refer to rules we don’t know about," the commander remained silent for a few seconds before adding.
Lian nodded.
The word "Mother" was still one of the strangest parts of the first Judgment, but now another term had been added to it.
Stillness.
He still did not know what the Judge meant by it, but at least he had more clues for his investigation.
He felt that he needed a book containing the rules and laws of the Hollow Sun, because the laws as understood by them and the laws of that Sun seemed to be completely different.
Just as Alaric was about to return, the warning sound of his communication device rang out.
"Commander!
Emergency in the eastern section!"
"Report."
"The ground beneath the first position is sinking!
The rate of collapse is increasing!"
"Is the second position ready?"
"Yes, Commander, but several people and some equipment are still at the first position."
"Begin the evacuation, abandon the heavy equipment," Alaric replied without hesitation.
"Commander, two defense units are still there, if we lose them—"
"I know what we’ll lose, get the troops out."
He ended the communication and looked at Lian.
"We might need the rapid-response force."
Lian nodded.
"I’m ready."
The eastern position was not far from the center of the base.
This area had been marked as one of the unstable locations since the previous day, and most of the troops and essential equipment had already been moved to the second position.
However, two large defense units and several metal boxes were still near the main platform.
After receiving the evacuation order, the guards began to retreat.

chapters.title: Chapter 635: The Base Is No Longer Safe
paragraphs: Several people left through the northern route, but before the second group could reach the alternative route, the old crack widened with a long, grinding sound.
Krrrrrk!
A large part of the main route collapsed.
The rocks fell into the depths, and hot steam rose from the crack. Several guards stepped back, but at that exact moment, the ground behind them also began to split apart.
"The route is blocked!"
When Lian and Alaric arrived, the eastern section had become a piece of land that was breaking away from both sides.
Red molten light could be seen deep inside the crack, and columns of hot steam rose between the rocks.
Alaric immediately contacted the officer in charge.
"How many people are still there?"
"Five people, Commander! Three guards and two staff members!"
"What’s the condition of the ground?"
"It’s unstable! We don’t know how long it will hold!"
"Keep the second route open, no one is going back to save the equipment."
At the same time, Lian looked at the crack.
It was wider than the crack he had covered with ice last night, and even more intense heat was rising from the depths.
Building a complete bridge here would only waste too much mana.
His previous experience had shown that the ice structure would not remain stable for long against this kind of heat.
So it was better to use another method.
"I’m going over there."
Alaric nodded.
"People come first, don’t go after the equipment."
"Don’t worry."
Two huge black wings spread out behind Lian.
Wings of God.
With one movement, Vorhelm’s body lifted off the ground and flew toward the eastern section.
When he landed, one of the guards was helping a staff member whose leg was trapped beneath a piece of rock.
Every time the guard tried to move the rock, the cracks around it spread further.
Lian approached them.
"Move back."
Then he placed both hands beneath the edge of the rock and lifted it without needing any special skill.
The staff member freed his leg, but he still could not stand properly.
"Can you move?"
The man nodded with difficulty.
"I think so..."
"You don’t need to."
Lian lifted him up, and a few seconds later, he handed him over to the healers on the safe side.
Then he immediately returned.
Four people remained.
But when he was about to carry the nearest guard to safety, one of the stone pillars beside the defense platform fell toward two of the staff members.
He changed his position, and his right fist struck the middle section of the pillar.
BANG!
The pillar broke into several large pieces, changing the direction of its fall.
However, the impact made the edge of the ground even more unstable.
Lian immediately lowered his hand.
\[Frost Dominion\]
Intense cold spread across the surface of the rock, but this time, instead of covering the entire crack, he focused the ice only on the connection between the broken edges.
Thick layers formed between the pieces of rock, and the ice structure held the damaged section in place like a temporary support.
This was much better.
He did not need to fill the entire width of the crack, he only needed to buy a few seconds.
"Move away from that side, stay close together so I can carry you over faster."
The guards immediately obeyed.
Lian first carried two people across with short flights, then returned for the next person, but when it was the last guard’s turn, the ground beneath the man suddenly dropped.
"Damn it!"
His body slipped past the edge, and at that very moment, Lian moved, his fingers closed around the guard’s arm, and the man hung in the air for a moment.
Several pieces of rock fell beside him and disappeared into the darkness.
Lian spread his wings with force.
A few seconds later, both of them landed on safe ground.
The guard was still breathing heavily.
"Th... thank you..."
"You’d better stay away from the edge."
The man immediately stepped back, and at that exact moment... KRRRAAAACK!
A large part of the eastern platform collapsed.
The ground, along with the two defense machines and the remaining equipment, fell downward and disappeared among the hot steam and red molten light.
Lian took a few steps away from the edge.
All five people had been rescued, and after checking the condition of the people, Alaric ordered the officer beside him.
"Remove the eastern area from the operational map, the second position will replace it from now on."
Then he looked at Lian.
"Good work."
"The ground here is more unstable than we thought, if the other routes become like this too, you’ll have to move the positions again."
At the rate the cracks were spreading, even the base might soon become unusable.
They had to find a way out as soon as possible.
"I know, we’ll probably have to change the plan before tomorrow ends."
Lian nodded.
Even if they defeated all the attacking Withered, no permanent base could remain safe forever in a land where the ground was breaking apart.
At that moment, the sound of a conversation came from the support storage area.
"I told you that shipment can still be moved." A young girl’s voice was cold and firm.
Lian turned his head.
Near one of the half-empty storage buildings, a girl with straight black hair that reached slightly below her shoulders was standing.
She wore a neat, dark combat outfit, and her dark blue eyes were fixed on a small map.
"The commander’s orders are clear, no one is going back into the danger zone to save equipment." The officer in front of her replied.
The girl raised her head.
"I didn’t ask for that either, the shipment is still inside the safe area, so why has the transfer team stopped?"
"The route near the storage building is becoming unstable."
"Which section? The southern route or the back route?"
"The southern route."
"Then the back route is still open."
The officer frowned.
"For now."
"That’s what I wanted to know from the beginning."
The girl lowered the map and then continued.
"Move the shipments near the exit through the back route, leave the rest behind, there’s no need for anyone to enter the section that’s collapsing."
Lian listened to the conversation for a moment.
This one isn’t bad either.
Instead of making pointless complaints, she was trying to find a practical solution based on the available information.
At that moment, she noticed Lian’s presence.
Her gaze stayed on him for a moment, as well as on the black wings that had not completely disappeared yet.
"Lian Vorhelm?"
"Yeah."
The girl closed the map.
"Myra Kessler, one of the representatives of the Twelve Ancient Guilds."
Her introduction was short and formal.
"Nice to meet you.
"You were over there just a few minutes ago, how much time do you think we have before the back route also becomes unstable?" Myra gave a slight nod.
Lian glanced at the route.
"I can’t give you an exact time, but the main cracks haven’t reached it yet."
"Then can we still move the shipments near the exit?"
"If it’s done quickly, probably, but if I were you, I wouldn’t go back for the boxes left over there."
"I’m not asking you to do that either." Myra nodded without showing any displeasure.
Then she turned back to the officer.
"Then only the shipments near the exit will be moved."
The transfer began.
Boxes containing mana recovery potions and medical supplies were taken out through the back route, and Myra personally recorded the number of shipments.
But just as the last group was about to leave, another tremor occurred.
One of the staff members lost his balance, and the box he was carrying fell to the ground.
Several glass containers rolled toward the crack, and the man tried to pick them up, but the ground near the edge began to split apart.
Myra immediately grabbed his arm and pulled him back.
Several containers fell into the crack.
"I’m sorry..."
The man looked down with a pale face.
"Can you walk?" Myra asked.
"Then move."
The man took a few steps back.
"Those were really expensive..."
She looked at the crack for a moment.
"I know."
She brushed the dirt off her sleeve.
"But if you had gone back to pick them up and died, we would have lost both the medicine and one of our people, but now we’ve only lost the medicine."
"Thank you." The staff member lowered his head.
Myra did not reply and ordered the person in charge of the transfer to close the route.
Lian watched the scene from a short distance away.
She’s cold and calculating.
But that did not mean she was indifferent to people’s lives, the girl preferred to make her decisions based on reality, even when the result was losing valuable resources.
Myra turned toward him again.
"You’re still here?"
"Is that a problem?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"No, I just thought you’d leave for your next mission."
"There’s nothing yet."
"Then there probably will be soon." She kept her gaze on him.
Lian gave a short laugh.
"I hope it takes at least a few minutes."
But the girl did not even smile.
"With the ground in this condition, I doubt it."
Then she walked toward the central area without continuing the conversation.
The young Vorhelm watched her leave for a moment.
She’s an interesting person.
Even when speaking with him, Myra had kept the same direct tone she used with the Association officer.
And that was not a bad thing in Lian’s eyes.
In the base’s medical area, several injured guards were resting on temporary beds.
He had gone there for a quick check to see if they needed anything.
But as he passed one of the tables, a short laugh caught his attention.
"If you keep this up, you’ll destroy all the medicine in the base before the Sun kills us."

A young man with light-colored hair and blue eyes was sitting on the edge of the table, he had a slim, well-trained body and wore a dark combat outfit whose high-quality fabric and stitching were easy to notice.
In front of him, one of the female staff members was trying to move several medical containers at the same time.

chapters.title: Chapter 636: The Sun Must Die
paragraphs: Just as one of the containers fell from the edge of the box, the light-haired young man moved his index finger.
Several thin, semi-transparent lines appeared in the air and formed a geometric angle.
Then, instead of hitting the ground, the falling container changed its path and landed inside the empty box on the table.
Tap.
He smiled.
"See? Even the medicine knows where it should go, only you still don’t know."
"If you’re so good at this, why don’t you help me yourself?" The female staff member looked at him with a tired expression.
"I am helping, didn’t I just stop that from breaking?"
"I mean, get up and move the boxes!"
The young man let out a short sigh and jumped down.
"Fine, fine, there’s no need to get so angry."
Lian watched the scene for a few seconds.
Strange magic.
The container had not stopped; only its direction of movement had changed.
This meant that instead of using a common element like wind or water, the young man had directly affected the path of the force acting on the object.
At the same time, the young man noticed Lian looking at him.
"Oh, we have a famous guest." He placed one of the boxes on the table.
"Lian Vorhelm, right?"
"Yeah."
"I’m Mathieu Renaud, from the French National Academy."
"You’ve probably heard of me." He continued with a confident smile.
Lian thought for a moment.
"No."
Mathieu stared at him for a few seconds, then let out a short laugh.
"Great, finally someone I don’t have to meet any expectations for."
The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile, thinking about the mana lines he had seen a few moments ago.
"Vector Magic?"
"Oh? You recognized it?" Mathieu looked surprised.
"You changed the container’s path, but its speed didn’t completely disappear."
"Exactly."
Then he spun one of the containers between his fingers.
"Most people think mages have to create fire or bring lightning down from the sky, but I prefer to use a force that already exists instead of creating a new one."
He threw the container into the air.
When it began to fall, two mana lines appeared and changed its path, making the container land in Mathieu’s other hand.
"Direction of movement, amount of force, angle of impact... These are simple things, but if you use them correctly, they can become very interesting."
"Then can you redirect any attack?" Lian asked.
He laughed.
"If I could redirect any attack, I wouldn’t be here waiting for the Sun’s Judgment right now." Then he continued in a slightly more serious tone.
"To change the direction of any force, I need to spend enough mana and have time to form its structure, if the pressure is too great or I can’t measure it correctly, my calculations fall apart."
Lian nodded.
That makes sense.
Vector Magic seemed to be Mathieu’s special ability, a non-elemental method that changed the direction and way a force was transferred instead of directly creating force.
Despite its limitations, such an ability could be very dangerous in a battle between Awakened of the same level.
"By the way, are you looking for someone?" Mathieu asked after placing the last box on the table.
"I came to check on the medical area and see if they needed anything." The medical area had been set up by Alaric’s order.
Previously, there had been no need for such a place in the Land Of First Dawn because there were no monsters that could harm the Awakened there, but that had changed since yesterday.
And since the medical area had only been set up a few hours ago, he wanted to see if they needed anything.
"We don’t need anything, since we already collected a lot of medicinal plants, there’s no need for anything else."
Mathieu fell silent for a moment, then his smile faded slightly.
"Anyway, there’s something else I wanted to ask."
"What?"
The young Frenchman looked at the medical containers.
"Amélie... You spent her last day with her, right?"
"Most of the day." Lian nodded.
Mathieu gave a short, bitter smile.
"You know, she was very happy on the first morning."
He spun one of the empty containers between his fingers.
"Ever since she heard about the mission, she kept talking about the medicinal plants here, she had even prepared a few medicine formulas so she could test them when she found the samples."
"She found some good plants." Lian replied softly.
Mathieu raised his head.
"Really?"
"Yeah, she even gave some of them to me and my friend."
The young Frenchman slowly breathed out.
"That’s just like her."
Silence fell for a few seconds.
"Whenever she found something interesting, before using it herself, she would look for someone who might have a better use for it."
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"I often told her that if she kept doing that, she would end up with nothing left for herself."
"It seems she already knew the answer." The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile.
"What?"
"She said that if she couldn’t save everyone, she would start with someone she could help."
Mathieu looked at Lian for a few seconds, then let out a very short laugh.
"Yeah... That’s exactly what she would say."
Lian thought about his storage space for a moment, then took something out of it.
The medicinal plant that Amélie had personally given him beside the spring.
Mathieu took the plant and examined it closely.
"This... It looks like a medicinal plant, judging by its shape, I guess it’s something rare, she probably wanted to use it to make a better healing medicine."
"I know."
"She always loved mixing medicinal plants to make something better, I argued with her a few times because doing that could make the final result less stable."
"And who was right?" Lian asked.
Mathieu shrugged.
"We still don’t know, we were supposed to test it when she came back to see who was right."
For a few seconds, neither of them spoke.
"If you want, you can keep it." The young Vorhelm finally said.
Mathieu immediately shook his head.
"No. She gave it to you."
He handed the plant back.
"Keep it, maybe one day it’ll really be useful to you."
Lian put it back into his storage space.
The young Frenchman remained silent for a while, then asked without looking directly at Lian.
"When they sentenced her... Was she very scared?"
Lian paused.
Mathieu was not trying to blame anyone, he only wanted to know what the final moments of someone he had known had been like.
"Yeah... It was natural for her to be scared."
Mathieu’s fingers tightened around the edge of the table for a moment.
"But she was still thinking about the others until the very end." Lian continued.
The young Frenchman lowered his head.
"That’s also... just like her."
Vorhelm did not add anything else, there was no need.
After a while, Mathieu took a deep breath, and when he raised his head again, some of his earlier playful expression had returned.
"Well, I think if Amélie were here and saw me wasting my time feeling sad, she would scold me badly."
He gave a small smile.
"She would probably say that so many injured people are waiting, and I’m still sitting here thinking about myself."
"Then you’d better get back to work." Lian nodded.
"Exactly."
He picked up one of the medicine boxes, but before leaving, he turned around.
"Lian."
"Hmm?"
"If you ever find out how to kill that thing in the sky..."
He paused, and his gaze grew colder for a moment.
"Let me know."
Lian nodded.
"Of course."
Mathieu gave a small smile and walked toward the treatment area.
The young Vorhelm watched him leave.
A talented mage, fast, smart... and apparently, he also liked making himself seem less capable than he really was.
But more importantly, Mathieu now had a personal reason to learn more about the Hollow Sun.
As night approached, Alaric gathered the people in charge of the main groups and the present Chosen Ones in the command building to review the situation on the second day.
A large map of the land was placed on the table.
Red markers showed the locations of new cracks, blue markers showed relatively stable routes, and black markers showed the locations where the Withered had been seen.
Lian was standing beside Rindo.
Noah was on the other side, and Myra Kessler stood beside the map with a serious expression.
Mathieu was leaning against the wall a little farther away, spinning one of the small map markers between his fingers.
Five Chosen Ones.
Of the ten people who had entered the land two days ago, Amélie was dead, and the other four had still not returned.
The situation of two of them was not even roughly known.
Alaric began the meeting.
"First, the condition of the ground."
One of the officers moved the map of the eastern section forward.
"Position One has been completely destroyed, the alternative route is still stable, but the cracks in the southeast are spreading."
"If this continues, how much time do we have?"
"We can’t say exactly, some cracks remain stable for several hours, then spread rapidly within a few minutes."
"Then we won’t keep any position based on an estimated time." Alaric nodded.
Rindo pointed to a section of the map.
"Two of our current routes also lie along the northern fault lines, they might be damaged and collapse at the same time."
After reviewing the situation, the commander ordered another backup route to be prepared for the emergency transfer of injured people.
Then it was time to discuss resources.
Myra placed a report on the table.
"Our supplies of healing medicine and mana recovery medicine are enough for the current situation, we even have more than we need, but today we lost several boxes of medicine and two defense arrays."
One of the officers sighed.
"Those arrays will be difficult to replace."
Myra looked at him, then added.
"I know. But losing them now is better, we should make our plans based on what we still have."
"What do you suggest?" Alaric asked.
"We shouldn’t limit the use of medical supplies yet, injured people who aren’t fully healed will leave us with fewer fighters to defend the base."

sentences.text: Just as one of the containers fell from the edge of the box, the light-haired young man moved his index finger.
Several thin, semi-transparent lines appeared in the air and formed a geometric angle.
Then, instead of hitting the ground, the falling container changed its path and landed inside the empty box on the table.
Tap.
He smiled.
"See?
Even the medicine knows where it should go, only you still don’t know."
"If you’re so good at this, why don’t you help me yourself?" The female staff member looked at him with a tired expression.
"I am helping, didn’t I just stop that from breaking?"
"I mean, get up and move the boxes!"
The young man let out a short sigh and jumped down.
"Fine, fine, there’s no need to get so angry."
Lian watched the scene for a few seconds.
Strange magic.
The container had not stopped; only its direction of movement had changed.
This meant that instead of using a common element like wind or water, the young man had directly affected the path of the force acting on the object.
At the same time, the young man noticed Lian looking at him.
"Oh, we have a famous guest." He placed one of the boxes on the table.
"Lian Vorhelm, right?"
"Yeah."
"I’m Mathieu Renaud, from the French National Academy."
"You’ve probably heard of me." He continued with a confident smile.
Lian thought for a moment.
"No."
Mathieu stared at him for a few seconds, then let out a short laugh.
"Great, finally someone I don’t have to meet any expectations for."
The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile, thinking about the mana lines he had seen a few moments ago.
"Vector Magic?"
"Oh?
You recognized it?" Mathieu looked surprised.
"You changed the container’s path, but its speed didn’t completely disappear."
"Exactly."
Then he spun one of the containers between his fingers.
"Most people think mages have to create fire or bring lightning down from the sky, but I prefer to use a force that already exists instead of creating a new one."
He threw the container into the air.
When it began to fall, two mana lines appeared and changed its path, making the container land in Mathieu’s other hand.
"Direction of movement, amount of force, angle of impact...
These are simple things, but if you use them correctly, they can become very interesting."
"Then can you redirect any attack?" Lian asked.
He laughed.
"If I could redirect any attack, I wouldn’t be here waiting for the Sun’s Judgment right now." Then he continued in a slightly more serious tone.
"To change the direction of any force, I need to spend enough mana and have time to form its structure, if the pressure is too great or I can’t measure it correctly, my calculations fall apart."
Lian nodded.
That makes sense.
Vector Magic seemed to be Mathieu’s special ability, a non-elemental method that changed the direction and way a force was transferred instead of directly creating force.
Despite its limitations, such an ability could be very dangerous in a battle between Awakened of the same level.
"By the way, are you looking for someone?" Mathieu asked after placing the last box on the table.
"I came to check on the medical area and see if they needed anything." The medical area had been set up by Alaric’s order.
Previously, there had been no need for such a place in the Land Of First Dawn because there were no monsters that could harm the Awakened there, but that had changed since yesterday.
And since the medical area had only been set up a few hours ago, he wanted to see if they needed anything.
"We don’t need anything, since we already collected a lot of medicinal plants, there’s no need for anything else."
Mathieu fell silent for a moment, then his smile faded slightly.
"Anyway, there’s something else I wanted to ask."
"What?"
The young Frenchman looked at the medical containers.
"Amélie...
You spent her last day with her, right?"
"Most of the day." Lian nodded.
Mathieu gave a short, bitter smile.
"You know, she was very happy on the first morning."
He spun one of the empty containers between his fingers.
"Ever since she heard about the mission, she kept talking about the medicinal plants here, she had even prepared a few medicine formulas so she could test them when she found the samples."
"She found some good plants." Lian replied softly.
Mathieu raised his head.
"Really?"
"Yeah, she even gave some of them to me and my friend."
The young Frenchman slowly breathed out.
"That’s just like her."
Silence fell for a few seconds.
"Whenever she found something interesting, before using it herself, she would look for someone who might have a better use for it."
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"I often told her that if she kept doing that, she would end up with nothing left for herself."
"It seems she already knew the answer." The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile.
"What?"
"She said that if she couldn’t save everyone, she would start with someone she could help."
Mathieu looked at Lian for a few seconds, then let out a very short laugh.
"Yeah...
That’s exactly what she would say."
Lian thought about his storage space for a moment, then took something out of it.
The medicinal plant that Amélie had personally given him beside the spring.
Mathieu took the plant and examined it closely.
"This...
It looks like a medicinal plant, judging by its shape, I guess it’s something rare, she probably wanted to use it to make a better healing medicine."
"I know."
"She always loved mixing medicinal plants to make something better, I argued with her a few times because doing that could make the final result less stable."
"And who was right?" Lian asked.
Mathieu shrugged.
"We still don’t know, we were supposed to test it when she came back to see who was right."
For a few seconds, neither of them spoke.
"If you want, you can keep it." The young Vorhelm finally said.
Mathieu immediately shook his head.
"No.
She gave it to you."
He handed the plant back.
"Keep it, maybe one day it’ll really be useful to you."
Lian put it back into his storage space.

Was she very scared?"

chapters.title: Chapter 637: Domain Of The Condemned
paragraphs: She pointed at the storage areas on the map.

"But the defensive equipment needs to be moved away from unstable areas, I also suggest keeping some essential supplies at the second location, if the ground beneath the main storage area breaks apart, we shouldn’t lose everything at once."
"We’ll create two separate storage locations." Alaric agreed after a few seconds.
Myra nodded.
Lian looked at her for a moment, she really didn’t seem like someone who made decisions based on emotions, and this trait was valuable in the current situation.
Alaric pointed at another part of the map.
"Now, the missing Chosen Ones... Of the four who haven’t returned yet, we have the approximate locations of two, the latest reports show that they were moving toward safer routes."
"What about the other two?" Rindo asked.
"We still haven’t received any confirmed information."
Noah frowned.
"Then we should send a rescue team."
"The routes are unstable, more people might get trapped." One of the officers disagreed.
Noah looked at him.
"But if we wait, there might not be another chance to save them."
"Both concerns are valid, we need to determine their possible locations first." Alaric raised his hand.
Mathieu, who had been silent until then, stepped closer.
"If we also have the time of their last communication, we can use their movement speed and the routes they can travel through to identify several possible areas."
He pointed at the map with his finger.
"Of course, that’s assuming the ground is still the same as it is on the map."
He gave a short smile.
"Which, unfortunately, it isn’t."
"Prepare the information." Alaric agreed.
At the same time, Lian pointed at several red markers on the map.
"Commander, I want the locations of the new cracks, the direction of the underground mana flow, and the movements of the Withered to be marked on the same map."
"All three?" One of the officers asked.
"Yeah. They might be connected, today, during the Judgment, I saw some of the Judgment energy enter the ground, and I had seen similar downward flows in other places."
Then he pointed at the cracks.
"Some of the cracks also follow clear paths, if these flows are connected, we might be able to figure out which areas will change first."
"I also noticed that the direction in which some cracks spread isn’t random." Rindo nodded.
"And the Withered?" Alaric asked.
"They appeared almost at the same time the Sun awakened, I want to know whether their movements are random or not."
"So you want to put three sets of incomplete information together and see if anything comes out of it." Mathieu smiled.
"Exactly."
"It’s not a bad method, there might be an important factor we haven’t noticed yet."
"Assuming there really is a connection." Myra said without taking her eyes off the map.
Lian gave a slight smile.
"That’s why we need to investigate it."
Alaric finally ordered the information to be recorded on a shared map.
"But no one is sending troops into a dangerous area based on an unconfirmed pattern."
"I agree." Lian nodded.
He still did not know what was hidden deep inside the land, but at least now he could gather the information needed to investigate it.
After the meeting, Myra went to check the transfer of supplies, and Mathieu returned to the medical area.
Rindo also began organizing the route reports.
Lian remained beside the map for a while, only two days had passed since they entered.
He had increased his level and learned new ways to use the Corrupt Sun’s power, but he still did not know the true purpose of that massive structure.
"At least now I know what I need to look for."
Then he left the building, the second night was quieter than most people had expected, but quiet did not mean safe.
Red molten light could still be seen through the distant cracks, and sometimes the sound of shifting rocks echoed across the plains.
However, the direct attacks from the Withered on the base had decreased.
As he passed one of the watchtowers, he saw Noah sitting on the wooden platform, his war umbrella was beside him, and he was looking at the Hollow Sun.
When he saw Lian, he smiled.
"Haven’t you rested yet?"
"Later."
"I think I’ve heard you give that answer several times since yesterday." Noah laughed.
"We still have work to do."
Lian stood beside the platform’s railing.
"You know, when I first met you at Base #3, I thought you would be a very different person." They both remained silent for a while before the young Frenchman spoke.
"What kind of person?"
"Maybe someone more arrogant, someone who thinks he doesn’t need to work with others just because he comes from a great family."
"Did I disappoint you?" The corner of Lian’s mouth rose.
Noah laughed.
"Not exactly. I just didn’t expect someone as powerful as you to spend so much time defending an emergency base."
"Why?"
"Because even if this base is destroyed, you could probably still survive on your own."
Lian thought for a moment.
"Maybe." In fact, this was a reasonable argument, he did not want to be arrogant, but he had no doubt that even if every human in the Land Of First Dawn was killed, he could survive on his own.
In fact, he could also leave this place whenever he wanted.
He opened the system panel and clicked on the ability.
[Do you wish to leave the Ruined Realm?]
Without hesitation, he clicked Yes, even if he left, he could return whenever he wanted, and this way, he could inform the Federation and the Academy about what had happened to them.
[Exit permission denied]
[Exit permission denied]
[Exit permission denied]
[Leaving the Domain Of The Condemned is impossible without being cleared of all charges]
Lian frowned deeply, this was the first time something like this had happened, and he had no idea what it meant, he tried several more times, but the result did not change.
Cleared of all charges?
He looked at the Hollow Sun, did this mean that he could not leave until the Sun declared them innocent?
And the Domain Of The Condemned? The system had called this place the Domain Of The Condemned?
’Now that I think about it, the Land Of First Dawn is a name the Awakened gave this place, so is this its real name?’
And as far as he could remember, the Sun had also listed entering the Domain Of The Condemned as one of Amélie’s crimes.
Whatever the reason was, it seemed he had to make new plans from the beginning.
"Is something wrong?" Noah asked when he noticed Lian’s long silence.
"No." Lian shook his head and continued their conversation.

"This base has resources, equipment, and people who can be useful to me, Alaric has command experience, Rindo can investigate the routes, and the others are gathering information that I can’t obtain on my own."
He looked at the golden wall on the horizon.
"If the base is destroyed, my own situation will also get worse. So protecting it is the more logical choice."
"That was a very calculating answer." Noah smiled.
"I prefer my decisions to have a reason." The young Vorhelm shrugged.
"I think that’s what helps you make fewer mistakes in difficult situations."
"Not always."
"Well, at least you know that yourself." The young Frenchman laughed.
Then he looked at the Sun.
"To be honest, I’ve always tried to get to know more people."
"I noticed."
"Is it that obvious?"
"You’ve talked to almost everyone at the base."
Noah smiled.
"I think when you get to know someone, it becomes harder to see them as just a name on a report."
His tone became a little calmer.
"I’ve known some of the people here since the first morning, now I know they have families, they’ve just started their jobs, or they only wanted to work here for a few days and then return home."
His gaze moved toward the medical area.
"That makes me not want to see their names added to the casualty report."
Lian looked at him for a moment, at least from what he showed, Noah seemed to truly value getting to know others.
"Then we’d better help keep fewer names off that report."
"Yeah. Exactly." The young Frenchman gave a warmer smile.
A while later, Ed stood up and picked up his umbrella.
But just as he was about to place it over his shoulder, his free hand briefly moved toward his side.
It was a quick, unconscious movement, as if he wanted to draw another weapon from that spot, but his hand stopped before reaching it, and he placed the folded umbrella over his shoulder.
Lian noticed the movement.
That habit again.
Ever since their encounter with the Black Vultures, he had noticed that some of Noah’s movements did not fully match the way he used his umbrella.
On the other hand, the young Frenchman’s skill with that weapon was truly impressive, perhaps his fighting style had been formed by combining several different methods.
Such a thing was not unusual among talented Awakened.
Lian put the matter aside.
"Are you going to rest?"
"Probably. But first, I want to check on a few people in the support section, anyway, you should get some rest too."
"Later."
"That same answer again."
Then he went down from the platform.
Lian watched him leave for a moment, over these two days, Noah had proven that his presence could be useful to the group.
More importantly, working with him had gradually become more natural.
A while later, he also returned to the command building, Rindo was still examining the map, and several new lines had been drawn in the western and northern sections.
"Did you find anything?"
"Maybe." Rindo raised his head, then pointed at one of the routes.
"Several groups of Withered were spotted in different areas since this morning, most of them didn’t attack the humans, they were just moving."
"In which direction?"
Rindo traced the lines with his finger.
"This group moved from north to south, that one moved from west to east."
Then he pointed at the third marker.
"But when I extend their paths, their overall directions start to look similar."
Lian examined the map, the lines started from different points, but many of them gradually moved closer to the same area.
"Do you also have the information about the new cracks?"
"Yeah."
"Add them."
Rindo marked several red locations.
The young Vorhelm examined the map for a few seconds.
Interesting.
Most groups of Withered were not simply following the nearest crack, some had even passed open cracks and continued moving without entering them.
So they’re not just looking for a way back underground.
If this pattern continued, many of their routes would lead toward a common area.
The center and deepest point of the Land Of First Dawn.
Of course, the central area had not been fully mapped yet, but the way the creatures’ paths were coming together could not be ignored.
"When did these movements begin?"
"Most reports came in after the second Judgment."
After the second Judgment...
Had the execution of the sentences changed the Withered’s behavior? Or had something else happened at the same time as the Judgment?
It was still unclear.
But one thing was clear, the Withered were moving with a purpose.
"Looks like we’ve finally found a route worth investigating."
