chapters.title: Chapter 645: The Broken Paradise
paragraphs: Lian stared at the communication device in his hand for several seconds.

No sound could be heard from the other side of the device anymore, not the shouts of the base staff, not Alaric’s orders, and not even the faint static that usually remained when the connection was interrupted.
Rindo stood beside him and tried to reconnect using his own device, but the result was the same every time.
"They’re not answering." He finally lowered the device and looked at the Hollow Sun. "Alaric said several people had been selected. And then that sound..."
He did not finish his sentence.
Lian was still looking at the black pupil in the center of the huge golden rings.
From his current distance, he could not identify the exact location of the condemned people, but the Judge’s gaze was still directed toward the area where the base was located.
"At least four people." Lian finally said.
Rindo looked at him.
"What?"
"Alaric first said three people, then he noticed that another person had been selected, of course, there could be even more."
Rindo tightened his fingers around the shaft of his spear.
Both of them had seen the fate of Amélie Moreau.
They knew what being selected by the sun could mean, and even the most powerful Awakened in this land had still not found a way to stop its judgment.
"Do you think Alaric managed to do something?" He asked in a low voice.
Lian did not answer for a few moments.
Yesterday, he had only managed to damage one of the smaller energy threads of the judgment structure for a fraction of a second, the main energy flow had repaired it almost immediately.
Even if Alaric gathered all his forces, it would be impossible.
But perhaps they had found time to evacuate, or maybe the forces had been moved to other positions before the judgment began.
"No, but I’m not going to stand here and keep guessing."
Rindo noticed the change in his expression.
"You want to go back?"
"Yeah."
"Then I’m coming too."
Lian shook his head.
"No. This time, it’s better if I go alone."
His friend frowned, but before he could protest, the young Vorhelm pointed toward the broken plain behind them.
"We’ve traveled almost a full day away from the base, and most of the paths we used this morning don’t exist anymore, if I have to carry you too, my speed will decrease."
He looked toward the horizon.
"Even at my maximum flying speed, it’ll probably take me two hours to get there, by then, it might already be too late."

Rindo remained silent for a moment, but in the end, he nodded and took a breath, he could understand the situation, he just did not like the thought that something terrible might have happened to the base.
Before leaving, Lian activated [Hive Dominion].
The space a few steps away changed for a moment, and the huge body of the Eight-Disaster Wolf appeared from streams of light.
Two.
Its large paws touched the rocky ground, and the weight of its body caused several small stones to fall from the edge of the cliff.

The wolf lowered its head toward its master, its body was larger than most of the creatures Rindo had seen during the mission, and the powerful muscles in its legs were clearly visible even while it was standing still.
"Did you get this one recently?" He had seen that huge ant in the Special Area before, but this one seemed new.
"Yeah, not too long ago."
The wolf moved its ears, but its attention did not remain on Rindo for long, because at that exact moment, it raised its head and saw the Hollow Sun.
For several seconds, its huge body remained almost completely still.
Its ears moved slightly backward, and the muscles along its back tightened.
A short, deep growl came from its throat, but unlike Three, it did not fall to its knees, and there were no signs of fear strong enough to stop it from moving.
Two turned its gaze away from the black pupil.
Then it looked at Lian again.
Through the Colony connection, its master felt a faint sense of unease; something between caution and worry.
"So you can feel something too."
But the difference between its reaction and that of the Dreadmaw Sovereign was very clear.
Three could not even bear to look at the sun, while Two was still calm enough to examine its surroundings and wait for orders.
Lian placed his hand on the wolf’s huge neck.
"Take care of Rindo until I return, if the ground here becomes unstable, take him somewhere safer."
The wolf lowered its head slightly.
"I can protect myself too." Rindo looked between the two of them.
"I know, but when you have a Level 40 wolf beside you, why make everything harder?"
Rindo sighed, but this time, he did not continue arguing.
Lian took a few steps back, and two huge black wings opened behind him.
"If I find anything and communication starts working again, I’ll let you know, but if I can’t contact you, stay around here, I don’t want to have to search for you too when I get back."
"Take care of yourself." His friend nodded and then added.
The young Vorhelm gave a faint smile.
"You too."
Then his wings moved with great force.
A wave of wind and dust spread across the rock, and he quickly flew toward the sky.
A few seconds later, only a black figure could be seen in the distance.
Rindo watched his flight path for a while.
Two stood beside him, moving its gaze between the sky and the broken plain.
Then he looked at the Hollow Sun, the golden rings were still rotating.
They were beautiful.
Even now, in a land where another part of the ground was collapsing every moment, the sunlight created a magnificent view.
But Rindo could no longer see it as beautiful, that beautiful thing was actually a killing machine.
Lian was flying at his maximum speed.
Warm air passed beside his body, and the strong wind created by the movement of his wings pushed away some of the steam floating along his path.
At first, he planned to follow the approximate route they had taken over the past few days, but only a few minutes were enough for him to realize that doing so was useless.
The land was no longer the same land they had crossed that morning.
Cracks that had previously been only a few meters wide had now turned into huge valleys.
Parts of the golden forests had collapsed along with thick layers of soil and stone, and in some areas, giant white roots were hanging from the walls of the cliffs.
Molten rock was flowing in the depths.
Sometimes the steam became so thick that he could not see the ground below even from his current height.
He moved his wings and gained more altitude.
"The situation is much worse than I thought."
But what caught his attention the most was the way the ground was collapsing.
In some areas, huge sections of the plain had almost completely disappeared, while several kilometers away, rocky platforms still remained relatively intact.
Inside some of the cracks, parts of old structures could also be seen; thick walls, broken pillars, and paths that had previously been hidden underground.
He could stop to examine them, but now was not the time for that.
Lian increased his speed.
After some time, he flew over an area where a small spring had once been located.
He recognized the location for a moment, it was one of the paths he had crossed with Rindo and Amélie on the first day.
When Amélie had seen the plants around the spring, she had stopped for a few minutes and talked about their healing properties.
Now, neither the spring nor the plants remained, that entire area had turned into a huge crack.
He looked down for a moment and then flew over it without slowing down.
The farther he traveled, the more Withered he encountered.
Some were moving along rocky platforms, while others were coming out of the cracks, many of them did not even attack each other and simply continued moving toward the center of the land.
But in several areas, he also saw signs of heavy battles.
The bodies of mutated creatures were lying among the rocks, and parts of the ground had been damaged by powerful impacts.
Even so, there were no signs of the base’s forces.
Time was passing.
Despite his physical abilities and large mana reserves, he could feel the strain of flying continuously at maximum speed.
Such speed required a constant flow of energy through his wings.
But he had only one goal.
Reaching the base.
Finally, after nearly two hours of flying, the huge golden wall appeared on the horizon.
The same barrier they had passed through on the first day, which had now turned into an impenetrable wall.

Even now, in a land where another part of the ground was collapsing every moment, the sunlight created a magnificent view.
But Rindo could no longer see it as beautiful, that beautiful thing was actually a killing machine.
Lian was flying at his maximum speed.
Warm air passed beside his body, and the strong wind created by the movement of his wings pushed away some of the steam floating along his path.
At first, he planned to follow the approximate route they had taken over the past few days, but only a few minutes were enough for him to realize that doing so was useless.
The land was no longer the same land they had crossed that morning.
Cracks that had previously been only a few meters wide had now turned into huge valleys.
Parts of the golden forests had collapsed along with thick layers of soil and stone, and in some areas, giant white roots were hanging from the walls of the cliffs.
Molten rock was flowing in the depths.
Sometimes the steam became so thick that he could not see the ground below even from his current height.
He moved his wings and gained more altitude.
"The situation is much worse than I thought."
But what caught his attention the most was the way the ground was collapsing.
In some areas, huge sections of the plain had almost completely disappeared, while several kilometers away, rocky platforms still remained relatively intact.
Inside some of the cracks, parts of old structures could also be seen; thick walls, broken pillars, and paths that had previously been hidden underground.
He could stop to examine them, but now was not the time for that.
Lian increased his speed.
After some time, he flew over an area where a small spring had once been located.
He recognized the location for a moment, it was one of the paths he had crossed with Rindo and Amélie on the first day.
When Amélie had seen the plants around the spring, she had stopped for a few minutes and talked about their healing properties.
Now, neither the spring nor the plants remained, that entire area had turned into a huge crack.
He looked down for a moment and then flew over it without slowing down.
The farther he traveled, the more Withered he encountered.
Some were moving along rocky platforms, while others were coming out of the cracks, many of them did not even attack each other and simply continued moving toward the center of the land.
But in several areas, he also saw signs of heavy battles.
The bodies of mutated creatures were lying among the rocks, and parts of the ground had been damaged by powerful impacts.
Even so, there were no signs of the base’s forces.
Time was passing.
Despite his physical abilities and large mana reserves, he could feel the strain of flying continuously at maximum speed.
Such speed required a constant flow of energy through his wings.
But he had only one goal.
Reaching the base.
Finally, after nearly two hours of flying, the huge golden wall appeared on the horizon.
The same barrier they had passed through on the first day, which had now turned into an impenetrable wall.

chapters.title: Chapter 646: Nothing Remains
paragraphs: Based on the position of the wall and the remaining geographical signs, the central base should have been somewhere nearby.
But when he reached the area, he slowed down.
For a moment, he thought he had taken the wrong route.
Because he could not see anything familiar.
No watchtowers, no defensive walls, and no tents where Alaric used to hold command meetings.
He stopped in the air.
His gaze slowly moved across the area, beneath his feet, a sea of molten rock was flowing.
A huge part of the land had completely disappeared, and the remaining pieces of rock stood like separate islands among the red cracks.
Even the paths leading to the golden barrier had disappeared.
Only the wall itself was still standing, without a single crack or sign of damage.
Lian said nothing for several seconds.
It was here.
He remembered the approximate location of the base.
He could even imagine the path between the medical section, the central warehouses, and the western watchtower in his mind.
But now, molten rock was flowing through those same places.
He lowered his altitude, hundreds of Withered were scattered around the area.
Some were moving across the remaining rocky platforms, others were coming out of the cracks, and several were standing still near the golden wall.
He examined one of the creatures.
[Race: The Withered]
[Rank: Mutated]
[Level: 51]
His gaze moved toward another creature.
[Level: 53]
And then a third creature.
[Level: 50]
Lian frowned slightly.
"So even creatures of this level have appeared here."
Of course, he did not know whether they had been here before the destruction of the base or had come out of the new cracks afterward.
But if the Association’s forces had been forced to fight a large number of these creatures while the ground was collapsing, their situation must have been much worse than he had imagined.
Lian moved toward one of the remaining rocky platforms.
He examined the area from above.
Nothing.
He changed direction and moved toward the place where the base’s medical section had previously been located.
But that area had also completely collapsed, he gained altitude several times and searched for signs of humans from different angles.
He found neither Alaric, nor Noah, nor Myra, nor Mathieu.
There were not even any clear remains of equipment or buildings that could help him identify the possible evacuation route of the forces.
On one of the platforms near the wall, a huge Withered noticed his presence.
The creature jumped from the rock with a rough roar and threw its thick arm toward the young Vorhelm.
He simply turned his head, and his right fist moved.
BAAANG!
The strike hit the creature’s face, the huge body of the Withered spun through the air and crashed into one of the nearby rocks with great force.
He did not even wait for it to fall completely and continued searching.
He had not come here to hunt, and killing hundreds of Withered could not bring back what had been lost.
After some time, he moved toward a section of the area that Alaric had previously chosen for an emergency retreat.
If the forces had evacuated before the complete collapse of the base, there was a chance they had used that route.
But when he arrived, he noticed that most of the path had disappeared, only a few large pieces of rock remained among the molten rock.
Lian landed on one of them and examined his surroundings for a moment, then looked down at the palm of his own hand.
Does that mean they’re all dead?
This question remained in his mind for several seconds.
He remembered Alaric’s face.
A commander who had remained calm even when the Second Judgment began.
Then Noah; the young Frenchman who had talked about the base staff and their families only last night.
Myra, with her direct and calculating personality, and Mathieu, who despite his playful behavior, seemed like a kind young man.
He slowly closed his fingers, he still did not know them very well, but that did not make their disappearance unimportant.
Especially when he knew that if he had been at the base just a few hours earlier, he might have been able to save some of the forces.
Of course, perhaps the result would not have been any different, he could not hold every part of the ground together at the same time, and he still had not found any way to stop the sun’s judgment.
Lian let out a short breath.
Nothing has been confirmed yet.
Alaric could have ordered a retreat before the base was destroyed, the forces might have moved to other areas in small groups.
But that was only one possibility.
There was another possibility as well, that none of them had found a chance to escape.
He lifted off the ground again.
He spent some more time searching around the golden barrier and the remaining platforms, but found no reliable signs of survivors.
Finally, he stopped in the air near the wall, the golden light on its surface was impressive even from this distance.
The same wall that had blocked their way out, the same structure that had previously repaired the damage from his attacks in just a few moments.
And now, while everything around it had been destroyed, it still remained unchanged.
"Damn it." Lian looked at it for several seconds and then said in a low voice.
This time, there was no trace of humor in his tone.
By the time he returned to the rock where he had left Rindo, several hours had passed since his departure.
Two was the first to notice his presence.
The huge wolf raised its head and turned its ears toward the sky, and Rindo, who had been sitting on one of the rocks, immediately stood up.
"Lian!"
Vorhelm landed with a controlled movement, his black wings slowly folded behind his back and disappeared.
"Well? How was the base?"
He looked at his friend for a moment and then answered.
"The base doesn’t exist anymore."
"Do you mean they moved it?" Rindo paused.
"No."
Lian pointed toward the distant golden wall.
"That entire area is covered in molten rock, there’s no command center left, no warehouses, not even the ground beneath them."
His friend remained still for several seconds, and his gaze slowly lowered.
"All of it?"
"Almost the entire area, only a few rocky platforms near the golden barrier are left."
"What about Alaric? Noah? The others?" Rindo placed his hand on the shaft of his spear.
"I couldn’t find any of them."
Silence followed.
Two lowered its head slightly and moved its gaze between the two young men.
Rindo pressed his lips together for a moment.
"Not even a single sign?"
"No, I searched the area for several hours, but I couldn’t find anything that could tell me what happened to them.
He slowly breathed out, then sat down on the same rock as before.
Several moments passed before he spoke again.
"Alaric had been preparing for the worst since the first day, even before the Second Judgment, he had already chosen the retreat routes."
Lian nodded.
"I know."
"So maybe he managed to get the forces out."
"Maybe."
"But you’re not sure either." Rindo raised his gaze.
This time, Lian did not answer immediately and finally said calmly.
"No. I’m not sure."
His friend lowered his gaze toward the ground, for several seconds, only the faint sound of stones moving down the distant cliffs could be heard.
"We lost Amélie right in front of our eyes, and now we don’t even know what happened to the others."
He rubbed his forehead with his hand.
"Until two days ago, I thought the biggest danger of this mission was not finding the treasure I wanted."
He let out a short, bitter laugh.
"Now I don’t even know if the ground beneath our feet will still exist tomorrow."
Lian stood beside him and looked at the broken plain for a moment, even in the Special Area, Rindo had always placed the lives of his companions above everything else.
All the ideas and plans he had suggested back then were meant to make sure that the majority, or even everyone if possible, would survive.
And yet, now they had not been able to save anyone.
"That’s why we need to find a way out as soon as possible."
"Do you think it’s still possible?"
"As long as we’re alive, we have to assume it’s possible."
"And what if we can’t find one?"
"Then we’ll have to make a new way out." The corner of Lian’s mouth rose slightly.
Rindo looked at him for several seconds and then slowly nodded.
"Sometimes I really don’t understand where all that confidence of yours comes from."
"Maybe because I’m not dead yet."
"That’s a very strong reason."
The young Vorhelm gave a short smile, but their conversation did not continue any further, because at that exact moment, both of them looked toward the sky.
The Hollow Sun was still hanging above the land.
The huge golden rings were rotating around its black pupil, and its warm light fell on the broken rocks.
From a distance, it still looked like the same sun they had seen on the first day.
Beautiful.
Calm.
Almost holy.
But for Rindo, that light now reminded him of a being that had destroyed Amélie without the slightest hesitation, and most likely, their other companions as well.
And for Lian, every golden ring reminded him of the energy threads that even his current power had been unable to break.
Two also raised its head.
Its ears moved backward, and a low growl came from its throat.
Neither of them spoke for a while.
"We don’t have any reason to return to the base anymore."
"Then where are we going?" Rindo also lowered his head.
"There." Lian stretched his hand toward the center of the land.

chapters.title: Chapter 647: The Kneeling Mourner
paragraphs: In the distance, parts of the plain were still relatively intact; the same areas that hundreds of Withered were moving toward.
"Do you think the answer is there?"
"I don’t know, but most of the clues we’ve found point in that direction, the energy flows, the paths of the Withered, the underground structures..."
Lian paused for a moment.
"Even if there’s a key to get out, we’re more likely to find it in an area where the structures are still intact."
Rindo thought for several seconds and then picked up his spear.
"Alright, we’re going to the center."
The young Vorhelm looked at Two.
"Then we’d better get moving."
The huge wolf immediately lowered its head.
Rindo looked at its large body for a moment.
"Are we going to ride it?"
"Yeah, it’s much faster than walking."
Then he climbed onto the wolf’s back without arguing.
Lian sat in front of him and then placed his hand on the wolf’s neck.
"Let’s go."
Two placed its paws firmly on the ground, the muscles in its legs tightened, and a moment later, it jumped into the air from the rock with a huge leap.
Rindo tightened his grip on the shaft of his spear without thinking.
Two landed on the rocky platform on the other side of the cliff and immediately prepared for the next jump.
Rindo glanced at the crack behind them and then sighed.
This is going to be a long journey.
The fourth day began under the usual light of the Hollow Sun.
Of course, in a land where day and night were no longer very different from each other, only the passage of time and changes in their bodies reminded them how many hours had passed.
After a short rest in one of the relatively stable areas, Lian and Rindo had started moving again.
Two moved through the rocks at an impressive speed, every time it reached a deep crack, it pressed its paws firmly against the stone and jumped to the other side without noticeably slowing down.
Sometimes the distance between two platforms was so large that Rindo could only see the cliff and the molten rock beneath them for a moment.
But Two landed accurately every time.
"I didn’t think a wolf could be this fast."
The huge wolf moved its ears slightly, but it did not slow down.
Lian placed his hand on its neck.
"It isn’t even using its full speed yet."
Rindo looked at him for a moment and then decided not to say anything, in his opinion, their current speed was more than enough.
During the journey, the young Vorhelm had more time to examine their surroundings.
He no longer had to focus all his attention on moving himself and could use [True Sequence] to observe the mana flows around them.
The closer they got to the center, the more underground structures appeared.
In some areas, huge white roots stretched through several layers of stone and carried energy toward the depths.
In other areas, ancient walls had been revealed from beneath the soil; walls that did not look much like ordinary buildings.
But what was even stranger was the condition of the ground.
Parts of the paths near the center were still relatively intact, while many of the areas behind them had been almost completely destroyed.
Why are these areas still intact?
Lian could not be sure, perhaps the underground layers in this area were stronger, or maybe the buried structures played a role in keeping the ground stable.
But he needed more information to examine it properly.
After some time, the number of Withered increased, the creatures were moving toward a common area from different paths.
Some could barely walk on their changed legs, while others dragged their bodies across the stones using their long arms.
Even so, most of them showed no special reaction even when they saw the huge wolf and simply continued along their paths.
Two also continued moving without paying attention to them.
Until near noon, they reached a very old road.
The road passed between two huge cliffs, and unlike the surrounding paths, a large part of it was still intact.

The road was nearly forty meters wide, and broken stone pillars could be seen along its edges, ancient patterns had been carved into some of the pillars, and white roots were growing out of their cracks.
Rindo looked toward the end of the road.
"This path leads straight toward the center."
"And it seems to be the only intact path around here." Lian nodded.
But Two slowed down, and it did not take long before it stopped completely.
The huge wolf raised its head and turned its ears toward the end of the road, a low growl came from its throat.
Two kept its gaze fixed on a point in the middle of the road.
Lian followed the same direction, and a few moments later, he also heard the sound.
The sound of crying.
At first, it was so faint that it was difficult to hear over the sound of flowing molten rock.
But the more he listened, the clearer it became, it was a broken and rough voice.
"I... I... didn’t want to..."
"What is that?" Rindo had also noticed the sound.
Lian climbed down from Two’s back.
"Let’s find out."
He took a few steps toward the road, but when he looked past the broken pillars, he stopped.
In the middle of the road, a huge creature was kneeling.
Even while kneeling, the creature was nearly three meters tall, its body was covered in gray, cracked skin, and old wounds could be seen along its arms and chest.
Its two very long hands rested on the ground, thick chains hung from its wrists, but their other ends were not connected to anything.
Dirty white hair covered its face, and black liquid was dripping from beneath it onto the stone, the creature had lowered its head.
Its huge shoulders shook slightly with every cry.
"Please..."
Its voice spread across the road.
"Not... again..."
Lian remained still for a moment and then examined the creature’s information.
[Race: The Withered]
[Rank: Mutated]
[Level: 50]
Rindo, who was standing beside him, slowly breathed out.
"Level 50."
Lian nodded, but his attention was not only on the creature’s level, several other Withered were also present around the road.
Some were moving along narrow stone edges, while others were taking more difficult paths to avoid getting close to the kneeling creature.
Even those who seemed to be pulled toward the center against their will changed their paths when they reached this area.
So even the others are avoiding it.
Rindo had noticed this too.
"Do you think it attacks them, and that’s why they’re afraid of it and stay away?"
"Maybe, but we haven’t even seen it stand up yet."
"Even so, it’s crying...? A monster? Crying?"
The young Vorhelm also found this interesting, seeing a monster crying was not something you could see every day.
The Mourner continued crying.
Lian looked at the surrounding paths for a moment, he could fly over the road with Rindo.
But unlike most of the Withered, this creature was neither moving toward the center nor paying attention to its surroundings.
It was also sitting on a path that seemed to have some of the underground structures passing beneath it.
He wanted to know why.
Then he signaled Two to stay near one of the higher platforms.
The huge wolf took a few steps back and stood on a section of stone that was wide enough.
Rindo took the Ten Star Spear from his back.
"Are you sure we should get close to it?"
Lian looked at the creature.
"I want to examine something, if it shows a dangerous reaction, we’ll retreat."
Rindo nodded, and they both entered the road, the sound of their footsteps spread across the old stones.
The Mourner showed no reaction.
The young Vorhelm took a few more steps forward, the distance between them was now about thirty meters.
"Hey." He said in a relatively loud voice. "Can you speak?"
The creature did not raise its head, but the sound of its crying became weaker for a moment.
"I... didn’t want to..."
"What didn’t you want to do?" Lian raised an eyebrow slightly.
He received no answer, and only the sound of black liquid dripping onto the stone could be heard.
Rindo looked down at the ground, one of the drops fell near the creature’s foot, but instead of spreading across the stone surface, it remained still for a moment.
Then...the drop slowly separated from the ground and began moving upward.
"Lian." He immediately held his spear in front of his body.
Vorhelm had also noticed the change, but before he could examine the energy structure, the Mourner’s crying suddenly became louder.
"Not... again...!"
A heavy pressure formed in the air, and a moment later, the first wave was released.
BOOOOM!
Rindo redirected the pressure with a quick movement of his spear, but the remaining force pushed him several steps backward.
Lian only moved half a step, his gaze remained fixed on the Mourner.
"So you finally reacted."
But just as Rindo regained his balance, a second wave spread from the creature’s body.
This time, the pressure was wider and more destructive.
( Scene Visualization )

Rindo looked at him for a moment and then decided not to say anything, in his opinion, their current speed was more than enough.
During the journey, the young Vorhelm had more time to examine their surroundings.
He no longer had to focus all his attention on moving himself and could use [True Sequence] to observe the mana flows around them.
The closer they got to the center, the more underground structures appeared.
In some areas, huge white roots stretched through several layers of stone and carried energy toward the depths.
In other areas, ancient walls had been revealed from beneath the soil; walls that did not look much like ordinary buildings.
But what was even stranger was the condition of the ground.
Parts of the paths near the center were still relatively intact, while many of the areas behind them had been almost completely destroyed.
Why are these areas still intact?
Lian could not be sure, perhaps the underground layers in this area were stronger, or maybe the buried structures played a role in keeping the ground stable.
But he needed more information to examine it properly.
After some time, the number of Withered increased, the creatures were moving toward a common area from different paths.
Some could barely walk on their changed legs, while others dragged their bodies across the stones using their long arms.
Even so, most of them showed no special reaction even when they saw the huge wolf and simply continued along their paths.
Two also continued moving without paying attention to them.
Until near noon, they reached a very old road.
The road passed between two huge cliffs, and unlike the surrounding paths, a large part of it was still intact.

The road was nearly forty meters wide, and broken stone pillars could be seen along its edges, ancient patterns had been carved into some of the pillars, and white roots were growing out of their cracks.
Rindo looked toward the end of the road.
"This path leads straight toward the center."
"And it seems to be the only intact path around here." Lian nodded.
But Two slowed down, and it did not take long before it stopped completely.
The huge wolf raised its head and turned its ears toward the end of the road, a low growl came from its throat.
Two kept its gaze fixed on a point in the middle of the road.
Lian followed the same direction, and a few moments later, he also heard the sound.
The sound of crying.
At first, it was so faint that it was difficult to hear over the sound of flowing molten rock.
But the more he listened, the clearer it became, it was a broken and rough voice.
I... didn’t want to..."
"What is that?" Rindo had also noticed the sound.
Lian climbed down from Two’s back.
"Let’s find out."
He took a few steps toward the road, but when he looked past the broken pillars, he stopped.
In the middle of the road, a huge creature was kneeling.
Even while kneeling, the creature was nearly three meters tall, its body was covered in gray, cracked skin, and old wounds could be seen along its arms and chest.
Its two very long hands rested on the ground, thick chains hung from its wrists, but their other ends were not connected to anything.
Dirty white hair covered its face, and black liquid was dripping from beneath it onto the stone, the creature had lowered its head.
Its huge shoulders shook slightly with every cry.
"Please..."
Its voice spread across the road.
"Not... again..."
Lian remained still for a moment and then examined the creature’s information.
[Race: The Withered]
[Rank: Mutated]
[Level: 50]
Rindo, who was standing beside him, slowly breathed out.
"Level 50."
Lian nodded, but his attention was not only on the creature’s level, several other Withered were also present around the road.
Some were moving along narrow stone edges, while others were taking more difficult paths to avoid getting close to the kneeling creature.
Even those who seemed to be pulled toward the center against their will changed their paths when they reached this area.
So even the others are avoiding it.
Rindo had noticed this too.
"Do you think it attacks them, and that’s why they’re afraid of it and stay away?"
"Maybe, but we haven’t even seen it stand up yet."
"Even so, it’s crying...?
A monster?
Crying?"
The young Vorhelm also found this interesting, seeing a monster crying was not something you could see every day.
The Mourner continued crying.
Lian looked at the surrounding paths for a moment, he could fly over the road with Rindo.
But unlike most of the Withered, this creature was neither moving toward the center nor paying attention to its surroundings.
It was also sitting on a path that seemed to have some of the underground structures passing beneath it.
He wanted to know why.
Then he signaled Two to stay near one of the higher platforms.
The huge wolf took a few steps back and stood on a section of stone that was wide enough.
Rindo took the Ten Star Spear from his back.
"Are you sure we should get close to it?"
Lian looked at the creature.
"I want to examine something, if it shows a dangerous reaction, we’ll retreat."
Rindo nodded, and they both entered the road, the sound of their footsteps spread across the old stones.
The Mourner showed no reaction.
The young Vorhelm took a few more steps forward, the distance between them was now about thirty meters.
"Hey." He said in a relatively loud voice.
"Can you speak?"
The creature did not raise its head, but the sound of its crying became weaker for a moment.
"I... didn’t want to..."
"What didn’t you want to do?" Lian raised an eyebrow slightly.
He received no answer, and only the sound of black liquid dripping onto the stone could be heard.
Rindo looked down at the ground, one of the drops fell near the creature’s foot, but instead of spreading across the stone surface, it remained still for a moment.
Then...the drop slowly separated from the ground and began moving upward.
"Lian." He immediately held his spear in front of his body.
Vorhelm had also noticed the change, but before he could examine the energy structure, the Mourner’s crying suddenly became louder.
"Not... again...!"
A heavy pressure formed in the air, and a moment later, the first wave was released.
BOOOOM!
Rindo redirected the pressure with a quick movement of his spear, but the remaining force pushed him several steps backward.
Lian only moved half a step, his gaze remained fixed on the Mourner.
"So you finally reacted."
But just as Rindo regained his balance, a second wave spread from the creature’s body.
This time, the pressure was wider and more destructive.
( Scene Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 648: When the Mourner Stops Crying
paragraphs: Rindo spun his spear with great force and moved out of the wave’s direct path at the last moment.
The wave passed beside him with a terrible sound and struck the stone pillar beside the road directly.
CRAAAAACK!

The impact instantly destroyed the upper part of the pillar, deep cracks spread quickly across the entire stone surface, and before the pillar could collapse, a wave of destructive force passed through it.
Pieces of stone were thrown in every direction, and thick dust filled the air.
A few moments later, a large part of the pillar collapsed with a heavy sound, and broken stones scattered across the ground.
He let out a short breath.
"Two waves?"
Lian did not answer, he had noticed that the energy around the Mourner had not completely calmed down yet.
He lowered his hand.
[Frost Dominion]
A thin layer of ice spread along the road, the surface of the stones turned white, and tiny ice crystals formed in the air.
Then, after a short pause, circular cracks appeared on the ice.
"Rindo, it’s not over yet!" He immediately said.
The third wave was released.
This time, the pressure was heavier than the previous two waves, Rindo, who had just changed his position, did not have enough time to retreat.
But instead of trying to stop the wave directly, he raised his spear with a spiral movement.
The fourth mark on the weapon’s body lit up.
[Ten Forms of the Heavenly Spear]
[Fourth Form: Azure Dragon Rends the Nine Heavens]
Azure mana wrapped around the spear.
The energy flow took shape with Rindo’s spinning movement and created an image similar to a long, thin dragon in the air for a moment.
Using that same movement, he lifted himself off the ground, the pressure wave passed beneath his feet and destroyed the layer of ice on the road.
But he did not stop moving.
His body spun in the air, and the spear’s tip moved downward toward the Mourner, and in a straight line, it struck the creature’s shoulder.
CLAAANG!
Mana sparks scattered from the point of contact, the blade only created a shallow cut in the Mourner’s thick skin.
Rindo immediately jumped backward.
At that same moment, the chains hanging from the creature’s arms dragged across the stone, but the Mourner still had not raised its head.
It was only crying.
"Its defense is really high." Rindo took several steps back after landing.
Lian nodded.
He was examining the mana flows around the creature with [True Sequence].
The first skill seemed to activate along with the sound of crying, but the pressure waves were released after different delays.
This difference in timing made it difficult to tell when the attack had ended.
’Interesting, it’s like it deliberately wants the enemy to move too early.’ He thought for a moment, if his guess was correct, this should be another Withered that had come up from underground.
But why is it crying? And what does it mean by those words, "I didn’t want to"?
The Mourner stopped crying for a moment and then placed both of its huge fists on the ground.
"Move away from where you’re standing." Lian noticed the change in energy.
Rindo immediately moved.
But right where his foot had been a few moments earlier, a dark mark appeared, the stones slowly shook, and then a thick pillar shot out of the ground.
He managed to move away from its main path, but when he landed on another stone, a second mark lit up beneath his feet.
What?
He quickly spun his spear, and the fifth mark lit up.
[Fifth Form: Heavenly River Returns to Its Source]
Azure and silver energy flows formed around the spear’s shaft, with circular movements, Rindo redirected part of the pressure from the rising pillar toward the sides.
The spear shook in his hands, and the remaining pressure passed into his arms, forcing him to take several steps back.
But he managed to survive without taking a direct hit.
He let out a heavy breath.
"This thing can even target where we step?"
Lian glanced at the dark marks on the road.

"It seems to track where we were a few seconds ago, you’d better avoid taking the same paths." He had planned for them to retreat, but it seemed the monster was no longer going to allow them to do that.
Rindo nodded.
But at that exact moment, another mark lit up behind him, he had not yet had time to change his position when a stone pillar weighing several tons began rising upward.
Lian raised his right hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
A huge claw made of solid ice formed in the air and struck the pillar with a quick movement.
CRACK!
The rising stone split into several pieces.
Rindo moved between the pieces and landed on a relatively intact part of the road.
The young Vorhelm looked at the Mourner.
’It has used two skills, one to control distance and another to punish our movements.’
If it were facing an ordinary fighter, such a combination would probably force them to spend all their time defending.
But Lian had no intention of allowing the creature to keep complete control of the battlefield.
He took a step and moved toward the creature, the thirty-meter distance between them disappeared in just a few moments.
The Mourner was still kneeling.
When he reached it, the creature raised its head slightly for the first time, part of its twisted face became visible through its dirty white hair.
Its mouth had a deep wound stretching from one side of its face to beneath its chin, and black liquid had gathered inside its dark eye sockets.
"Please..."
But Lian did not wait for the rest of the sentence, and his right fist struck the creature’s shoulder.
BAAANG!
The Mourner’s huge body bent backward, the stone beneath its knees cracked, and part of the thick skin on its shoulder split open.
The creature made a muffled sound from its throat, but it still remained on the ground.
The young Vorhelm looked at it for a moment.
’It has good physical strength.’ At least, that was what he had learned from the first strike he had landed on the monster.
Of course, not enough to truly resist his current physical strength, but something about the Mourner’s structure had caught his attention.
A large amount of the creature’s energy moved along its arms, and near its chest, several paths connected to each other.
Lian decided to apply more pressure, he clenched his right fist, and mana became compressed along his arm.
[Disaster Suppression Fist]
This time, unlike his normal strikes, the skill’s power was focused into a dense structure around his fist.
The Withered tried to raise its hand, but it was too late, Lian’s fist struck the upper part of its chest.
BOOOOOOM!
The creature’s defensive layers shattered under the strike, and a wave of pressure passed through the back of its shoulder and broke the surrounding stones.
The Mourner’s huge body slid several meters across the road, and the chains hanging from its arms left deep marks on the stone.
Rindo, who was watching the scene from a short distance away, lowered his spear for a moment.
That strike should be enough...
But at that exact moment, something else happened.
The sound of crying stopped.
The Mourner lowered its head and did not move for several seconds...then it placed its right hand on the ground and slowly began to stand up.
Vorhelm did not retreat either and simply watched the creature’s movements.
When the huge Withered finally stood on its feet, its full height was nearly five meters.
Thick chains hung from its wrists, and old wounds could be seen across its chest and stomach.
But what had changed even more than its appearance was the way it stood, its shoulders were no longer shaking, its head was no longer lowered, and no sound of crying came from its throat anymore.
Its feet were placed a certain distance apart on the stone, it held its right arm in front of its chest and lowered its left hand slightly.
The stance of a fighter.
"Oh?" Lian gave a faint smile for a moment.
At that same moment, the monster moved, and its right fist came toward him in a short, straight path.
Vorhelm moved out of the strike’s path with a slight turn.
But just as he was about to counterattack, two gray images of the creature’s previous movement remained in the air.
One of them repeated the punch at the same angle, while the other attacked from the opposite side after a shorter delay.
Lian immediately changed his position.
The first fist passed beside his waist, and the second almost struck the side of his body, forcing him to move several meters away.
But the Mourner was no longer in its previous position.
The five-meter-tall creature had stepped forward heavily and sent its left fist toward Lian’s body from a lower angle.
Lian raised his arm, and the two fists collided.
BOOM!
The pressure from the collision spread through the stones beneath their feet.
But the young Vorhelm only took half a step back, while the Mourner’s arm shook violently.
Even so, the creature immediately changed its movement, and instead of continuing to push directly, it pulled back its right hand and attacked from another angle.
Two new gray images also remained from its previous movement.
[Funeral of the Nameless]
Lian examined their structure with [True Sequence], these images were not simply illusions.
Each one was made of compressed mana flows that repeated the creature’s previous movement after a short delay.
But none of them had as much power as the real body.
"So it can repeat its previous strikes." He whispered, this was almost like cheating.
At that moment, Rindo approached from the right.
He intended to stop one of the images with his spear, but just before the impact, the Mourner changed the direction of its real punch.
This time, its target was Rindo, and the young spearman immediately moved backward, the huge fist passed in front of his face.
But one of the gray images repeated the same strike after a short delay.
He could not retreat in the same direction, because a dark mark had appeared where he had previously stepped, the same kind of mark that had appeared during the monster’s first attack.
So he changed his movement path, and the seventh mark on his spear lit up.
[Seventh Form: Phoenix Returns Beneath the Moon]
The spear’s shaft disappeared behind Rindo’s body for a moment.
A trail of silver mana remained along his retreat path; a trail that showed the wrong direction for the weapon’s next movement.
The Mourner sent its fist in that direction.
But Rindo turned at the last moment, and the real blade returned from a lower angle and struck the creature’s forearm.
CLAAANG!
The strike only created a shallow wound, but it caused the fist’s path to change for a moment.
He used the opportunity to move out of the attack’s range.
Lian, who had watched the situation, gave a short smile.
But the Mourner had also noticed something.
The spearman was much weaker than the human who fought with his fists, and unlike the fist fighter, he could not withstand its heavy strikes with his own physical strength.
The creature focused on Rindo for a moment and then moved toward him with a long step.
Lian noticed this change.
The monster had decided to eliminate the easier target first.

chapters.title: Chapter 649: The Tenth Form
paragraphs: Lian immediately moved, but this time, he did not intend to end the battle with just one punch, apart from the fact that it was impossible, he also wanted to examine the structure of the Mourner’s third skill.
Because something about the way the creature’s movements worked together was connected to its previous two skills, first, mana flowed from its right arm into its chest.
Then it spread along several other paths and formed the gray images, the same area that Lian’s previous punch had damaged.
He looked at Rindo.
"Keep an eye on its right arm, I think that’s where its skills are connected."
"Understood." He nodded and then held his spear in front of his body.
The sixth mark lit up.
[Sixth Form: Seven Stars Seal the Dragon Veins]
Seven small points of light formed along the path of the blade, and Rindo began a series of attacks with very precise movements.
The first strike hit the outer part of its forearm.
The second hit its shoulder.
The third targeted the mana flow around its chest, and the fourth and fifth strikes reached the same area from different angles.
But despite the damage, the Mourner did not retreat, it sent its left fist toward Rindo.
The young spearman was forced to change his attacks for a moment.
He moved out of the fist’s path with a quick turn and delivered the remaining two strikes to the damaged part of the creature’s right arm.
CRACK!
For a fraction of a second, the mana flow in that area became unstable.
One of the gray images that was forming broke apart before it could be completed.
But the skill’s effect did not last long, and the creature quickly regained its power.
Rindo immediately moved away, his breathing had become heavy.
Just that much?
He could clearly feel the difference in level between himself and the creature.
Even with his special martial art and high-quality spear, disrupting the mana flow of a Level 50 enemy required a lot of effort.
But that short disruption was enough for Lian to move, and the light around his hand turned dark.
[Corrupt Sun]
A weak flow of Eclipse Energy moved along the corrupted light and reached the damaged part of the Mourner’s arm.
The mana layer began to weaken, and then he quickly moved in front of the creature and struck the same point with another punch.
BAAANG!
The arm’s defensive structure broke apart for a moment.
The monster took several steps back.
But just as Rindo was about to use the opportunity, the creature raised both hands.
The mana flow around it changed, this time, the energy did not remain in one place, it gathered along its arms and chest and then moved toward the back of its body.
Lian raised his head and saw nine huge, partly transparent rings forming one after another behind the creature.
This one was different.
The Mourner clenched its right fist, and a heavy pressure settled over the road.
Countless stones rose from the ground and shook in the air, but contrary to expectations, the creature did not attack Lian directly.
Instead, it struck the ground with its fist, causing the first ring to collapse.
BOOOOM!
A wave of pressure moved along the road, cracks appeared across the stone surface, and part of the eastern edge collapsed.
Rindo jumped quickly out of the wave’s path, but before he could land, the second ring began to collapse.
He spun his spear.
[Fourth Form: Azure Dragon Rends the Nine Heavens]
Azure mana moved around his body in a spiral, and using the force of the rotation, he changed his direction in the air and passed through the second wave.
But just as he was about to land on an intact part of the road, a dark mark lit up beneath his feet.
[Graves of Return]
Damn it!
A stone pillar rose from the ground, but before it could hit him...CRACK!
A huge ice claw passed beside Rindo and split the pillar into several pieces, allowing the young spearman to land among the broken stones.
"Watch your steps." Lian lowered his hand from a short distance away.
"Understood!"
The Mourner released the third layer of pressure, this time, the wave moved directly toward the central part of the road.
Lian jumped high out of its main path, but Rindo was forced to use his spear to redirect part of the force.
The Fifth Form.
[Heavenly River Returns to Its Source]
Silver energy flows formed rings around the spear, and the pressure was redirected away from its original path, but the remaining force passed into his shoulder and arm.
He slid several meters backward across the stone, and his palm was burning with intense pain, part of the skin on his fingers had been damaged.
Even so, he did not release his spear.

A large part of the road in front of him collapsed, and stones fell into the cliff, while hot steam rose from beneath the road.

"Can you still continue?"

"Yeah, but I can’t fight like this for very long."
"You won’t need to."

He looked at Rindo.
"I need an opening."
"How long?" Rindo let out a short breath.
"Just a moment."
His friend looked at him for several seconds, and then the corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"I think I can do that."
Lian smiled.
"Good."

The eighth mark on its body lit up.
[Eighth Form: Ten Thousand Spears Traverse the Star River]
Blue and silver mana spread along the blade.
He took a step forward and then began a series of attacks.
The first strike hit the creature’s left arm, the second hit its shoulder, and the third hit the damaged part of its chest.
But this time, Rindo did not pause between his strikes, every movement prepared the path for the next attack.
Dozens of silver and azure trails formed along the spear; trails that looked like a river of stars under the sunlight.
The Mourner was forced to take several steps back, not because Rindo’s strikes had enough power to destroy it.
But because the continuous attacks disrupted the formation of its gray images.
Every time one of the images appeared, the spear’s next strike hit its mana structure.
But Rindo was also under pressure, he was consuming a lot of mana, and the muscles in his arms had become extremely tight, he could not maintain this form for very long.
Lian watched the situation and then lowered his palm.
A thick pillar of ice formed a few meters away from the Mourner.
Rindo immediately understood what he meant, and with the final movement of the Eighth Form, he sent his spear toward the monster’s shoulder.
Then he took a step back and jumped onto the ice pillar, his body rose several meters into the air, and the ninth mark lit up.
[Ninth Form: Falling Star Pierces the Nine Palaces]
Mana gathered along the spear, and Rindo turned his body in the air and aimed the weapon’s tip toward the same damaged point on the Mourner’s chest.
For a moment, the glowing trail of his movement looked like a blue star falling from the sky.
Then...CLAAANG!
The spear struck the Mourner’s chest, this time, the blade passed through the outer layer and pierced several centimeters into the previous wound.
But the creature immediately reacted, raising its right hand and trying to grab Rindo.
Before the huge arm could reach his friend, Lian moved, and his fist struck the monster’s wrist.
BAAANG!
The creature’s hand was thrown aside, and Rindo used the opportunity to pull out his spear, but when he landed, he fell onto one knee.
His breathing had become heavy, his right palm was covered in blood, and his fingers could barely hold the weapon’s shaft.
He had consumed a large amount of his mana, even so, he had achieved his goal, the defensive structure near the Mourner’s chest had been badly damaged.
Lian looked at the same point.
Now.
But the Mourner had also noticed the danger and pulled back its right hand, the fifth ring behind it began to collapse.
A huge amount of pressure gathered around its body, this time, Rindo could no longer escape every attack with quick jumps and repeated forms.
If the next strike hit him directly, the difference in level between them would probably have very serious consequences.
The young Vorhelm took a step forward.
But at that exact moment, Rindo tightened his grip on his spear.
"Lian."
He looked at him.
Despite the pain in his hand, his friend slowly stood up from the ground.
"You said you needed a moment, right?"
Lian paused for a moment and then gave a faint smile.
"Yeah."
"Then I’ll give you that moment." Rindo nodded.
He held the Ten Star Spear in front of his body, it was time to perform the Tenth Form.

chapters.title: Chapter 650: The Funeral Of Nameless
paragraphs: All the marks on the spear’s shaft lit up one after another.
The first mark.
The second.
The third.
All the way to the tenth.
Mana began flowing along the weapon, but unlike the previous forms, this time, the energy did not spread around the spear.
All the lights slowly moved toward the tip of the blade, and then the marks on the shaft went dark one after another.
Only a small point of blue light remained at the tip of the spear.
Rindo held his breath for a moment.
Just one strike this time.
He knew very well that he could not defeat the Mourner’s huge power with his own strength.
But there was no need to do that, Lian had already identified the weak mana path, the Sixth Form of the spear had damaged it, and the Ninth Form had pierced the defensive layer around it.
Now he only needed to disrupt the connection for a moment.
The monster moved its right fist downward, and the fifth ring was about to release its pressure.
But Rindo moved first.
[Tenth Form: One Spear Silences the Nine Heavens]
No huge dragon appeared in the sky, no river of light formed across the battlefield, there was only one spear and one strike.
The blade moved in a straight line toward the damaged point.
The Mourner tried to change the position of its arm, but at the last moment, Rindo turned his wrist and adjusted the angle of impact.
The spear’s tip reached the mana connection point.
CRACK!
For a fraction of a second, the energy flow inside the Mourner’s chest became unstable.
The fifth ring broke apart before releasing all its pressure, and then the sixth ring also began to collapse without fully activating.
But this time, instead of moving normally through the skill’s path, the force spread through the creature’s damaged structure.
He breathed out heavily, his fingers became numb for a moment, but he had succeeded.
"Lian!"
There was no need to say anything else.
Vorhelm had already moved, his black wings opened with great force, and his body rushed toward the Mourner in a straight line.
The creature was still trying to stabilize its disrupted mana flow, but this time, it did not have enough time.
Lian appeared directly in front of it, clenched his right fist, and compressed mana into an extremely dense structure.
[Disaster Suppression Fist]
His fist struck the damaged part of the Mourner’s chest.
BOOOOOOM!
The layers of natural armor around the point of impact shattered.
The mana structure that Rindo had disrupted for a moment collapsed from within under the huge pressure of the strike.
The monster tried to raise its hands, but the force of the punch had already reached deep inside its body before another defense could form.

The sound of breaking bones filled the battlefield, and the creature’s five-meter-tall body was lifted off the ground, thrown several meters backward, and crashed into the stone wall at the end of the road.
BAAANG!
Part of the wall collapsed, and broken stones fell onto the Mourner’s body, while thick dust spread across the battlefield.
For several seconds, no one moved.
Rindo leaned on his spear, he was breathing with great difficulty.
Lian lowered his hand, his gaze remained fixed on the pile of stones, through the dust, part of the Mourner’s body could be seen.
The creature still made a weak movement for a moment, it raised its head slightly, and its mouth opened, as if it wanted to say something, but no sound came out.
Then its huge hand fell to the ground and stopped moving.
The nine remaining mana rings in the air went dark one after another.
A deep silence settled over the road, and the sound of crying could no longer be heard.
"Is it over?"
Lian looked at the body for several seconds and then nodded.
"Yeah.
Rindo laughed for a moment, but his laughter immediately turned into heavy breathing.
"Good... because I don’t think I can perform even one more form right now."
The young Vorhelm approached and looked at his friend’s injured hand.
"You’d better rest for now."
"I think I actually agree with you this time." Rindo lowered his spear, he had a considerable amount of healing herbs in his storage space.
He took some out to use them.
At that moment, the sound of heavy paws moving could be heard.
Two had come down from the higher platform and was slowly approaching.
The huge wolf first examined the Mourner’s body, then looked at Rindo and lowered its head slightly.
"It seems even he thinks you should rest." Lian smiled and then turned his full attention toward the monster’s body.
[Greater Glutton Activated]
[Available Skills: 3]
He immediately turned his attention to the options.
[Graves of Return]
[Nine-Heaven Collapse Fist]
[Funeral of the Nameless]
His gaze stopped on the third option.
Oh?
Lian looked at the Mourner’s body for a moment.
What kind of creature were you really before becoming a Withered?
Of course, he could not find a definite answer from the skill alone, but now he had another opportunity.
Without hesitation, he selected the third option.
[Skill Acquired: Funeral of the Nameless]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Upon performing an attack, the user can manifest two gray phantoms that replicate the original attack]
[Each phantom follows the trajectory of the original strike and delivers a delayed, independent impact.]
[Phantom attacks possess physical force and can damage enemies, defensive barriers, and surrounding structures.]
[Effects]
[Phantom Replication: Creates up to two phantoms of a single attack.]
[Delayed Impact: Each phantom can strike after the original attack at a separately controlled interval]
[Attack Synchronization: Phantoms replicate the direction, movement, and offensive properties of the original attack.]
[Limitations]
[Phantom attacks consume additional Mana. Their power depends on the Mana invested]
[Phantoms cannot perform independent movements or execute attacks different from the original strike.]
A faint smile appeared on his face, he had obtained the monster’s annoying skill, it was not a bad result.
He also glanced at his level progress bar, there was not much left before his next level.
"Are you alright?" He then looked at his friend.
Rindo nodded, after consuming the elixirs and healing herbs, he had returned to his best condition.
Then they both looked at the Mourner’s body.
The creature that had once been kneeling and crying in the middle of the road now lay motionless among the broken stones.
They did not know what kind of past was hidden behind those tears.
But something about the creature’s fist skill and fighting style showed that before becoming a Withered, it probably had not been an ordinary fighter.
"The farther we go, the stranger these creatures become."
Before moving again, they divided the loot, Rindo took forty percent of the body, and Lian kept the rest for himself, he could later use it as food for the Devourer Egg.
He finally turned his gaze away from the body.
There was still a long way to go before reaching the center, and they did not have much time left before the next Judgment.
The ancient road became narrower beyond the battlefield.
Both sides still ended at deep cliffs, but the central part was covered with large, evenly placed stones that seemed much older than the surrounding forests and plants.
The huge wolf approached and lowered its body slightly so they could both climb onto its back.
But this calm did not last long.
Because when Two passed between several broken pillars, another sight appeared in front of them.
A huge arch made of black stone stood at the end of the road.
It was nearly twenty meters tall, and parts of its surface were covered with white roots.
On the upper part of the arch, an image of a ring with an empty center had been carved.
It looked very similar to the Hollow Sun.
"That same symbol again." Lian said quietly when he saw it.
Rindo nodded.
"This is another ancient structure."
Two slowed down, several Withered were moving around the arch, but unlike the previous groups, these creatures stopped when they reached a certain area.
Some fell to their knees for several seconds, others hid their heads between their hands, and several stood up again and continued moving despite clearly trying to resist.
"Rindo, look at them." Lian climbed down from the wolf’s back.
His friend pointed toward one of the creatures, a thin Withered with very long arms was standing directly in front of the arch.
The creature was trying to move in the opposite direction, but every time it took a few steps, it stopped, then its body turned back toward the arch against its will.
Rindo narrowed his eyes.
"Just like that creature we saw yesterday."
"Yeah, but this time, almost all of them react at the same point."
Lian activated [True Sequence].
The mana flows around the arch became visible.
Several thin paths moved along the stones and connected to the depths of the ground through the white roots.
But what caught his attention was the short connection between this structure and the mana of the Withered.
Every time a creature passed through the area around the arch, part of the mana flow around its body became unstable for a moment, and then the energy flow returned to normal.
"So there’s some kind of connection point here too." All of this was confusing him greatly, and he could not understand its purpose.
At that moment, one of the Withered near the arch noticed their presence.
The creature had a thin body and a badly twisted face, but unlike most of its kind, it could still speak to some extent.
"Help..."
Rindo kept his spear ready, and Lian took a few steps forward.
"What’s wrong?"
The Withered looked at him for a moment, then raised its shaking hand toward the arch.
"There..."
Its voice became weaker.
"They’re... waiting..."
"Who’s waiting?" The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes.
The creature opened its mouth, but before it could say anything, its body tightened violently, and its long fingers dug into the soil.
Its legs began moving against its will.
"I don’t want to... go back..."
Lian focused on the mana flow around the creature for a moment, the same familiar pulse could be seen, but this time, part of the flow was directly connected to the structure of the stone arch.
Interesting.
He could try again to disrupt the smaller energy path with [Corrupt Sun], but yesterday’s experience had shown that the effect only lasted a few seconds.
And he still did not know what would happen if he completely broke such a connection.
So he decided to observe for now.
The Withered slowly passed beside them, its head was lowered, and its hands were shaking, but its body continued carrying it toward the center.
"Do you think all of them were prisoners?" Rindo looked at the creature for a moment.
Lian shook his head.
"I’m still not sure, but the charges announced by the sun sound more like the rules of a prison."
He looked at the arch.
"And these structures are probably part of the same thing."
Rindo looked at the image of the hollow sun for several seconds.
There was no doubt that this place had once been a prison, and these Withered might have been its prisoners.
Prisoners who were waiting for their judgment.

Two slowed down, several Withered were moving around the arch, but unlike the previous groups, these creatures stopped when they reached a certain area.
Some fell to their knees for several seconds, others hid their heads between their hands, and several stood up again and continued moving despite clearly trying to resist.
"Rindo, look at them." Lian climbed down from the wolf’s back.
His friend pointed toward one of the creatures, a thin Withered with very long arms was standing directly in front of the arch.
The creature was trying to move in the opposite direction, but every time it took a few steps, it stopped, then its body turned back toward the arch against its will.
Rindo narrowed his eyes.
"Just like that creature we saw yesterday."
"Yeah, but this time, almost all of them react at the same point."
Lian activated [True Sequence].
The mana flows around the arch became visible.
Several thin paths moved along the stones and connected to the depths of the ground through the white roots.
But what caught his attention was the short connection between this structure and the mana of the Withered.
Every time a creature passed through the area around the arch, part of the mana flow around its body became unstable for a moment, and then the energy flow returned to normal.
"So there’s some kind of connection point here too." All of this was confusing him greatly, and he could not understand its purpose.
At that moment, one of the Withered near the arch noticed their presence.
The creature had a thin body and a badly twisted face, but unlike most of its kind, it could still speak to some extent.
"Help..."
Rindo kept his spear ready, and Lian took a few steps forward.
"What’s wrong?"
The Withered looked at him for a moment, then raised its shaking hand toward the arch.
"There..."
Its voice became weaker.
"They’re... waiting..."
"Who’s waiting?" The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes.
The creature opened its mouth, but before it could say anything, its body tightened violently, and its long fingers dug into the soil.
Its legs began moving against its will.
"I don’t want to... go back..."
Lian focused on the mana flow around the creature for a moment, the same familiar pulse could be seen, but this time, part of the flow was directly connected to the structure of the stone arch.
Interesting.
He could try again to disrupt the smaller energy path with [Corrupt Sun], but yesterday’s experience had shown that the effect only lasted a few seconds.
And he still did not know what would happen if he completely broke such a connection.
So he decided to observe for now.
The Withered slowly passed beside them, its head was lowered, and its hands were shaking, but its body continued carrying it toward the center.
"Do you think all of them were prisoners?" Rindo looked at the creature for a moment.
Lian shook his head.
"I’m still not sure, but the charges announced by the sun sound more like the rules of a prison."
He looked at the arch.
"And these structures are probably part of the same thing."
Rindo looked at the image of the hollow sun for several seconds.
There was no doubt that this place had once been a prison, and these Withered might have been its prisoners.
Prisoners who were waiting for their judgment.
